# Architecture

## Precision bitmap projection

`engine/bitmap-projection.ts` preserves the ordinary Canvas draw path and selects a double-precision reference path when projected coordinates exceed the subpixel precision range of float32 drawing. It samples native 64×64 source patches through a 64-entry LRU, interpolates recovered encoded-sRGB premultiplied bytes, then writes bounded output patches. Axis-aligned image edges preserve existing half-pixel ties; affine image support uses exact square/pixel intersection. Original image resolution and bytes remain asset-owned. Mutable native canvases receive one privately owned ImageBitmap snapshot, closed on success or failure. Numerical loops check source/cancellation and yield at shared task boundaries.

Raster/mask/texture, native wet and filtered projection callers share this boundary. Ordinary raster draws retain their original five-argument Canvas call and transform order. Raster and mask preparation pin source identity/lifetime; retained mask keys include bitmap identity and dimensions. Texture batches wait for capture/cache/error arrivals before flushing the existing worker conversion. Numerical captures run serially with a shared two-millisecond yield deadline, bounding active native tile retention to one reader per batch; clear/disposal/source changes reject before late worker conversion. Cache retirement remains separate from cancellation. A circle-chord expression selects the stable form near the center and near the endpoint, preventing one floating-point ulp from becoming visible missing coverage at huge radii.

The native reader cache is a per-operation working bound, not a whole-process memory measurement. Original decoded assets, returned patches, renderer caches and other concurrent jobs retain independent ownership/budgets. Public OO mutation/history, document37/project3/workspace2, isolated scripting/plugin permissions and separate REST sessions are unchanged.

## Native frequency working partitions

`engine/pixel-work-grid.ts` partitions independent raster work by aspect ratio. Linear Light/Burn retains the former 1024×1024 pixel budget, with at most 8192 pixels on a working edge. Pixel equations and worker snapshot/result validation stay unchanged; cancellation is checked before and after each awaited blend before publishing pixels.

Recognized native frequency sampling may combine rectangles only when request count falls and estimated total halo work does not increase. Both width-first and height-first candidates include projection/filter margins and prefer at most 1,000,000 sampled pixels, within the existing 4 MP/8192-edge allocation checks. Composition accounts for both nested projection margins. Literal unchanged raster-band eligibility and exact integer unit placement are unchanged; complex masters, affine/fractional placement and masks retain their existing eligibility/fallback behavior. The original 256/512/1024 grids remain available for large halos or unimproved partitions. Document/source geometry is independent of these working budgets.

## Canonical ordinary paint coverage

`engine/paint-coverage.ts` owns raw untextured brush/pencil/eraser/clone coverage and fill geometry. Complete contributing native primitives replay into canonical 256-pixel cells with a support halo and an eight-pixel gradient phase. Rebasing preserves source coordinates at large translations. Scratch allocation stays within 4 MP/8192 edges; larger projected primitives use `primitive-coverage.ts` pixel-area integration and `paint-premultiplied.ts` destination-byte composition, without shrinking authored geometry. Proven solid strips at unit flow can overwrite exact opaque RGB; all uncertain edges keep integration. Soft coverage bounds bypass integration only when every possible value produces identical stored bytes.

`ActiveStrokeRaster` retains at most a 16 MiB raw viewport, independently owns mutable accepted points and stages numerical extensions privately. Superseded/cancelled work cannot install a partial prefix. Native padding has its own bounded allocation; `PaintedMaskRaster` reserves both viewport and padding bytes in its shared 16 MiB LRU, recalculating reservations when an existing key grows. Numerical replay shares a two-millisecond task deadline across primitives and pixel blocks, including accelerated opaque stamps. Clip/whole-stroke opacity apply once after raw coverage.

This corrects crop-sensitive antialiasing, so some edge pixels differ from older replay. Authored samples, original assets, OO commands/history, schema 37/project 3/workspace 2 and isolated scripting/REST boundaries remain unchanged. Textured/wet coverage, broader backend/device fidelity and sustained/process-memory performance retain their separate acceptance requirements. Current verification is recorded in the implementation roadmap.

Inverse-scaled integral crop positions recover their exact lattice indices before native cell selection and numerical dither, without snapping authored geometry. Native vector masks share this index helper. Cache invalidation controls retention separately from explicit caller cancellation: a direct mask read must survive a viewport cache reset. Busy active-mask entries have exclusive producer leases; concurrent readers replay privately, and retired entries dispose their surfaces after the current lease ends.

## Native frequency workflow controls — schema 37, functionally verified

GroupLayerData.frequencyRadius is an optional finite shared radius. LayerGroup exposes its OO setter; Layer.frequencyGroup locates the nearest controller. Attached updates use ordinary strict layer.update validation/locks/history. The smart resolver derives frequency-filter sigma in a private render tree while descending groups, and resets inherited scope when entering a component master. Source DTOs, individual fallbacks and locked correction children are not mutated. Capture the effective scope when isolating, converting, rasterizing or copying artwork into another document plane; Photoshop plane/prefix planning does likewise. Legacy groups remain independent.

PreparedFrequencySeparation owns one full-native capture, a stable private base document and source leases. Native preview extracts only a bounded crop plus Gaussian support, computes low once and encodes high from that exact rounded low. Frames own independent canvases. Commit assembles/probes a fresh private document, so a rejected setting does not consume the base snapshot. Source identity, bitmap/blob/native dimensions, lifetime, revision, selection, cancellation and publication guards remain authoritative. No output asset or undo reaches the host before successful commit.

The dialog coalesces rapid changes through one active preview job and retains only the latest complete frame. Original comparison redraws retained pixels without recomputation; pointer/arrow panning changes native crop coordinates. Busy/cancel state remains separate from preview activity. The inspector exposes a shared radius for a selected band/retouch layer and hides ineffective individual radius fields. Existing script isolation, native export fidelity and working-buffer/source-resolution boundaries remain unchanged. The preceding schema-37 workflow baseline passed build, all 1,381 unit/API cases, 207 native browser cases and 84 normal-production workflows. Current tiling verification is recorded below. Native preview, scope capture, shared controls, retry/cancel, source ownership, workspace/recipe and interchange evidence is in [frequency workflow verification](benchmarks/frequency-workflow-2026-10-19.json). Portrait-quality, sustained/device/process-memory and full F05/F14 acceptance remain open.

### Exact native reconstruction and bounded render sharing

A strict structural recognizer can render the captured raster directly where the original low/high/precision arrangement still reconstructs it exactly. It checks native dimensions, source identity, effective radii, appearance, alpha mask and component structure. A conservative retouch-ink intersection keeps full decomposition in every affected native region. Modified filter/mask/geometry/stack states fall back to the ordinary compositor. Authored source bytes, bands and editable strokes remain intact; this is an exact RGB8 identity, not a lower-resolution preview. Radius working-budget errors remain observable.

Exact unit-scale frequency-band planes with safe integer placement may use 512-pixel native tiles so an outer tile plus overscan no longer creates a tiny second request. Affine/fractional placement and halos whose worst-case 512-pixel padded footprint exceeds the existing 4 MP/8192-edge budget retain 256-pixel tiles. Native composition/retouch canvas regions retain their original grid; the ordinary paint correction above does not by itself establish broader tiling equivalence. No source geometry, public model/API or persistent format changes. The main build, all 1,381 unit/API cases, 60 affected native cases and 84 normal-production workflows pass. Fourteen frozen-renderer PNG pairs and six full native 50 MP exports are independently pixel-exact. See [native tiling evidence](benchmarks/frequency-native-tiling-2026-10-19.json); wider F05/F06/F14 acceptance remains open.

Every Canvas render owns an 8 MiB frequency scratch cache shared with recursive native tiles and cleared on return/failure. Identical source/region/effective-sigma/prefix requests can reuse the rounded low and original input across sibling bands, including cache-free export. Raw source elision applies only to a single frequency filter; arbitrary prefixes and filter-mask mixing retain their own original-input semantics. Existing persistent viewport retention stays separate. Recursive smart sampling checks a shared eight-millisecond task budget; PNG assembly also yields between tiles when its budget expires and rechecks cancellation. These are scheduling checkpoints, not a promise that a browser draw/decode or garbage collection cannot take longer.

## Native frequency workflow — introduced in schema 36

`engine/frequency-separation.ts` owns private source leasing, full native PNG capture, cancellation/revision/selection/source-identity checks and atomic publication. `dom/frequency-separation.ts` assembles existing OO groups, smart masters, filters and paint layers through commands; original source bytes and IDs remain unchanged. It preserves original appearance on the outer group, ordinary raster erasures in a post-placement coverage mask, and original raster tone in the document phase. Active wet sources are reconstructed with their complete expanded native ink before separation. The source is hidden only at successful commit.

Native low/high/correction planes share the captured master. AssemblyScript kernels perform premultiplied Gaussian sampling, detail/correction encoding and Linear Light/Linear Burn source-over blending in the existing worker. The three-plane encoded-RGB8 rule is exact before affine projection. `NativeCompositionFilter` makes the native composition and image-frame edge clamp precede resampling; `DocumentToneFilter` preserves raster tone's post-placement/pre-mask stage. Native filter masks remain native; document-phase masks project native feathered coverage through the full affine map. Reachable-master dependency signatures and the bounded filter cache allow sibling bands to share their rounded Gaussian; cache-free reference/export remains authoritative.

Schema 36 adds these strict filter kinds, `raster-erasures` masks and two appended blend modes (indices 16/17). Earlier blend indices retain their values. Canvas uses actual WASM for the new blend equations; supported WebGPU blends use WGSL. Smart-filter content retains its existing whole-scene Canvas fallback. Photoshop keys lLit/lbrn follow the [Adobe format specification](https://www.adobe.com/devnet-apps/photoshop/fileformatashtml/). SVG/Photoshop preparation must preserve pixels through the established baking/report boundaries. No new network, provider, isolated host service or headless renderer is introduced. Full workflow and performance acceptance remain in progress.

## Parametric red-eye correction

Schema 35 adds a cross-channel `red-eye` adjustment with strict threshold/strength fields and immutable `RedEyeAdjustment` DOM value. Attached changes use existing validation, transactions and history; embedded-master validation applies the same schema-age rule. UI creation captures the active document-space pupil selection into a layer-local editable mask after insertion, within the same transaction. The independent controls use existing paired Slider/number inputs, preview/cancel/commit and lock behavior.

For nontransparent straight encoded RGB8, positive `R-max(G,B) >= threshold` enables a strength-weighted move of R toward `(G+B)/2`, rounded once; G/B/alpha remain unchanged. Native rendering delegates bounded 1024-pixel tiles to actual WASM in the pixel worker. The GPU processing pass canonicalizes straight RGB8, packs `ceil(threshold)` to preserve integer classification through float32 uniforms, and retains normal mask/opacity/blend handling. Unsupported documents retain the existing reference fallback. Source dimensions/bytes are independent of tile budgets. SVG/native Photoshop adjustment-prefix preparation uses the generic raster-bake path and its warnings. This is manual pupil correction; portrait-quality and full F05/F14 gates remain open. Functional verification passed the full 1,363-case unit/API suite, 38 focused browser regressions, seven final feature cases and 120 actual-WGSL software-adapter comparisons (maximum premultiplied RGB error one byte; alpha exact). The final feature run exports a full 50 MP PNG and preserves source bytes/project pixels. Project v3/workspace v2, isolated privileges and REST session separation are unchanged.

Private result records carry same-session native raw epochs. Ordinary snapshot()/finish() results remain complete and independently owned. The internal snapshotSince handoff captures hints before queueing and omits only unchanged, previously projected cells; immutable descriptors identify their already owned output. The trusted adapter shares one current prefix's prepared Blob/bitmap leases into independently owned full views, rebuilding changed cells and validating the complete candidate before replacing those leases. Failure releases private deltas/views/cache without closing earlier caller/render-owned prefixes. Final finish still flushes all original/result records; final authoring can reuse its last prepared pixels without decoding them again.

Finish hands storage ownership to its result, which is decoded/validated/disposed before publication. Source/revision/asset validation and one synchronous OO transaction remain authoritative. Prepared output memory scales with affected stroke area and shares actual bitmaps with frames; the numerical32 MiB working-cache budget remains separate from source/output/process memory. A first ready prefix can prepare immediately; later prefixes reuse the boundary requested by the previous preparation and add no wait after it has elapsed. A freshly created, unused native private store can be claimed once by the retained session's bounded working cache. Own every incoming typed array before awaiting I/O. Keep intermediate originals, destinations and spatial reservoirs resident within the existing 32 MiB default; evict dirty cells through an atomic native batch, and update cache metadata only after success. Obsolete unpublished epochs can be discarded without a backing write. Custom, previously used, already claimed or method-modified stores retain write-through behavior; a zero-byte cache remains the reference path.

Independent prefix snapshots still own native stores and locks. Each original/result pair is copied in one optional atomic batch, with sequential custom-store fallback. Before finish transfers its original store, flush every referenced original/result in groups bounded by 64 keys and 4 MiB, with source/cancellation/store guards around I/O. Failed eviction, quota, closed/version-changed storage or stale sources publish no host command/assets. Disposal deliberately discards unpublished state; ordinary clear rejects dirty data. These are working-memory policies, not source-resolution limits or durable unsaved gestures.

Field age is checked outside immutable drawing proofs in ordinary/embedded/filter masks. Shared asset discovery/remapping includes both native image pairs and nested original brush textures. `wetDocumentOperations` and commandHasWetPaint jointly cover every command location that introduces prepared output, so the REST asynchronous gate cannot miss new masks; scripts validate the complete candidate before publishing. `wet-state.ts` owns shared result/types and the bounded tile cache. `wet-session.ts` owns captured settings, serialized append/snapshot/finish/dispose, original native tiles, current canvas epochs, independent per-symmetry reservoirs and cached whole-stroke projections. `wet-stroke.ts` retains the existing one-shot signature by creating and finishing the same session. Returned prefixes survive later appends, source closure and parent disposal; each owner must dispose its result. Unchanged raw epochs reuse cached selection/opacity projection; changed epochs invalidate that tile's projection. `core/wet-operation.ts` defines distinct prepared replacements rather than colored brush dabs. Output is premasked in native pixels; coverage removes destination and output adds once. ## Native spatial wet-paint replay — internal authoring dependency in verification

`engine/wet-stroke.ts` prepares a complete recorded brush/pencil path independently of the viewport. Shared stamp spacing, pressure/tilt/tip geometry and original-first symmetry order feed native dabs; each symmetry copy retains a separate spatial Float32 pigment field. The previous tip basis multiplied by the inverse current basis transports that field through translation, rotation, reflection, shear and changing pressure. `wet-spatial.ts` gathers native bilinear neighbors by source tile, preserving a fixed per-pixel summation order across backing layouts. It never allocates a transformed source bounding rectangle. Absent neighbors outside the preceding native support are transparent; missing tiles within that support reject as incomplete state.

Every dab reads the same previous canvas/reservoir epoch and stages all native tile results before advancing. Overlapping symmetry copies read preceding copies' completed dabs in the shared iterator order. Initial load uses the current native canvas under each copy. Fixed 256-pixel native coverage cells, with a two-pixel gutter, reuse actual Canvas footprint/texture sampling independently of the backing policy. Flow/pressure opacity applies during deposit/pickup; captured selection and whole-stroke opacity mix the completed original/result once. Unchanged pixels receive zero final blend coverage, preserving even hidden RGB outside the operation. Original/result tile pairs and binary changed-pixel support are prepared replacement data, not yet an authored operation or a live dependency on underlying layers.

`wet-store.ts` owns a unique private IndexedDB job database. A bounded LRU retains working tiles; evictions preserve their backing records. Completed results own their original/result bytes until explicit asynchronous disposal. Cancellation, callback/processor/source/storage failures dispose the private job and publish no document command or assets. Web Locks protect active jobs across tabs/workers; the next preparation can delete unlocked abandoned job databases after their context terminates. Only the reserved UUID job namespace is eligible. Browsers without Web Locks or database enumeration retain explicit disposal but cannot automatically identify abandoned jobs; broader device/storage acceptance remains open. Cleanup failures surface, and preparation plus cleanup failures retain both causes.

Trusted `prepareDocumentWetStroke` captures the requested rendered composition/branch, native source identities and font readiness before asynchronous sampling. It validates their lifetime/identity throughout, including source replacement under an unchanged asset ID. Its result can outlive source closure after all bytes are prepared. Rendered-document preparation is read-only; the separate wet-authoring adapter samples neutral target content so its own masks/opacity are not baked twice. No new public DOM constructor, command, schema, script/plugin host service, REST endpoint, preset or UI tool is added by this internal dependency.

Backing cells default to 128 pixels per side (internal policies permit 1–256), with a 32 MiB resident cache by default. Requests still use the numerical core's bounded working allocations; original image/document/stroke geometry remains independent. Unsafe integer pixel centers and noninvertible working bases fail explicitly. Metadata, native source/result/backing data, processing scratch and worker/WASM copies remain workload dependent. One-shot preparation consumes the complete supplied path; retained internal sessions now support appended prefixes. These policies do not prove whole-process memory or interactive latency. Prepared authored commands/history/assets and publication have a sealed baseline; actual interactive tools/previews/cancel/presets and the remaining F06/T16/F14 gates stay open.

## Wet paint simulation — internal dependency, authoring workflow unfinished

`core/wet-paint.ts` defines strict internal load/mix settings; `engine/wet-paint.ts` validates bounded working tiles and invokes actual AssemblyScript/WASM kernels through the ordinary pixel worker. This is not yet an authored operation, public DOM constructor, tool, script/plugin service or REST endpoint. Document32/project3/workspace2 and portable preset v4 remain unchanged. Mixer/smudge completion still requires native spatial reservoir transport/replay, ordered layer replacement including transparency, shared commands/history/source references, UI gestures/previews, persistence and native/SVG/GPU capability handling.

Reservoirs store Float32 encoded-sRGB premultiplied normalized RGBA, preserving sub-byte pigment between dabs. Initialization interpolates captured source pigment and an RGBA8 loaded color by `load` (0…1, default0); hidden RGB in transparent inputs contributes no pigment. Source and loaded alpha participate in that interpolation. Load is finite initial pigment, not an automatic refill on every dab. The default loaded color is opaque black.

For each native destination pixel, `t = flow * coverage/255`. Deposit interpolates original premultiplied RGBA toward carried pigment by `t*(1-wetness)`. Pickup separately interpolates carried pigment toward the **pre-deposit** destination by `t*pickup`, avoiding feedback from partially processed output tiles. Flow defaults1, wetness0 and pickup0.5; each is finite0…1. Zero flow/coverage preserves both inputs exactly. Wetness1 preserves destination bytes while allowing pickup. Results have RGBA8 destination pixels and Float32 carried pigment; RGB is zero when an active deposit rounds output alpha to zero. Whole-stroke opacity and captured selection must mix the completed original/result once afterward, never scale each dab's pickup. This is encoded-channel paint mixing, not linear-light, spectral pigment or physical fluid simulation.

Working requests admit at most4,000,000 complete pixels; larger native regions must be tiled without resizing their source. Carrier extent must match destination RGBA components; finite normalized alpha and premultiplied RGB are checked on both sides of the worker. Inputs/settings are captured before worker readiness and exclusively private buffers transfer. Outputs own their bytes across memory growth and subsequent requests. The working budget is not an image/stroke-size cap or a whole-process memory bound. No latency/device/60fps acceptance is implied by numerical correctness.

## Image-backed brush textures — authoring integration in verification

`core/brush-texture.ts` and `engine/brush-texture.ts` define internal image-backed coverage preparation. `BrushTextureSampler` reads an existing `AssetStore` bitmap into a requested output tile or native source crop; original Blob bytes and decoded dimensions remain asset-owned. Working tiles use the existing 4,000,000-pixel/4096-dimension allocation policy, independently of source image geometry. Larger output requests must be split by the caller, never implemented by resizing/rejecting the original. Fractional source rectangles must remain representable and inside the original image. Smoothing is explicit, default true; false requests native nearest-neighbor sampling.

The ordinary pixel worker executes actual `brushTextureMask` WASM. Alpha mode uses source alpha; rectangular crop inversion uses `255-alpha`. Affine inversion subtracts projected alpha from the projected opaque source-image support, preventing antialiased image-frame halos. Luminance mode uses encoded RGB weights `(2126R+7152G+722B)/10000`, with black as ink by default; inverted luminance uses white as ink. Both luminance modes multiply by source alpha, so transparent input remains transparent. Coverage rounds half up to an 8-bit alpha and returns white RGB. Canvas canonicalizes fully transparent pixels to transparent black. This is encoded-channel coverage, not linear-light or ICC-managed luminance. Conversion happens after native image sampling.

The sampler retains at most 32 MiB of private working surfaces by default, using the existing byte/entry-bounded Canvas cache. Keys include bitmap identity, channel/inversion, exact source crop, output grid and smoothing. Returned canvases are caller-owned copies, never cache-owned buffers; the caller must release them. Explicit clear/disposal invalidates pending publication, and cancellation/source ownership/lifetime checks reject stale results. Retiring viewport-cache retention does not cancel independently owned reads; retired conversions cannot repopulate a newer cache epoch. Worker inputs/settings are copied before readiness and returned type/extent are validated. Cache-copy allocation failure releases its private surface and preserves successfully prepared caller output. The sampler borrows the pixel processor and does not dispose it or the source assets.

`prepareAffine` additionally projects the original bitmap directly into a bounded working tile through a complete validated source-to-output affine map. The existing transform schema rejects singular/nonfinite matrices; mapped source bounds must remain finite. No source-sized intermediate is allocated. An inverted-alpha projection carries matching opaque image support through the same affine map; inverse coverage is clamped support minus sampled alpha. Callers still apply the intended footprint. Native conversion still happens after projection/sampling.

`TexturedStrokeRaster` is the asynchronous raw-ink replay adapter for authored textures, in verification. Texture coverage stretches over the existing normalized ellipse or pencil rectangle, modulating its native hardness coverage. Roundness, tilt, pressure and full symmetry copies use the existing shared stamp grid. A texture's orientation matters even on a round tip, so `paintStampGeometry` has an internal optional `preserveTipAngle` flag; the default retains existing isotropic geometry for ordinary untextured callers. Small texture footprints retain complete native sampling canvases. Larger footprints use document-anchored 256×128 output cores with a two-pixel projection halo; complete small footprints use at most 260×260 pixels. Footprint mattes reuse canonical ordinary coverage at the same output phase. Disjoint integer core clips apply flow through the native whole-image compositor, preserving repeated low-flow byte rounding. The caller must apply captured selection and whole-stroke opacity once afterward. No point/sample is replaced or dropped.

Append-only replay retains at most a 16 MiB raw prefix, with a separate private staging surface during asynchronous updates. Results reach the caller target and replace the retained prefix only after source/lifetime/cancellation checks. Cancelled partial work cannot advance the prefix. Larger output surfaces replay ephemerally without rejecting their geometry. Source identity/settings/view changes invalidate the prefix; concurrent requests serialize and clear/dispose invalidates pending requests. Returned source tiles are released after drawing, and the adapter borrows rather than closes its processor/assets. These working budgets do not describe whole-process peak memory or prove interactive frame rate.

Authored `BrushTexture` values and schema-32 brush DTOs now connect the adapters to ordinary paint, masks/filter masks, raster erasures and tonal coverage. Existing shared commands/history/asset validation remain authoritative. Native rendering shares one bounded sampler per renderer; borrowed prefix rasters never dispose that sampler. Texture paint selects complete Canvas fallback. SVG streams source-resolution coverage PNGs before emitting per-dab masks. Central asset visitors retain/remap texture references in projects/workspaces, recipes and cross-document copies; raster/SVG source capture pins these dependencies across asynchronous export. This integration is in verification. Active-tool source controls, gesture ownership and bounded texture cursors are now connected and in verification; source-bearing portable brush presets are now connected and in verification. No new script/plugin privilege, REST rendering operation or completed F06 claim is introduced.

`core/text-style.ts` applies the complete native font/spacing/direction state for text measurement, Canvas glyph drawing and SVG baseline preparation. It resets absent tracking/word spacing/kerning/direction and rejects unsupported nondefault word spacing/kerning before drawing. It retains native whole-line shaping instead of splitting glyphs or words. TextLayer setters, `resetSpacing` and strict layer.update share ordinary locks/history; typography patches require text layers. Immutable content signatures already include new primitive typography fields, invalidating reference/GPU glyph caches. Resize gestures capture complete typography and measure the new font size without overriding it with the captured size. Approximate headless bounds do not claim font parity. Schema 25 validates optional wordSpacing/fontKerning and gates them outside any immutable drawing proof; legacy roots/history migrate without inserted defaults. See the TextLayer guide for defaults, limits, feature detection and exact export behavior.

For nonzero word spacing, SVG preparation measures complete native/SVG responses against zero spacing before considering private whitespace-only inline styling. A candidate must match advance and outer non-whitespace character-position/ink responses; scalar advance equality alone is insufficient. Root typography, literal line content and a single shaped text chunk remain intact. Native grapheme boundaries after ASCII normalization guard every optional span and boundary trim. The established boundary-offset fallback handles unsupported/signed cases; a trim that would split a grapheme is declined. Per-layer caches key repeated lines by spacing, batch/candidate and in-line position-read yields preserve cancellation/font pins without dropping edges, and finally releases the hidden closed-shadow host and measurement canvas. The encoder independently validates private span ranges and whitespace/grapheme ownership. This changes no authored model/schema, public command, undo, source asset, REST or isolated script/plugin contract. Combining-mark, font-state, fractional/affine and cross-viewer fidelity gates remain open.

## TIFF source and editing representation

`core/interchange/tiff/inspect.ts` reads exact Blob ranges and validates classic/BigTIFF directories/addresses; `decode.ts` streams the supported strips/tiles into PNG rows. A per-operation module worker owns parser/codec state. The client validates reports/results and terminates on abort/callback errors. `engine/tiff-import.ts` stages one page's AssetStore and revision-zero OO Document privately, with affine orientation; `EditorApplication.openTiff` guards session/revision/I/O generation and disposes failed staging before publication. Inspection and conversion warnings precede the UI import action.

The immutable source is the original TIFF Blob plus `{page, allowPrecisionLoss}`, while `ImageAsset.bitmap` contains decoded 8-bit editing pixels in raw source coordinates. Project/recipe asset manifests and workspace transport preserve these decode settings; cross-document copies compare them as part of source identity. Recovery captures and hashes settings alongside source bytes/metadata, so distinct pages cannot alias and corrupt settings invalidate a checkpoint. Existing non-TIFF checksum encoding remains unchanged. Document/project/workspace schemas stay 27/3/2; older checkpoints cannot restore choices they never recorded. Source-dependent decoded/output/browser memory remains a real constraint despite row-streamed decompression and no arbitrary import-size cap. The exact supported subset, errors, parser budgets and trusted-only API are in SCRIPTING_API.md.

## Raster PDF export boundary

`core/pdf.ts` owns PDF real/address/page validation and Blob-backed objects with an eight-byte cross-reference offset field. `engine/pdf.ts` captures the immutable document and shared visible raster/font dependencies before callbacks, reads PNG's canonical native grid, and streams bounded RGB/alpha row buffers into two native Deflate streams. One PDF image/soft mask and one placement matrix preserve source sampling across non-72 DPI; independently placed strips can introduce reader edge shifts. The writer retains compressed output and small object metadata, not a document-sized canvas/full RGBA image. Row width, resident decoded sources, output and PDF readers remain real memory constraints. Source/callback/font/cancellation failures abort private streams and release all native surfaces.

`pdfDpi` changes physical page geometry only; large pages use bounded MediaBox/UserUnit geometry. Unsupported physical extents appear in the preflight report, while actual export rejects invalid geometry. UI/host output remains a raster page, with editability, metadata, searchability and prepress losses disclosed. No document/project/workspace schema, isolated export privilege, REST rendering route or batch format is added. Generated sRGB/Display P3 ICC profiles now use 4,096-entry ICC-v2 transfer tables for the sRGB piecewise curve; Adobe RGB/linear behavior remains unchanged. Original embedded profiles and source bytes are not rewritten. See SCRIPTING_API.md for signatures, defaults, errors, memory/reader limits and the tested constructor example.

## Affine coordinates and masks

`core/affine.ts` exposes the immutable public `AffineTransform` value using double-precision coefficients `[a c e; b d f; 0 0 1]` and column vectors. `parent.multiply(child)` applies the child first. Positive rotation is clockwise in the downward-positive editor plane. Inverse operations reject singular matrices; extremely ill-conditioned transforms may be singular at working precision.

Layer DTOs store x/y translation separately from an optional invertible basis with zero e/f. `core/spatial.ts` composes `translation(x,y).multiply(basis)` and accumulates parent matrices. DOM `Layer.transform` reads and writes the full local-to-parent transform, splitting its translation into x/y through one validated update. Raster width/height remain placed geometry, not a request to resample original source bytes. Layer selection supports translation, alignment, distribution, rotation, scaling and flipping through shared commands, with selected descendants excluded when their ancestor is also selected.

Canvas and WebGPU composition, inverse hit testing, tool coordinate conversion, transformed layer bounds and mask rendering consume composed matrices. `engine/canvas.ts` rebases translation against the tile origin in double precision before scaling. Cache placement signatures include the matrix. Reparenting and cross-document transfer preserve world placement through coordinate conversion; source assets remain immutable. Perspective and general warp are not implemented by the affine matrix model.

`core/masks.ts` composes linked mask geometry with the complete layer matrix; unlinked masks remain in document space. `Layer.setMaskLinked` converts offsets and basis to retain world placement. A literal mask DTO replacement does not perform that conversion. Selection/path capture maps geometry between source and target planes, including Bézier handles. Feather remains a document-pixel coverage operation after geometry transformation, so scaling geometry does not scale the feather radius. Rotation/scaling of layer or mask planes is distinct from bitmap-mask import and other unfinished mask tools.

Read [PRODUCT_BRIEF.md](./PRODUCT_BRIEF.md) for intent and [API.md](./API.md) for both automation surfaces. The product is named Canoli Studio.

## Object identity and transactions

Constructors create detached objects. Adding to a document or owned group establishes ownership. A layer cannot belong to two documents, and groups cannot create cycles. Attached handles resolve their stable ID in the current revision, so retained handles reflect undo/redo. Access to a removed node throws until it exists again. Duplicates have independent node/effect IDs and share the original source asset. Constructor-driven duplicate commands include an ID mapping so replay in a script's host produces the same references.

`Document.transaction(label, callback)` is synchronous, atomic and one undo entry. Nested transactions and async callbacks are unsupported. Do not schedule asynchronous mutation from a transaction; prepare asynchronous results first. Failed transactions discard document changes; handles created during a failed transaction must be discarded. Active-layer selection (`selectedLayer`) is session state and does not create history. Pixel selection (`selection`) is undoable document content. History retains up to 60 metadata revisions, not copied pixel arrays.

The underscore-prefixed methods are internal adapters, not supported external API. DTOs are for serialization and transport, not direct mutation. Current document schema 16 adds pixel selections and raster erasure records; supported older documents migrate after validation. Unknown layer/effect kinds and fields unsupported by a reader fail rather than silently disappearing.

## Resolution and memory

**No fixed megapixel, image-byte-size, session-pixel-count, or 8192-pixel import cutoff.** User requirement: modern high-resolution images retain their original dimensions and source data. Document integer dimensions need only be positive and safely representable in JavaScript; this is a numeric representation constraint, not a product-resolution tier.

Working allocations are independent of document size:

- The browser decodes the original image with `createImageBitmap`; original compressed bytes are retained as immutable blobs for the v3 project container. Images are never silently resized on import. Layer placement may fit an image within an existing composition without modifying its source.
- The viewport renders only the visible document region. Zooming to 100% requests the corresponding source-resolution region. Screen buffers use a 4 MP / 4096-pixel-side allocation budget, not an import limit. Very dense/high-DPI viewports can use a reduced working preview.
- Each tone operation runs on tiles no larger than 1024 × 1024 in a worker. Tone and Blend If are point operations and require no halo. Drop shadows render padded regions that include blur/offset contributions across tile boundaries; verify seams against a full-region reference.
- Group opacity and blending apply once to an isolated group buffer for the current region. Intermediate canvases are released after compositing.
- PNG export renders full-resolution tiles and feeds rows into `CompressionStream('deflate')`. It never creates a document-sized output canvas. Scanline strips target about 4 MB; compressed PNG chunks remain in memory until download. Format dimension restrictions are export-format constraints, never image import limits.
- Thumbnails use small separate images, avoiding a second full-size decode per layer row.

This is **not** a claim of infinite-size support: browser decoding still materializes the source bitmap; original image assets remain resident for undo; the document manifest still materializes JSON; legacy `.luma` JSON/base64 imports still allocate large strings. Device memory, browser decoders, numeric representation, and output formats impose real constraints. Recoverable decoder/allocation failures must report the actual operation, not invent an MP cutoff. A browser process killed by its OS cannot be caught reliably.

Next scaling boundary: lazy/region-capable image decoding, disk-backed asset storage and caches, streaming manifest/asset I/O beyond the current blob container, cancellation/progress, and expanded GPU coverage where measured performance justifies it. Do not reintroduce document caps to compensate for whole-image buffer allocation. Test 50 MP end to end and dimensions beyond prior cutoffs in model/API tests.

At reduced preview scale, adjustments operate on the resampled working pixels; nonlinear clipping can differ from final full-resolution export. Source-size crops and export use full-resolution processing. The first kernel uses encoded sRGB 8-bit channels; linear-light processing, ICC fidelity, RAW, CMYK and HDR need explicit future design.

## Tools and extended document content

`ToolController` tracks gestures, settings, command previews and a separate transient paint preview. Brush/pencil input accumulates all delivered/coalesced pointer samples, while preview publication is limited to one animation frame. A new empty paint layer is placed with the existing commands once at gesture start; subsequent samples never clone or validate the whole document. Pointer release includes the final endpoint and creates one validated DOM transaction. Escape, focus loss or session replacement cancels the gesture, including in-flight clone capture; a generation counter and document revision prevent stale commits. New paint/vector layers are placed above the selection or inside a selected group with document coordinates preserved. Preview placement uses the same commands.

Paint operations are immutable metadata (points, pressure, clip, style, source-tile references). Each operation renders into the current region, then its opacity applies once. Pencil uses pixel-aligned stamps. Clone snapshots the visible composition in at-most-1024px tiles before committing; staged assets are removed on cancellation/failure. Committed assets remain available for undo, and project serialization includes assets referenced by both rasters and clone operations. Stroke IDs and path IDs regenerate on duplication; original source assets remain shared.

Paint replay reuses one scratch canvas within a `drawPaint` invocation for ordinary fill, brush, pencil and eraser strokes. Each reuse clears pixels and resets transform, alpha and compositing before drawing. Per-stroke opacity and clipping still apply separately on the unchanged render grid. Clone and live Clone-source paths keep separate replacement surfaces. The scratch is invocation-local, never shared across concurrent renders, and released in `finally`, including failure paths. Long replays check an approximately 2 ms time budget between strokes and every 32 stamps within cold strokes, yielding through a private MessageChannel task; both ports close before continuing. This creates opportunities for input and painting while retaining operation order and complete-frame presentation. Active incremental previews retain synchronous stamping. A shared stamp iterator preserves interpolation, pressure, spacing and viewport clipping across synchronous previews and cooperative cold replay. The budget is best-effort: a native canvas operation or a batch of 32 expensive stamps is not interrupted; scanning offscreen segments and geometry bounds also remains synchronous.

Vectors store anchors and absolute local Bézier handles, stroke/fill and closure. Attached paths resolve by ID. Marquee regions evaluate ordered Boolean operations into a 4×4 subpixel mask in the WASM worker, with consistent coordinates across tiles; strokes capture that selection in local coordinates. New optional selection/style/fill-opacity fields are additive in prototype schema 1, with defaults for old files. Older builds may reject paint/vector layer kinds rather than silently discard them.

The region compositor isolates content, builds a shadow with padding, adds the color overlay, applies fill opacity to content, applies WASM Blend If to the styled result against preceding siblings, then composites with layer opacity/blend mode. Group child Blend If sees that group's internal backdrop. Color overlay and shadow pixels are browser Canvas operations; per-pixel tonal gates execute in the WASM worker.

`npm run build:docs` converts repository Markdown into local HTML/CSS under `public/developer`. Both `dev` and `build` generate these pages. The canonical source remains `docs/`; source-file references are labeled as repository references in the generated pages.

## Interactive rendering caches

`ActiveStrokeRaster` retains one unmasked brush/pencil canvas and draws only newly appended segments with the same stamp grid as full replay. It composites a copy with the captured selection mask and stroke opacity once, then feeds the normal layer/group/effect compositor. This preserves pressure, soft edges, translucent overlaps and export parity. A changed stroke/settings, rewritten or shortened point prefix, transform, viewport or scale resets the surface. The active surface retains at most 16 MiB; larger effect halos use full replay without imposing a document-size limit.

`CanvasCache` retains up to 64 MiB (and 256 entries) of least-recently-used layer content and active selection-mask canvases. Keys include the document, asset store, complete layer content, absolute placement and render space. Frozen layer signatures are memoized by object identity. Content is cached before its own styles; backdrop-dependent Blend If always runs against the current composition. Ancestors containing a live stroke recompose their children. Reads/writes copy synchronously, so asynchronous jobs cannot retain references to evicted buffers. Session replacement/disposal clears retained pixels and prevents in-flight jobs from repopulating an obsolete cache.

`RenderOptions.paintPreview` is an internal trusted tool/render adapter, not a scripting or REST mutation API. Export and clone sampling pass `cache: false` to avoid replacing useful viewport entries with one-off tiles. The same option provides the full-replay reference in renderer regression tests. Completed strokes remain editable metadata; the cache is neither persisted nor part of history. Stroke commit can still replay a changed paint layer once, and complex shadows/Blend If still cost work per frame; there is no universal frame-rate guarantee.

Browser tests in `tests/rendering.e2e.ts` cover pixel parity, segment work, frame batching, final samples, cancellation, cache eviction, and tone invalidation. The existing high-resolution import/export and tiled-effect tests remain required.

## GPU viewport backend

`AdaptiveRenderer` preserves `CanvasRenderer.render()` for export, clone capture and reference pixels. Its `prepareViewport()` selects `WebGpuRenderer` when a hardware adapter is available in a secure context (HTTPS or localhost), and otherwise prepares a Canvas/WASM frame. Software adapters are rejected in normal operation; an internal constructor option permits them in shader tests. This does not require a backend server, cloud upload, paid service or document-model change.

GPU viewport behavior:

- Source images are drawn into **visible-region** buffers before upload, never into a GPU texture sized to the entire imported image. Unchanged raw raster, paint and vector content stays in an LRU texture cache. Tone changes reuse the original uploaded raster.
- WGSL implements incremental brush/pencil stamps using the shared stamp-spacing iterator, tone adjustments, captured Boolean selection masks, color overlay/fill opacity, isolated group compositing, all 18 blend modes, and source/underlying Blend If. Brush coordinates are rebased in JS double precision before entering GPU buffers. Stroke opacity and clipping apply once to the accumulated surface.
- Fill/clear, clone and vector primitives currently use reference rasterization on a cache miss and then retain their uploaded texture. Drop-shadow documents use the complete Canvas/WASM path; GPU blur is not implemented. Brushes with projected stamp diameters below two working pixels use the reference path so supersampling cannot erase subpixel marks. These are backend choices, not document/tool restrictions.
- RGBA8 textures use premultiplied alpha and encoded sRGB. GPU preview and committed GPU strokes match; Canvas/export comparisons allow small 8-bit rounding and edge-antialiasing differences. The tested stacked-effect fixture differs by at most four channel values; the tested soft-brush edges by at most eleven, with mean error below 0.1. Do not describe the two backends as bit-identical or claim universal tolerances from these fixtures.
- Cached textures retain at most 64 MiB and 64 entries, plus at most 16 MiB for an active stroke. Renderer-owned live textures have a 192 MiB working budget. These exclude browser/driver overhead, source decoding, Canvas fallback allocations, diagnostic readback buffers and the browser-owned swapchain. Device texture limits, allocation/validation failures and precision-sensitive masks trigger fallback rather than resizing/rejecting the document.
- `ViewportFrame.present()` writes directly to a WebGPU canvas after the UI checks its render generation. It does not read pixels back to the CPU. The host replaces the canvas when switching backend because context types cannot be changed in place. Device-loss notifications request a fresh fallback frame automatically. Session replacement clears caches and invalidates pending frames; every prepared frame must be disposed.

The Canvas factory defaults to drawing surfaces without `willReadFrequently`; tone readback tiles, Blend If buffers and PNG readback explicitly request CPU-friendly buffers. Drawing surfaces no longer read back a probe pixel on allocation. The reference renderer continues to run per-pixel CPU operations in the WASM worker.

The footer reports **GPU accelerated** or **Standard rendering** for the displayed frame. Trusted development code can inspect `editor.renderer.gpu.diagnostics` (state, cumulative uploads/stamps/cache hits/frames/readbacks and retained/allocated bytes). This is an internal diagnostic, not a scripting or REST API. `ViewportFrame.readPixels()` exists for explicit GPU test readback only; ordinary viewport rendering does not call it.

`tests/webgpu.e2e.ts` runs actual WGSL through Chromium's SwiftShader adapter and reads GPU output buffers to check pixels, texture reuse, large-document regions and device-loss recovery. The presentation shader is separately tested against a real GPU texture in the preferred canvas format. The current headless software-adapter environment cannot present a browser-owned WebGPU swapchain canvas reliably; hardware presentation and hardware performance must be checked on a real GPU. Shader tests are not proof of hardware speedup. The regular browser/production suites exercise the automatic Canvas fallback, gestures and exports.

Reference: [WebGPU specification](https://gpuweb.github.io/gpuweb/), [canvas readback contexts](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLCanvasElement/getContext#willreadfrequently).

## Parameter controls

`src/ui/controls.tsx` owns the shared slider/number pair. Both tool options and bounded inspector properties use it. Tool previews update session settings directly; document-property previews remain transient commands until the gesture commits through the DOM. The control tracks pending gestures separately from committed values, so release followed by blur does not duplicate history. Path-width previews use the same command preview path as layer/tone/style adjustments. See the design system for keyboard, numeric-validation and scale rules.

## Asynchronous work

Reference-renderer pixel buffers transfer to a dedicated worker and back; the main thread does not execute WASM pixel loops. The adaptive viewport uses GPU shaders when supported and the Canvas compositor otherwise. A serial preview drain starts at most one render per animation frame and takes the newest queued snapshot. It rejects stale revisions, viewports and cancelled/replaced gestures; an earlier prefix of the same live stroke may display while its next frame waits, avoiding starvation during expensive effects. Cursor updates are frame-paced too. Export uses the same region compositor at source scale. Replacing a session releases its assets; callers should finish asset-dependent work before replacing a session.

The constructor API is TypeScript, not compiled to WASM. AssemblyScript is a separate, constrained TypeScript-like language used only for the numeric kernel. It is replaceable behind the worker protocol. The GPU viewport backend and Canvas reference/export renderer share document snapshots without changing the public DOM or document schema.

## Scripting boundary

See [SCRIPTING_API.md](SCRIPTING_API.md) for the public scripting contract, reference and runnable examples.

A sandboxed opaque-origin iframe creates a dedicated worker containing the bundled DOM implementation. The script receives a document snapshot, selected ID and constructor bindings, never host object references, credentials or image bytes. CSP denies network and external code loading. The host validates returned commands, checks that the document/revision has not changed, validates referenced assets, and commits one atomic transaction. A thrown error, invalid result, cancellation, timeout or conflict commits nothing.

The runner retains the starting document by reference only when it belongs to the internal recursively immutable registry. The subsequent message send makes the isolated copy; mutable inputs still use `toJSON()` immediately. This avoids a redundant main-thread clone while retaining snapshot semantics across host edits and staged transaction rollback. Public `Document.toJSON()` remains a defensive copy. `Document.fromJSON()` asks `EditorStore` to migrate the schema. The store first makes one owned deep copy, validates that exact snapshot under its supplied version, validates any retained history, and only then upgrades the owned schema version and freezes it. This avoids a second full-document validation and prevents getter-backed input from changing between validation and ownership. Store construction without the migration option preserves the supplied schema version. Caller metadata stays mutable and independent. Worker/frame lifetimes, CSP, relay transport and host commit checks are unchanged.

This is an initial local scripting environment, not a reviewed public plugin security platform. Time is bounded to 5 seconds and result complexity is bounded; worker heap allocation is not strictly metered. Do not describe it as safe for arbitrary hostile code or enable server execution of user scripts. Constructor/command DTO validation alone is not a JavaScript sandbox.

## Plugin boundary

`src/plugins` validates version-1 packages and maintains an immutable registry backed by local browser storage. Installation stores inert data. `editor.runPlugin` resolves only an installed command, invokes the scripting runner, enforces document read/write permission at the host commit boundary, checks revision/assets, and applies one labeled transaction. Plugins inherit the script runtime's time, command and result limits; there is no privileged page-context execution. The React Plugins panel provides package/source review, explicit installation/replacement, run/stop/output, export and removal. See [PLUGINS.md](PLUGINS.md).

## REST boundary

The optional local service binds `127.0.0.1:8787` and checks loopback Host and allowed browser origins. It maintains in-memory document sessions separate from browser tabs. Routes cover document commands/history, asset upload/retrieval and asynchronous jobs with polling/cancellation. `ApiServerOptions.authToken` enables Bearer or X-API-Key authentication (health remains public); an explicitly supplied generation executor owns external provider authorization and billing. No production provider is bundled. These local facilities do not establish public deployment hardening, durable server storage, browser synchronization or server-side execution of arbitrary scripts. See [API.md](API.md) for route-level constraints.

The full proposed design is in [AI_FEATURE_SPECS.md](AI_FEATURE_SPECS.md), with dependencies and migration gates in [IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md](IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md). It introduces local metadata extraction and review, immutable generation candidates, asynchronous host jobs, versioned masks/provenance, and future permissioned scripting/REST job surfaces. Local extraction and authored layer metadata are implemented as described below; review states, generation jobs, richer masks/provenance and host job APIs remain planned. Preserve the current synchronous transaction and sandbox boundaries; prepare asynchronous outputs first, validate against the document revision, then atomically install assets and accepted document changes. Project schema/storage evolution, color management and format support require explicit migration and conformance work before product claims.

## Storage implementation progress

[STORAGE_FORMAT.md](STORAGE_FORMAT.md) documents the current v3 checksummed blob container, legacy v1/v2 readers and atomic IndexedDB recovery. `RecoveryController` coalesces committed snapshots; `RecoveryRepository` commits assets and checkpoint manifests together. Workspace snapshot v2 additionally retains tabs, bounded undo history and smart-object contents-editing links. Disk-backed decoding, broader crash/device testing and large-file memory guarantees remain open.

## Local asset analysis

`AssetStore.metadata` owns a queued `MetadataService`; its worker extracts file declarations through exifr and normalizes inert fields. Work is bounded by one concurrent worker and an eight-second deadline. Asset removal/session disposal cancels analysis. Completion is guarded by worker identity; disposal is terminal, message errors fail explicitly, and queue continuation after completion/failure uses a microtask to avoid recursive synchronous failures. Derived results are rebuilt from source blobs after opening a project; no document commands or undo entries are emitted. `AssetInfoPanel` displays origins and exports privacy-filtered sidecars. See [ASSET_METADATA.md](ASSET_METADATA.md) for current coverage, output bounds and remaining hardening work. `LayerMetadata` provides a live OOP handle to authored layer records through `layer.update`; these persist from schema v2 onward, share locks/history, and remain distinct from worker-derived declarations.

## Historical implementation notes

The sections below record successive implementation slices. Earlier schema/status statements describe their original stage and may be superseded by later notes and the current baseline above.

### Layer masks

`LayerMask` stores selection regions or compound closed Bézier geometry plus enabled/inversion/density settings in a mask coordinate plane. Linked masks inherit layer translation; unlinked masks use document coordinates, with optional mask x/y offsets. `maskFromSelection` captures document-space regions using accumulated layer/ancestor translation. The layer patch is a complete mask replacement, validated in core and exposed through scripting/REST. Schema v3 prevents old readers from silently ignoring masks. Masks leave source assets and geometric bounds unchanged.

Canvas/WASM applies coverage to uncached working content after paint previews and before layer styles; group masks apply to composed children. Export uses identical region coordinates, including existing shadow halos. WebGPU uses the shared selection shader and a separate density/inversion pass, after tone/strokes and before styles/blending. Reference content uploaded for vector/text/raster layers has its mask removed to avoid applying it twice. Existing GPU failure/precision fallback remains available. Vector masks rasterize compound paths through Canvas using even-odd or nonzero fill on a fixed 256-pixel coverage grid with a two-pixel halo. Viewport and export strips crop the same coverage tiles to avoid clip-size-dependent curve differences; the GPU caches coverage per layer and uses its existing inversion/density/compositing pass. Coverage is keyed by geometry, fill rule, render region and layer origin. The OOP path getter returns detached copies; capture from a vector layer converts between source/target coordinate spaces. Bitmap-mask import, rotation and scaling remain T06 work.

### Mask feather processing

`engine/masks.ts` generates raw selection/vector coverage with a complete finite-support halo for each at-most-512-pixel output tile. The `featherAlpha` WASM ABI performs three horizontal/vertical fractional box passes with sliding sums and float intermediates; only final alpha is rounded. The pixel worker owns execution and scratch memory. RGBA plus two float planes are bounded by the four-million-pixel working-tile guard before allocation; extreme preview zoom/radius combinations fail explicitly. The final coverage canvas is shared by reference/export rendering and GPU uploads. Canvas and GPU cache coverage independently of inversion/density. The GPU rounds density-adjusted coverage to byte alpha before applying it, matching the reference mask surface and limiting accumulated group differences. Source pixels are never blurred; normal styles and group composition happen afterward.

Mask origin resolution is shared by Canvas and WebGPU through `core/masks.maskOrigin`. Coverage cache signatures use the resolved origin, so parent motion invalidates linked coverage but can reuse stationary unlinked coverage. `Layer.setMaskLinked` converts offsets when changing planes to preserve world position; it emits an ordinary complete mask update with the existing locks/history. Document data is not mutated when an unlinked mask's layer moves. Reparenting and duplication retain the stored plane and offsets.

Direct mask translation uses the existing UI gesture preview boundary: capture the complete initial mask, preview an x/y replacement, and commit one validated `layer.update` on release. No renderer, document schema or REST/script contract changes are required. Keyboard nudges use `LayerMask.with` through the attached layer setter. UI target state is separate from document data; source position and mask linking are unchanged.

Painted masks add `kind: "paint"` with base coverage and validated ordered brush/pencil operations. Coverage replays through the existing stroke rasterizer, clips in the mask plane, and composites Hide with destination-out or Reveal with source-over before feather/inversion/density. Source tile references are disallowed. Canvas/export share this coverage function; WebGPU uploads and caches its result, then uses the existing mask pass. ToolController captures a mask/coordinate snapshot, publishes transient stroke previews at most once per animation frame and commits one full mask replacement via the public value API. Revision checks prevent stale commits. Painted-mask coverage now retains finished prefixes in the shared viewport cache and appends active points to a bounded tile LRU. Feather processing still runs over affected coverage tiles; preview data carries only the active stroke, target layer ID and hide/reveal mode.

### Painted-mask coverage retention

`PaintedMaskRaster` shares the existing 64 MiB CanvasCache for finished prefix/full raw coverage and keeps at most 16 MiB of active raw stamp surfaces (at most 64 entries). This is additional to the existing ordinary paint-stroke 16 MiB surface. Cache keys include mask identity, render space and resolved origin; signatures include base coverage and full ordered operations. A completed full mask can become the next stroke’s prefix. Active coverage checks settings and the entire point prefix before appending, and resets on edits/undo. Clip, opacity, hide/reveal, feather, inversion and density are applied to disposable copies, preventing cumulative clipping or opacity. Cache eviction/oversized surfaces use fresh rendering without changing document data. Export/reference `cache:false` bypasses retention. Clearing the renderer releases active mask surfaces, and epoch guards prevent stale asynchronous jobs from repopulating cleared caches.

A layer’s unmasked content signature omits only its own mask. Group signatures retain descendant masks because those affect the group’s rendered children. Canvas and GPU source textures can therefore survive edits to their own masks without hiding child-mask changes. `CanvasRenderer.maskDiagnostics` reports prefix hits/replays, appended point work and active pixel bytes for verification; these counters are application diagnostics, not a scripting API or hardware speed guarantee.

### Transient painted-mask previews

`PaintPreview.maskMode` distinguishes mask hide/reveal from ordinary artwork strokes. ToolController uses this trusted renderer-only value rather than rebuilding a document command per pointer frame. Canvas and GPU append the active operation only inside coverage rendering, preserving document snapshot identity, history and source content. The target group may reuse its unmasked child composition, but ancestors of a masked child must recompose. The UI may present an older prefix of the same stroke only when document, assets, region, scale, target layer, stroke ID and mask mode still match; cancellation/commit/revision changes invalidate pending previews. Stroke/total-point budgets are checked before and during capture; the final DOM assignment still receives full shared validation.

Selection/vector masks may retain the same ordered brush refinements as a uniform painted base. `maskGeometry` includes kind, base geometry and strokes in coverage signatures, preventing stale caches when either component changes. Raw coverage first rasterizes regions/paths, then composites strokes; prefix caching and transient previews share this ordering. GPU selection shaders are used directly only when no strokes/feather need reference coverage. Shape/path values remain independently editable through the OOP API; no source rasterization or schema migration is needed.

Mask-pen gestures capture the original immutable LayerMask, revision, resolved origin and a detached editable path snapshot. Hit testing uses a seven-screen-pixel tolerance in that plane. Frames publish complete mask command previews at most once per animation frame; release applies `mask.with({paths})` through the attached layer, retaining strokes and mask-wide settings. Cancellation discards previews and revision checks reject stale commits. Keyboard edits resolve the selected mask contour/anchor against the current document; target state is UI-only. Existing layer pen creation remains separate. No schema, REST or scripting signature change is required.

Bézier subdivision uses the pure `core/bezier.ts` De Casteljau helper. Public `VectorPath.splitSegment` commits through existing path validation/history; the mask pen splits detached path copies and replaces the attached mask once, retaining its settings and paint refinements.

Mask contour creation retains a draft across pointer releases, including the original document/revision, immutable mask, resolved origin and new anchors. Each pointer gesture clones the draft points; frame previews append one closed contour to the captured mask DTO. No intermediate anchor enters document history. Completion assigns `LayerMask.with({paths})` inside a single named transaction. Explicit cancellation clears the draft and previews; revision/selection checks reject stale commits, and the UI discards an idle draft when the document revision changes. Contour drafts are transient tool state and are not saved, recovered, exposed through scripting or sent to REST. Those surfaces continue to accept completed closed path geometry.

Mask curve hit testing uses `core/bezier.ts` with pointer-relative screen coordinates. An iterative De Casteljau search bounds candidate intervals by control-point boxes and evaluates actual cubic points. It prunes improvements below 0.01 screen pixels, stops at representable parameter/depth bounds, and shares a 65,536-node work budget across a mask. A work-budget error leaves the document unchanged and suggests zooming in or using Insert midpoint. This is a bounded numerical search, not a symbolic nearest-point solver or an image-resolution limit. Anchor/handle hits precede curve hits. Successful curve hits subdivide only the affected segment in a detached mask preview; release commits through the existing mask update. The insertion is fixed at the pointer-down location; moving the new anchor is a subsequent editing gesture. Cancellation cannot leave a selected transient anchor index referring to a different committed anchor.

`document.crop` delegates to `core/crop.ts`: validate an integer rectangle, rebase root positions and document-space selections/unlinked masks, then retain all local content and assets. It operates on the command executor’s detached document clone, so schema/coordinate overflow errors discard the entire operation. Existing schema-v3 geometry stores the result; no crop bitmap or new project version is needed. Document-level crop/resize can include locked content because they change the canvas basis rather than local artwork. `EditorStore` history records whether an entry contains a crop/resize (including transactions); a session-only `canvasRevision` increments on dispatch/undo/redo of those entries. `EditorApplication` observes that marker to reset transient tools even for same-dimension crops or scripted transactions. It is not serialized into project document data. The crop dialog captures a document/revision stamp and rejects stale application.

`CropController` owns a document/revision-bound transient rectangle and pointer gesture, independent of document snapshots and command previews. `ToolController` delegates crop pointer events and publishes its frame-paced state changes to the UI. `CropOverlay` presents shading, thirds and screen-sized keyboard-operable handles; `CropDialog` can initialize from the draft. Pointer release retains a draft, while Apply dispatches `Document.crop` once. Cancellation clears RAF work and the frame; stale document identities/revisions reject before commit. Enter/Delete/arrows use the existing shortcut registry with crop-specific behavior, and focused handles consume their resize arrows to avoid a second global nudge. Existing canvas-revision resets handle successful crop and undo/redo. Public REST/scripting geometry contracts are unchanged.

The viewport render-region memo depends on current document width/height, not the stable DOM handle identity, so crop/resize and undo immediately request the correct region. An artwork-only clipping container bounds the previous frame while an asynchronous replacement is pending; editing overlays and crop handles can still extend outside the canvas. Pointer conversion uses that container’s canvas-sized bounds.

The internal raster draw boundary now receives the full world matrix, computes visible transformed bounds, and applies that matrix directly when drawing immutable source bitmaps. Tone effects still process bounded output tiles; each tile subtracts its output origin from the same placement matrix. Rotation, reflection and shear are tested at this internal boundary with independent Canvas references, including coverage across the 1024-pixel processing boundary. This does not make general layer transforms serializable or available in the UI; remaining leaf types, masks and GPU reference delegation must still carry complete matrices.

Vector and text leaf drawing now receive full world matrices and apply them directly through applyTransform. Vector culling maps path bounds into world space before testing render-region overlap, preserving paths rotated or sheared into view. Internal fixtures compare transformed Bézier fills and reflected/sheared text pixel-for-pixel with independent Canvas drawing. These boundaries are ready for affine data, but the translation-only schema and remaining paint/mask/tool/GPU boundaries still prevent public layer rotation.

Paint leaf drawing now takes a full world matrix for fills, brush/pencil stamps and clone source tiles. Visible stamp bounds are inverse-mapped into local space; stroke/clone bounds are mapped into world space for culling. ActiveStrokeRaster retains its translation adapter for mask callers but accepts a full matrix and includes it in reuse signatures. Selection coverage inverse-maps output subpixel samples using both diagonal and cross-axis steps in the WASM kernel; omitted cross-axis steps default to zero. The existing 4×4 Boolean coverage rule and bounded processing tiles remain unchanged. This internal WASM ABI change requires rebuilding pixels.wasm together with the JS wrapper. Mask geometry rasterization, GPU native strokes and tools still require affine propagation before stored layer transforms are enabled.

Mask coverage now accepts the mask-plane world matrix through selection/vector geometry, painted refinements, active stamps, prefix caches and feather tiles. Vector coverage keeps the fixed output tile grid and applies the complete matrix within each tile. Raw coverage/cache signatures include that matrix. Canvas composition passes linked/unlinked mask matrices directly. Feather remains a document-pixel coverage operation after geometry transformation, so scaling geometry does not scale the feather radius. Translation adapters remain for callers not yet migrated, particularly GPU mask delegation. General affine GPU sampling, document schema and tools remain unfinished.

GPU layer-mask coverage now receives the complete mask-plane matrix and includes it in its retained texture signature. Translation-only, unfeathered selections retain the existing native shader. Other transformed mask coverage uses the shared Canvas/WASM renderer and uploads the result before GPU density/inversion/compositing. Matrix changes with identical origins invalidate the texture. A SwiftShader test reads the actual uploaded texture, verifies exact alpha agreement with shared coverage, and checks reuse versus invalidation. This is hybrid GPU compositing, not a claim that affine mask geometry is rasterized natively in WGSL.

GPU reference leaf rendering now passes a complete world matrix into a Canvas-only rootTransform option. Its isolated neutral layer uses zero local translation, preventing double application of the source position. The option is an internal Canvas reference basis, not a generic GPU render option, persisted property or scripting API. Raster/vector/text reference callers and clone/fill delegation carry the composed world matrix; native GPU brush/pencil sampling remains a separate migration. An actual GPU texture-readback fixture checks transformed reference geometry against independently specified Canvas curves.

## Adjustment layers and tonal primitives

`AdjustmentLayer` introduces non-destructive, full-stack adjustment layers with `kind: "adjustment"`. Unlike content layers, adjustment layers do not own raster assets or spatial bounds. Instead, they evaluate non-linear transfer functions against the accumulated preceding backdrop stack.

Stack ordering and masking:

- An adjustment layer modifies the accumulated backdrop up to its position in the layer tree.
- Stack bounds: layer masks (selection, vector, or paint) constrain the adjustment's spatial influence. Outside the mask, the backdrop remains completely unchanged.
- **Alpha preservation invariant**: adjustment layers strictly preserve the backdrop's alpha channel. Transparent pixels remain zero alpha and color; semi-transparent pixels retain their exact alpha.

Transfer math and lookup tables:

- **Curves**: Evaluated via monotone cubic spline interpolation (Fritsch-Carlson algorithm in `src/core/adjustments.ts`), ensuring monotonicity between control points and preventing overshoot artifacts. Generates 256-byte lookup tables per channel (RGB master, red, green, blue).
- **Levels**: Evaluated via piecewise transfer functions mapping input black/white points and midtone gamma to output black/white points.
- **Lookup table composition**: Precomputed composite 768-byte lookup tables (R, G, B) allow single-pass evaluation across pixel buffers.
- **Processing space**: Strictly encoded 8-bit sRGB processing space. High dynamic range, 16-bit float, and non-sRGB working spaces remain future architectural milestones.

WASM and WebGPU execution:

- **Canvas/WASM Reference Renderer**: The backdrop region is read back and passed to the compiled WASM kernel (`applyLut` for 768-byte table lookup, `blendAdjustment` for in-place alpha-preserving interpolation).
- **WebGPU Compositor**: Evaluates Tone adjustments and Master Levels natively in the processing WGSL shader (`case 6u` and `case 7u`), preserving backdrop alpha and premultiplied color representation. Non-master (per-channel) levels and non-linear spline Curves trigger clean fallback to the reference CanvasRenderer via `AdaptiveRenderer`.
- **Tonal Histogram**: Bounded 256-bin histogram computation (R, G, B, Luminance using `0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B`) with mean, median, stdDev, and total pixels statistics. Computed via WASM `histogram` kernel with a pure TypeScript fallback.

## Generation and batch review corrections (2026-09-30)

Generation must reject unconfigured providers. Procedural providers belong exclusively in test fixtures; no synthetic fallback is permitted in job execution, reference capture, source-image loading, or batch export. The provider bakeoff remains incomplete and must not infer real scores from fixture images or profile constants.

Encoded candidate images must decode successfully, match declared dimensions, and have their transparency verified from decoded pixels. Invalid candidates cannot be promoted into project assets. Masked edits use reference-rendered document pixels, including groups, masks, text, paint and adjustments; capture errors prevent submission. Synchronous recipes reject `ai.generate` before applying any commands.

Batch runs persist source bytes and completed variant checkpoints. Reload recovery resumes interrupted work and skips successful items; completed variant bytes are hash-checked before reuse. Missing or undecodable sources and rendering/encoding failures fail the item explicitly. PNG, JPEG and WebP deliverables must contain the requested format and dimensions, independent of viewport allocation defaults.

### GPU affine stroke and selection sampling
