GPU brush/pencil stamps now use complete linear transforms, with centers rebased in double precision before upload. Selection regions carry an inverse transform into normalized local coordinates, preserving rotated/sheared Boolean clips. Incremental surface keys include all matrix coefficients. Brush flow, size-pressure and opacity-pressure settings reach native stamps; bounds honor disabled size pressure. Subpixel marks under non-axis-aligned transforms use the reference path when the sampling grid cannot preserve coverage. Axis-aligned pencil coverage remains analytic.

This is internal rendering support for T07. Stored layer transforms and public tool coordinates remain translation-only until the model/command/tool migration is complete. SwiftShader tests exercise real WGSL correctness, not hardware performance. Transformed antialiasing is compared with bounded tolerances, not claimed to be byte-identical to Canvas.

GPU erasers use destination-out against accumulated paint in both preview and committed replay, including clipped coverage, flow and opacity pressure. Hard brush/pencil edges use 8×8 coverage samples; fully covered interiors skip sampling, and soft gradients retain 4×4 sampling. One hard eraser fixture differs from Canvas by up to 33 alpha values at an antialiased edge (mean below 0.32 over the image); that GPU edge agrees with independent 64×64 numerical circle integration. This is a documented rasterizer difference, not a universal backend tolerance.

Generation job dispatch must check queued state before invoking an adapter. Host abort races settle provider/staging waits even when an adapter ignores its signal; late validation results are discarded. External cancellation billing still requires a production adapter's reconciliation contract. Candidate promotion owns a separate decoded bitmap from the staging shelf. Apply checks revision both before promotion and inside the commit transaction; failed commit removes only the promoted asset, preserving staged pixels for retry.

Candidate placement captures the protected reference before asynchronous promotion. Promotion rechecks candidate identity after bitmap cloning; preview/apply recheck after composite rendering and before returning or committing. Discard or staging disposal during either wait rejects placement, releases temporary assets/surfaces, and leaves document history unchanged. Rollback must not turn a discarded candidate back into a staged candidate. Override approval does not bypass candidate lifetime checks.

The staging repository owns copied protected-edit verification context. It computes reports from actual raw/decoded pixels at staging and again before apply; provider reports are discarded. Invalid references or unreadable candidate pixels cannot be treated as successful verification. Protected application additionally inserts the proposed layer into an isolated document snapshot and renders the complete composite in native-resolution 1024-pixel tiles through the Canvas/WASM renderer. The final comparison includes placement, parent transforms, blending, masks, and existing effects; pixels outside the edit coverage are protected even without a separate protected mask. The final report replaces the raw-candidate report before commit. A violation requires an explicit override, rendering failures reject, and a revision change during verification rejects even when stale placement was previously authorized. Rejection removes the promoted asset without changing document history. Rendering surfaces are bounded; reference, result, and diff buffers still scale with document resolution. Recipe compilation preserves complete recorded layer templates, using constructors for defaults and generating fresh identities before shared command validation.

Batch delivery fitting uses a renderer view that maps output tile regions back into source-document coordinates. `RenderOptions.outputSize` selects the output aspect ratio independently of the source region, subject to the renderer's working allocation budgets. Both Canvas and GPU derive their sampling scale from that region/output pair. This preserves nested transforms, local mask coordinates, font geometry and effects without rewriting layer DTOs. The delivery view clips contain margins to the source artboard and does not own/dispose the shared renderer. PNG continues to render bounded output tiles; JPEG/WebP use the existing full-output encoding allocation.

Recovery storage v2 retains three session checkpoints. Document and source-metadata/blob SHA-256 checksums are computed before the atomic IndexedDB write. Retained revisions share immutable hashed source records; garbage collection uses their combined references. Restore validates each revision newest-first and returns both its project blob and fallback information for the recovery dialog. Legacy records remain structurally readable. This does not restore undo history or supply portable-file integrity checks.

Portable container v3 adds a raw SHA-256 manifest digest in its 48-byte header and a hexadecimal SHA-256 field per original asset. Save captures the document/source references synchronously, then hashes compressed assets sequentially and returns a Promise<Blob>. Load verifies checksums before decoding or replacing active state. V1/v2 readers remain for compatibility; their lack of checksums is not represented as verified integrity. UI save state records the revision captured before asynchronous hashing.

Command discovery reads `ShortcutRegistry.actions`; palette execution rechecks availability and invokes the same callback rather than constructing a parallel command path. Search ranking is a pure helper. The palette unmounts before dispatching actions that may open another modal, preventing focus restoration from stealing focus from the new dialog. The central shortcut hook treats palette and recovery dialogs as modal state. This adds no new document schema or scripting mutation surface.

Layer filtering is view-only. A pure traversal computes direct matches and the union of matching ancestors while carrying effective visibility/locking down the tree. LayersPanel renders the original layer objects by those IDs, preserving commands, drag targets and active selection. Filter state is not serialized or added to history and resets on document replacement. Collapsed group state remains separate from the temporary filtered expansion.

EditorStore keeps immutable ordered `selectedIds` plus compatible `selectedId`, pruning absent handles after commands/undo/redo. LayerSelection is a document-owned OOP view; selected roots exclude descendants whose selected ancestors already receive a transform. Translation, alignment and removal use existing commands inside one transaction and preflight root locks. Script worker transport includes the full set, validates active/set consistency and extends read-only-plugin checks. Multi-layer canvas movement captures root positions and revision at pointer-down, previews a transaction, and validates revision before commit. Selection is not serialized into artwork or undo snapshots.

### Batch recipe ownership

New batch configurations persist a deep-cloned `recipeSnapshot` alongside `recipeId`. Cost estimation and item execution use this snapshot, so changing or deleting a reusable recipe cannot change an existing run. Missing recipes are rejected before batch creation. Legacy runs with a recipe ID but no snapshot must be recreated explicitly; the runner refuses to infer the historical definition from current recipe storage. Runs without recipes remain supported.

### Batch persistence failures

Browser batch storage requires IndexedDB. Open, write, delete, and read failures propagate to callers; browser reads use durable records rather than the headless memory backend. Writes update memory only after the transaction commits. A worker-pool checkpoint failure aborts remaining workers, waits for them to settle, emits `run_failed`, and makes `waitForRun` reject. The Batch dialog displays the error. The last durable checkpoint remains available for explicit resume; an unsuccessful persistence attempt cannot itself record a new durable status. Headless Node tests retain an in-memory backend.

### Batch execution ownership

Browser start/resume acquires an exclusive Web Lock named for the run and holds it until its worker pool settles. A competing tab fails explicitly instead of interpreting a live run's `running` items as interrupted work. Browser termination releases ownership automatically. Same-instance starts retain deduplication, and resume waits for a previous local ownership scope to finish. Browsers without Web Locks reject execution rather than silently run without coordination. This covers execution ownership only; remote pause/cancel/review mutations require additional coordination.

### Atomic batch updates

`BatchStorage.updateRun` applies a synchronous mutation inside one IndexedDB read/write transaction. Missing records and callback errors reject and abort. Worker picking/checkpointing, pause/cancel, worker-pool finalization, and review edits use this operation; cancelled item state is preserved against late worker patches. Completed manifests are derived from each service read/export snapshot, rather than persisted by overwriting a potentially stale run. This prevents lost updates in these paths. Start/recovery/retry and deletion still require broader lifecycle coordination.

### Batch retry and deletion ownership

Retry acquires the same execution lock as start/resume before resetting failed items. Start/recovery transitions use atomic run mutations and check that preflight has not been superseded by a lifecycle change. Deletion through the batch service rejects active local/remote workers and holds exclusive execution ownership while removing the run and its source/output blobs in one IndexedDB transaction. Deterministic variant blob keys are also removed, including outputs written before their checkpoint. Remote cancellation still needs provider/worker notification and cancellation-output cleanup.

### Cross-tab batch control notifications

Pause/cancel persist their state before publishing a same-origin BroadcastChannel notification. Active owners reread the durable run before applying a pause flag or abort signal, avoiding stale-message cancellation of a later run. Disposing a batch runner closes its channel and aborts local workers. Canvas calls already in progress still settle before ownership is released; abort guards prevent subsequent variants and cancelled item state remains durable. Environments without BroadcastChannel retain durable-state checks at worker picking/finalization but cannot promptly notify an in-flight worker.

### Atomic batch output publication

Rendering returns encoded bytes without persisting them. `commitDeliverable` writes the blob and its item checkpoint in one transaction over runs/blobs, after verifying the item still accepts outputs. Cancelled or removed items reject publication. A post-render abort check avoids submitting known-cancelled bytes; the durable-state check also covers cancellation whose notification has not reached the worker. Previously checkpointed variants remain available after cancellation. This prevents new unreferenced outputs from interrupted publication; deletion still removes legacy deterministic variant blobs.

### Per-document canvas views

The editor UI retains zoom and pan by live Document object identity in a weak map. Switching tabs immediately reads that document's view; a new document fits once, while later viewport observer notifications preserve the user's view. Explicit Fit and Actual Size actions still reset the active view. Reopening the same project into separate tabs does not share view state merely because serialized document IDs match. View state is session-only, not restored after page reload or included in portable projects.

### Current T07 layer matrix migration (schema 6)

Superseding the earlier translation-only schema status: layers may now persist an invertible zero-translation affine basis, composed after the existing x/y translation. DOM `Layer.transform` reads/writes the full local-to-parent matrix, sharing command validation/history with REST and scripts. Canvas/GPU traversal and hit testing already consume `localTransform`, so they now render stored matrices. Cross-document copying records the composed world basis when lifting a selected descendant to the destination root. Tool coordinate conversion, reparenting, mask link toggles and alignment are still being migrated; those operations on nontranslation layers are not yet complete.

Recipe `stepResult` targets may include `childPath: number[]`, a zero-based path through the group at the producing step. Compilation binds this path to that descendant's generated ID when the group is added or duplicated. Later reorders do not change the binding; removal causes subsequent references to fail validation. The recorder emits these references for descendants of added and duplicated groups. Duplicate commands reserve IDs for the whole subtree before simulation so dry-run and transactional execution agree. Existing targets without a child path still resolve the producing root.

Recipe parameter targets resolve exact layer IDs first, then exact names. Multiple name matches fail dry-run by default and with `ambiguityStrategy: "fail"`; explicit `"first"` permits choosing the first match; `allowMultiple` executes against every matching layer. Failed resolution prevents the entire recipe from mutating the document.

Generation accounting recovery foundation: the host-only `BudgetLedger.snapshot()` returns a detached schema-version-1 snapshot of approvals, accumulated spending, and outstanding reservations. `restore(unknown)` validates the entire snapshot and all reservation references/identities before atomically replacing memory. Recovery retains over-budget actual charges and revoked/expired approvals. Creation rejects negative prior spending and duplicate budget IDs; reservations reject duplicate outstanding job IDs. This snapshot API is not exposed to scripts/plugins. The durable accounting journal uses it; full job reconstruction remains incomplete; saved candidate restoration is described below.

Browser generation now uses `GenerationJournal` for authoritative accounting. The service awaits recovery at submit, hashes an immutable request, reserves/deduplicates atomically, and saves dispatch intent before invoking the adapter. Confirmed settlement is asynchronous and durable before output staging; failed writes retain unresolved reservations. Recovered explicit keys return a terminal explanatory job instead of issuing a second provider request. The host can inventory and reconcile persisted accounting even without an in-memory job. Generation dialog approval changes use the durable service method and generation stays disabled until accounting recovery succeeds. Complete job reconstruction and cross-tab execution ownership are still pending. `GenerationRecoveryPanel` loads unfinished accounting on opening/focus and explicit refresh, displays pending reservations, and exposes `cancelRecoveredQueued` only for reserved entries. Cancellation uses the journal transaction as the authority, so a stale UI cannot release a request that another tab has already marked dispatched. Failed writes retain the row and budget; successful cancellation refreshes available funds.

Browser generation injects `GenerationCandidateStorage` alongside the accounting journal. Successful output receives a host-owned candidate identity and is saved with provenance and copied protected context before job completion. Candidate restore is lazy when opening the generation dialog; it validates integrity and image decoding, re-evaluates protection, and marks candidates as restored so placement needs explicit review even if revision numbers happen to match. Saved candidates remain reusable until durable discard. Storage failures keep usable charged output in the current session with an error. Cancellation during storage removes the candidate, while billing settlement remains authoritative.

Completed-job idempotency recovery checks the journal before provider resolution. Matching requests load verified candidate pixels and provenance, reconcile them against saved accounting, and reconstruct a completed GenerationJob with original timestamps and base revision. Concurrent recovery uses one in-flight promise per job. Reading a paid result does not require new consent; incompatible request fingerprints still reject. No result is fabricated for an unresolved or discarded candidate, and recovery never redispatches such requests.

REST generation correction: server/app.ts no longer synthesizes placeholder output by patching PNG headers. Unconfigured generation returns 503, and analysis remains explicitly unsupported. An injected host executor returns validated-size decoded RGBA; the server encodes the complete PNG through the shared encoder. Cancellation/target deletion/shutdown abort execution and prevent late staging. REST idempotency binds normalized inputs within the document and retains keyed records for the server session. This executor boundary remains separate from browser accounting and is not a bundled production-provider integration. The shared headless GenerationJobService also now binds keys to request/provider/budget and retains terminal failures instead of silently charging again.

### Batch terminal failure reporting

When workers finish all pending items, any failed item makes the run `failed`; otherwise cancelled items make it `cancelled`, and only a run without either outcome becomes `completed`. A terminal item failure emits `run_failed` with the persisted run and an actionable error summary. Successfully produced deliverables remain available, and selective retry continues to preserve successful items. Explicit pause/cancel takes precedence over finalization.

### Recipe write failure recovery

Recipe saves and deletions write the proposed library to browser storage before replacing the in-memory library. Write failures propagate; the previous saved library remains authoritative. A stopped recording that fails to save remains in `RecipeService.pendingRecording` for the application session. The recipe dialog exposes retry and JSON export, including after closing and reopening the dialog. Starting another recording is rejected until the pending recording is saved. This draft is not durable: export it before reloading or closing the application when storage remains unavailable. Headless execution without localStorage retains its in-memory behavior. Corrupt-library recovery and cross-tab write coordination are described below.

### Candidate-specific protected-edit approval

The generation dialog binds override consent to the selected candidate ID and the currently displayed verification report. Switching candidates clears consent, including when returning to a previously reviewed result. Replacing a report invalidates earlier consent. The application call passes an override only for the approved candidate. Reference preview association remains separate outstanding review work.

### Candidate reference preview association

Protected-edit review obtains its Before image from the selected staged candidate's captured protection context, including contexts reconstructed from saved candidate storage. Changing candidates changes the reference image; live document or form changes no longer replace it. The display thumbnail samples into a surface with a maximum 512-pixel edge and does not copy the full reference buffer. This preview is for navigation only; invariant verification continues to use the original full-resolution pixels. Final-composite versus raw-candidate After visualization remains a separate outstanding improvement.

### Unreadable recipe library preservation

Recipe loading validates the complete library before replacing its cache, rejecting malformed JSON, non-array roots, invalid entries, and duplicate IDs. A failed read retains the last readable cache and blocks persistence so an apparently empty library cannot overwrite unreadable data. The recipe dialog reports the failure and offers an exact copy of the original stored text for external recovery, plus retry-read after repair or restored storage access. No automatic reset or data deletion occurs. Browser saves, imports and deletions acquire the exclusive `luma-recipe-library` Web Lock, reload and validate current storage inside the lock, then commit the mutation. Independent tabs cannot overwrite unrelated saves or resurrect deleted records from stale caches. Same-ID writes follow lock order (last committed write wins). These persistence methods and their RecipeService wrappers return promises; callers must await completion. Browsers without Web Locks reject writes explicitly and retain export recovery. Read methods return detached snapshots; use `reload()` to refresh a cached library.

### Generation geometry validation before billing

GenerationJobService validates target/reference integer geometry and representable RGBA byte counts before idempotency lookup, reservation, or dispatch. Supplied references must contain exact RGBA byte lengths; edit/protection masks must match target geometry with one coverage byte per pixel. Masked/protected edits require a matching reference. Invalid feather radii and protected region geometry reject before provider activity. These are format/geometry invariants, not an arbitrary megapixel cap; provider-specific capability constraints remain separate.

### Verified-composite review imagery

Final placement verification attaches a transient bounded thumbnail of the rendered composite to the candidate alongside the resulting invariant report, document ID and revision. When this report is shown after a rejected placement, the inspector displays and labels the verified composite rather than the raw candidate, and identifies the checked revision. Raw candidate re-verification clears this derived preview. Placement always renders and verifies again; thumbnails never serve as verification evidence. This does not yet provide a separate pre-apply placement preview operation or persist composite previews across recovery.

### Explicit protected placement preview

Check placement invokes a host-only preview branch of the shared placement implementation. It renders into a proposed document, publishes the verified composite report/thumbnail, and removes its temporary promoted asset while restoring candidate review state. It never enters the live document transaction. Concurrent document changes reject preview results; every later Apply rechecks. Preview clears prior UI override consent. The operation is restricted to protected candidates and does not call providers or reserve budget.

### Mask containment and protected placement decisions

When a candidate has host-owned protection context, final-composite verification determines whether placement requires an override. Raw candidate differences remain visible for review but do not reject a placement before its mask, opacity, blend and surrounding composition are rendered. A containment mask can therefore safely hide changed protected pixels. This retains exact native-resolution verification of the proposed document before commit and all revision guards; it does not trust a provider-supplied report. Without host protection context, an existing failed report still requires explicit override.

### Selected-root rotation

LayerSelection.rotate computes a canvas-space rotation around the union of selected-root bounds, applies it to each root's world matrix, then converts through the unchanged inverse parent matrix. All target matrices are prepared before one shared document transaction. Descendants of selected roots are excluded, inherited locks are preflighted, and every root must have geometry. Layer.transform dispatch provides common command validation and history for UI and scripting.

### Multi-selection rotation gesture

The rotation gesture captures selected-root world matrices, inverse parent matrices, shared bounds center, document ID and revision at pointerdown. Pointer moves derive a transaction preview from the captured matrices; pointerup processes its final position and commits the captured root patches in one transaction after the revision guard. Escape/pointer cancellation clears the preview. This extends single-layer rotation without changing the underlying transform commands or serialized representation.

### Selected-root scaling

LayerSelection.scale shares the center-transform preparation path with rotate. Positive canvas-axis scale factors are applied around the selected-root geometric union, then converted through each root's inverse parent matrix before a shared transaction. This preserves source geometry and asset identity; validation and transaction rollback reject singular/unrepresentable transforms or invalid roots without partial edits. Uniform presets use the same method as arbitrary-factor scripting.

### Multi-selection corner scale gesture

Multi-layer corner scaling captures root world matrices and inverse parent matrices at pointerdown, with the opposite union-bounds corner as the fixed pivot. Pointer coordinates relative to that pivot derive positive horizontal/vertical factors; Shift selects their shared maximum for uniform scaling. Captured matrices drive a transaction preview and one revision-guarded commit, sharing rotation's cancellation lifecycle. Pointer clamping prevents singular/reflected drag results; the DOM's explicit scaling method retains its positive-factor validation contract.

### Canvas snapping during movement

The pure snapToCanvas kernel compares translated bounds anchors with canvas edges/centers, choosing the smallest correction within tolerance per axis. Move gestures derive original bounds from the live document (not the already translated preview) and convert a six-screen-pixel threshold to document space using zoom. Corrected canvas deltas flow through existing parent-space movement conversion for single and multiple roots. Guide overlays are transient, pointer-inert, and cleared with the gesture preview; no document schema or serialization changes are introduced.

### Stationary-artwork snap targets

artworkSnapBounds traverses visible nonzero-opacity artwork, excludes moving subtrees and suppresses ancestor groups whose bounds would change with the selection. Geometric world bounds contribute edge/center coordinates to the same per-axis nearest-target solver as the canvas. Move gestures cache target bounds once per drag, avoiding repeated hierarchy scans during pointer movement. Canvas targets win exact distance ties by deterministic ordering. Snap results continue through existing canvas-to-parent movement conversion.

### Revision-bound canvas gestures

Layer and mask move gestures and single-layer resize now capture document identity/revision, matching multi-root rotation/scaling. A revision-change effect clears stale gestures, previews and snap guides; pointer updates also check the live revision before calculating from captured geometry or cached snap targets. Subsequent pointerup therefore cannot overwrite an intervening document edit. Gesture previews do not increment revision, so normal pointer movement remains uninterrupted.

### Empty recipe recordings

Stopping a recording with no supported actions returns the recorder to idle and rejects without creating or persisting a recipe. The dialog reports this outcome and allows a new recording. Empty recordings never synthesize selection changes. Document renames are recorded as declarative `document.rename` steps and replay through shared transactional history. Unsupported command coverage remains incomplete.

### Recorder coverage and effect bindings

The recorder captures effect additions and updates. Added effects receive fresh IDs at compilation; explicit references to an effect added earlier in the same recipe are mapped to that new ID. Recorded updates use a zero-based `effectIndex` in the target raster's current effect list; a missing position fails dry-run. Existing explicit `effectId` recipes remain supported. Unsupported commands are collected and shown in the recording UI, and stopping rejects the entire partial recording instead of silently saving an incomplete recipe. Starting a new recording resets this list. This makes coverage gaps explicit; it does not implement every editor command.

### Multi-target recipe steps

Compilation resolves `role: "all"` to all layers, including nested layers, and `allowMultiple: true` to all matches for name, kind, tag, parameter and prior-step-output selectors. Each step snapshots its targets before simulation. Individual property/effect operations run once per target; removal and duplication drop descendants of already-targeted groups because those structural operations include the subtree. Dry-run displays an operation per target. Any failed target prevents the entire recipe transaction from committing; successful execution is one undo entry.

Multi-output creation steps retain every output (including creation-time descendant bindings) for subsequent `stepResult` targets. Multiple results require `allowMultiple: true` or explicit `ambiguityStrategy: "first"`; default ambiguous references reject. Insertion parents must resolve to exactly one group. Single-target `resolveTarget` remains a compatibility helper; compilation uses the plural resolver.

Recipe effect lifecycle also supports `effect.remove` (optional `effectId` or zero-based `effectIndex`, defaulting to the layer's conventional tone effect) and `effect.reset` (remove all raster effects). The recorder emits positional removal bindings and captures reset directly. Missing removal targets fail dry-run rather than silently succeeding; reset requires a raster target. Both actions participate in multi-target validation and the recipe's single undo transaction.

Authored document guides render as pointer-inert DOM overlays at zoom-scaled document coordinates. Only in-canvas lines are displayed; off-canvas guide data is retained. Move snapping includes authored guide coordinates on the corresponding axis, using the existing six-screen-pixel tolerance and Alt bypass. Overlays are outside the artwork renderer and export pipeline. Session snapping remains opt-in.

The collapsed Guides inspector section uses Guide/GuideCollection for add, orientation/position edits, removal and clear, preserving command validation and undo. Guide visibility is a session-local App setting, shared across tabs in that editor workspace; toggling it changes neither document revision nor saved guide data. Hidden guides are excluded from move snapping. Numeric fields accept negative/fractional coordinates within the model bounds and support keyboard commit/cancel.

Existing guide lines are focusable drag handles only in the Move tool when layer movement is active and the editor is not busy or space-panning. GuideOverlay holds preview positions locally; pointer release submits one collection update. Escape, capture loss, pointer cancellation, document/revision, editability or zoom changes invalidate drafts. Focused guide arrows nudge on the matching axis; Shift uses ten pixels. The empty-document welcome overlay is suppressed when guides exist so guide-only documents remain editable.

Viewport rulers use 1/2/5-based pixel increments with at least 60 screen pixels between labeled ticks. Tick allocation depends on visible viewport extent, not document dimensions. Origins follow zoom/pan and ResizeObserver measurements. Ruler drags preview locally and create one Guide only when released inside the document; Escape/capture loss and document/revision/view changes cancel. Keyboard activation creates a centered guide. Rulers share guide visibility and remain outside artwork exports.

Recipe numeric parameters accept finite numbers or complete decimal strings (optional sign, fraction and exponent). Whitespace-only strings, unit suffixes, arrays, objects, booleans and nonfinite values reject before execution. Numeric layer patch conversion uses the same decimal parser. Boolean parameters accept actual booleans or the exact strings `true` and `false`; other coercions reject. Invalid parameters invalidate the entire plan even if conditions skip affected steps, preserving document state and revision.

Recipe compilation accepts an optional available-asset ID set and validates all references in the simulated final document with the shared `referencedAssets` traversal (raster sources, bitmap masks and clone tiles). Interactive dry-run supplies the active asset store; execution uses the Document's attached store; batch preflight supplies each item's staged store. Missing references invalidate the plan before document mutation or export. Data-only compilers without an asset context cannot establish availability. This guard does not bundle source bytes: JSON recipes containing source asset IDs remain dependent on those assets until portable recipe packaging is implemented.

## Retouch tonal kernel foundation

`core/retouch/dodgeBurn.ts` supplies the internal pure `applyDodgeBurn` operation for straight-alpha sRGB RGBA tiles. It returns new pixels, never changes source bytes or alpha, and preserves fully transparent hidden RGB and zero-coverage pixels. A one-byte-per-pixel coverage array represents brush/pressure coverage. Exposure and flow are each in [0,1]. Linear-light luminance L uses overlapping range weights: shadows 1−L, midtones 4L(1−L), highlights L. Signed strength spans at most two stops, scaled by exposure, flow, coverage and range weight. With gain g, the luminance curve is L′=gL/(1+(g−1)L); RGB shares its linear-light scale. Protect tones defaults on and limits the common gain before any channel clips. This is a defined Canoli Studio curve, not Photoshop compatibility. Non-sRGB inputs must be converted before use.

The kernel is connected to `PixelProcessor.dodgeBurn(pixels, width, height, options, coverage?)`, which runs it as JavaScript in the existing pixel worker. This method snapshots caller inputs before awaiting worker readiness and transfers only its private pixel copy; it does not detach caller buffers. This is CPU worker execution, not a WASM or GPU retouch kernel. It now renders persistent tonal adjustments through the shared compositor and public DOM/scripting constructors; interactive brush tools remain unfinished. T20 still requires non-destructive stroke storage, sampling controls, preview/commit behavior, healing/patch solvers and performance/browser evidence. The current unit tests establish neutral-ramp monotonicity/direction, neutral-channel equality, alpha/source preservation, zero coverage and input validation; they do not establish complete retouching quality or the healing performance gate.

`engine/retouch.ts` now supplies internal `renderTonalStroke(source, brush, adjustment, space, processor, world?)`. It validates a brush/pencil path using the existing mask-stroke contract, snapshots inputs, renders pressure/hardness/spacing/flow/selection coverage and sends the sampled source tile to the tonal worker. Flow belongs to brush stamp accumulation and is not multiplied again by the tonal kernel; zero flow returns unchanged pixels. Coverage rasterization uses a fixed 256-output-pixel lattice with two-pixel gutters to make request tiling independent of Canvas clip bounds. Temporary coverage canvases are bounded and released per cell. Persistent tonal adjustments now use this bridge against their preceding live backdrop. Additional sampling policies and interactive tool gestures remain required.

Tonal adjustment layers persist in document schema v8. `TonalStroke` is a detached constructor value containing an ordinary validated brush/pencil path and tonal parameters. `AdjustmentLayer.addTonalStroke` appends through shared layer-update commands, preserving masks, inherited locks and undo. The compositor samples the preceding backdrop, applies each stroke in order through bounded working tiles and then applies normal adjustment opacity/mask/blend semantics. GPU capability detection rejects this spatial adjustment kind and uses the Canvas fallback; it must never be treated as a global lookup table. Older document schemas with tonal data reject before migration.

Portable recipe execution through RecipeService captures the active document session generation before repository loading or image decoding. Document activation and service disposal invalidate the generation, including switching away and back to the same document. The private package executor invokes the captured guard after asynchronous preparation and before source installation, alongside existing revision/store/selection checks. Invalidated runs close staged bitmaps and commit no assets or history. Batch execution uses its independent staging document and does not depend on the interactive active session.

Batch estimates compile one plan per item using captured source geometry, final item naming, and merged batch/item parameters. Invalid plans (including enabled AI generation steps unsupported by the synchronous runner) reject preflight before workers start. Conditions that skip those steps remain usable. The dialog and persisted runs share the same filename/duplicate-name transformation. This preflight checks plan executability, not source decoding or package integrity: execution still validates actual source bytes, decoded geometry, installed asset references and commands. Asynchronous AI recipe/batch orchestration remains unfinished.

### Poisson retouch kernel foundation

`src/core/retouch/poisson.ts` implements a four-neighbor Dirichlet solve on selected pixels using matrix-free conjugate gradients with an IC(0) preconditioner per encoded-RGB channel. The geometry-only incomplete-Cholesky factor is shared across channels. The numerical formulation follows [Pérez, Gangnet and Blake, Poisson Image Editing (2003)](https://www.cs.princeton.edu/courses/archive/fall16/cos526/papers/perez03.pdf). Donor pixels must already be aligned to the target; callers supply a padded patch with zero coverage on its outer ring. Holes and disconnected selections use the surrounding target as fixed boundary values. Source guidance transfers donor gradients; mixed guidance chooses the stronger signed gradient per edge/channel. Transparent donor edges fall back to target guidance; transparent targets and target alpha remain unchanged. Coverage feathers the clamped solution against the target. Inputs remain immutable.

`PixelProcessor.poissonBlend` snapshots target/donor/coverage/options before asynchronous readiness and performs the iterative solve through the allocation-free AssemblyScript/WASM kernel in the pixel worker. A TypeScript numerical backend remains the reference. Private donor and coverage buffers transfer without a second structured-clone copy. Its result includes pixels, convergence, maximum channel iteration count and maximum absolute equation residual before RGB clamping/quantization. Defaults are 500 iterations and 0.001 residual in 8-bit RGB units. Exhausting iterations is an explicit nonconverged result, which future tool commits must reject or recompute. Malformed geometry/options and missing padding reject. This is an internal engine API, not a public healing DOM method. Fixed boundary values do not establish arbitrary C1 gradient continuity. Donor selection, non-destructive patch storage, gestures, cancellation during solving and GPU acceleration remain unfinished.

Run `node --import tsx scripts/benchmark-retouch.ts` for a correctness-checked Node reference timing baseline, or append `--wasm` to measure the production numerical backend; it is not browser interaction latency. The initial measurements are in `docs/benchmarks/poisson-kernel-node-2026-09-30.json`. The 128/256-pixel cases exceed the roadmap's 50 ms requirement, so the performance gate remains open.

The IC(0)/WASM comparison is retained in `docs/benchmarks/poisson-kernel-ic0-node-2026-09-30.json` and `docs/benchmarks/poisson-kernel-wasm-node-2026-09-30.json`. Both use unchanged fixtures, tolerance and pixel checks. WASM versus TypeScript regressions cover both guidance modes, irregular masks, varied RGB/alpha and incomplete convergence. WASM memory is host-managed, aligned and reused; out-of-range working-buffer/iteration requests reject rather than truncate. The 256-square median improved from approximately 682 ms (unpreconditioned TypeScript baseline) to 400 ms (WASM IC(0)); this still fails the 50 ms gate and is not a hardware/browser interaction guarantee.

### Retouch sampling and patch preparation

`retouchSampleDocument` captures a detached layer tree for `current-layer`, `current-and-below` or `all-layers`. Current-layer retains only the selected branch, including ancestor transforms, masks, visibility and opacity; selecting a group includes its complete subtree. Current-and-below retains preceding siblings at every ancestor level. Following siblings are excluded. All-layers uses the complete visible composition. Missing targets or unknown modes reject. These are engine sampling semantics, not yet UI options.

`sampleRetouchRegion` reads native pixels in at-most-1024-square render surfaces; cancellation and readback failure release the current surface and stop further tiles. The returned buffer still scales with the requested region. `prepareRetouchPatch` captures document/selection/options before asynchronous work, computes a canvas-clipped padded bounding rectangle, rasterizes selection coverage with the existing WASM selection kernel, and samples target/donor pixels from that captured composition. Donor offset uses integer document pixels; selected donor coordinates outside the canvas reject. The worker solves and feathers the patch while preserving target alpha. Empty selection and nonconvergence reject explicitly. Preparation returns pixels/coverage/bounds and solver diagnostics without installing assets or creating history. It is not yet a persisted patch layer, host commit, DOM method or interactive patch/healing tool. Automatic donor search, commit-time session guards, edit storage and the performance/quality gates remain outstanding.

### Recipe target and displacement semantics

The `active-mask` semantic target resolves only the selected layer when it has a mask; missing selection or an unmasked selection fails resolution. It never substitutes another masked layer. Recorded output aliases use generated identifiers independent of user layer names.

Recipe `layer.translate` actions accept finite numeric `dx` and `dy` values (or parameter references resolving to numbers), in the target layer's parent coordinate space. They compile to shared position commands and participate in the recipe's atomic undo transaction. `layer.duplicate` accepts optional `inPlace: true` to retain the source position; the default retains the editor's 24-pixel duplicate displacement. The product shadow preset duplicates in place, then translates by its requested offsets. Invalid offsets fail dry-run before any mutations.

### Persistent patch adjustments

Document schema v9 adds `adjustment.kind: "patch"` with `assetId`, `width`, and `height`. The immutable `PatchAdjustment` scripting/DOM value captures this descriptor. Rendering transforms the referenced corrected RGB/coverage image through the layer matrix in bounded 1024-pixel tiles, interpolates RGB by coverage while preserving preceding alpha, then applies normal adjustment opacity/mask/blend behavior. Corrected colors are stored snapshots, not live Poisson recomputation. Project asset enumeration, cross-document copy and portable recipe collection/remapping retain the referenced images, including patch replacements in layer-update actions. Versions below 9 reject patch data. Solver preparation and persistent patch assets remain separate until the commit/tool integration is completed; callers must not apply feather coverage twice.

The trusted `EditorApplication.applyPatch(offset, sampling?, solverOptions?, signal?)` operation now captures the selection/document, prepares corrected RGB with binary solver support, encodes original fractional coverage once, and commits one patch layer at the document root. The preparation result retains both unfeathered `correctedPixels` and coverage-composited `pixels`. Revision, active-session generation, asset-store identity, selection and cancellation checks precede installation; stale work releases private resources. The host method is not an isolated scripting binding or REST endpoint. Browser PNG encoding/decoding still requires a surface large enough for the selected patch and can fail on device limits; no megapixel import restriction is introduced.

The Patch tool captures a document revision and settings on pointer-down. Pointer motion updates only its integer donor offset and a transient translated selection outline. Pointer-up invokes `applyPatch` with a controller-owned abort signal; tool cancellation/reset aborts pending work. Shared keyboard registration provides `J`; editable-field handling remains centralized. Selection geometry is retained after commit and the new patch adjustment becomes selected. The tool currently displays donor geometry rather than a solved pixel preview.

### Local donor-search proposal

`core/retouch/donor.ts` implements deterministic local exemplar scoring. The selection mask marks excluded/damaged pixels. Candidate offsets must keep the selected support and its visible four-neighbor boundary inside the sampled region, avoid all selected pixels, and supply sufficient alpha. Scores compare boundary RGB differences after removing most constant channel offsets (variance plus a 0.01 mean-square color penalty), plus alpha error. Lower score wins; equal scores prefer shorter displacement and then traversal order. The damaged interior's RGB is never used to rank candidates. This is a boundary heuristic, not semantic recognition or a guarantee that an unselected donor is defect-free.

`PixelProcessor.findDonor` captures caller pixels, mask and options before awaiting worker readiness, and transfers private copies. `engine/donor-search.ts` captures the requested layer sampling scope, renders a native-resolution window around the selection and proposes an integer document-space offset. Search radius defaults to 64 pixels and is configurable; it is a local search parameter, not an image import cap. Empty/no-context/no-valid-donor inputs reject explicitly. Abort signals stop future sampling and reject late proposals; disposal of a dedicated processor can terminate an in-flight search. No result mutates assets, document data or history. No public DOM/REST binding, automatic healing gesture or confidence threshold ships with this foundation. Exhaustive candidate scoring still needs performance/corpus evaluation and optimization for larger search windows.

### Healing stroke integration

`renderRetouchCoverage` is the shared fixed-grid brush mask rasterizer for tonal and healing paths. `prepareHealingStroke` captures brush data, selected sampling scope and solver options; renders native coverage and local source pixels; searches intact donor support; and solves a padded patch with fractional coverage applied once. The trusted host `EditorApplication.healStroke(brush: BrushStroke, sampling?, solverOptions?, radius = 64, signal?)` uses the same private guarded encode/install/transaction path as Patch, with a single `Healing stroke` history entry. It never changes the current pixel selection to stage a stroke. The method is an application-host service, not an isolated script or REST binding. The tool creates a stroke on pointer-down, accumulates/smooths pressure points with animation-frame overlay updates, and calls the host on pointer-up. Cancellation/reset aborts the owned signal. Each stroke currently becomes a new adjustment layer; editable source-stroke/donor provenance, review/reselection UI, live solved previews and the full public retouch API remain open.

Retouch operations attach their abort signal to their dedicated pixel processor. Aborting terminates that worker and rejects active numerical requests, instead of waiting for donor search/Poisson completion before discarding results. Shared viewport rendering is not terminated; cancellation still checks after an in-flight render/PNG encode/decode. PixelProcessor disposal is idempotent and rejects readiness as well as queued/active requests, including shutdown before the WASM worker becomes ready. Synchronous message-cloning failures remove the failed pending entry and preserve worker usability.

Donor search uses exact packed 32-bit support checks when all selected pixels have the same target alpha. A blocked-source bitmap represents selected/damaged pixels and insufficient donor alpha; shifted word intersections reject invalid candidates. Arbitrary masks and word/row boundaries retain scalar semantics. Variable target alpha falls back to per-pixel comparisons. Boundary scoring, candidate count and deterministic tie-breaking are unchanged. The scalar reference remains executable for parity verification.

When selected support and visible boundary have the same alpha, donor validation packs both into the checked footprint. After validity is established, candidates cannot improve a zero-score winner unless closer: all score terms are nonnegative. Such candidates still increment the valid-candidate count but skip redundant RGB scoring. The scalar path remains exhaustive, including boundary checks, and parity tests verify identical donor/score/count under transparency and distance ties. Nonzero winners and nonuniform-alpha cases retain their existing scoring behavior.

The pixel worker now supplies a WASM packed-validity backend to donor search. One allocation-free ABI call scans all candidate offsets in dy/dx order and returns a private byte validity grid; RGB scoring, counts and tie-breaking remain in TypeScript. Host validation checks grid geometry, support rows, memory size and aligned buffer layout before copying. Returned validity bytes are detached from reusable WASM memory. Variable-alpha support still uses the scalar path. Actual WASM parity checks compare donor, score, counts and errors against the scalar oracle across irregular masks, transparency and 7/31/32/33/65px row widths.

Healing reuses its captured native donor-search pixels when they fully contain the requested target/donor solver rectangles. Extraction copies detached row-aligned RGBA arrays and validates safe integer geometry and source byte length. Incomplete windows return a miss; the solver renders that rectangle normally. This fallback is essential at canvas edges because artwork can extend beyond the artboard and solver halos must preserve those pixels rather than substitute transparency. Reuse is scoped to one captured preparation, not a persistent cache or live-document read.

### Candidate target lifetime and repeated placement

Candidate promotion captures the destination AssetStore lifetime before cloning its bitmap and checks it before installation. Shared preview/application also checks that lifetime after rendering and before commit. Closing a document disposes its store and invalidates outstanding placement, even when the document revision remains unchanged or stale placement is authorized. Each promotion receives a fresh project asset identity; the staged candidate identity remains stable. Reapplying after undo therefore preserves assets retained by history, and rollback removes only the current attempt's asset.

Recipe output bindings represent unique layer identities. An output alias equal to its own step ID is valid and binds once. Aliases colliding with another step ID or alias reject both schema validation and execution preflight.

### Tonal sculpt public operation

`Document.applyTonalSculpt` validates a shared operation envelope, constructs immutable BrushStroke/TonalStroke values, and inserts a complete AdjustmentLayer through one root `layer.add` command. It captures pixel selection by default and keeps path coordinates in document space. This avoids selected-group transforms changing the meaning of public paths. REST `/documents/:id/tonal-sculpt` adds revision validation then invokes the same DOM method. The existing isolated scripting runtime bundles the method automatically. Rendering remains the existing live-backdrop tonal worker path; no new rasterization or provider dependency is introduced.

### Patch source/destination placement

`PatchOptions` extends Poisson solver options with an independent `direction`, defaulting to source. `prepareRetouchPatch` captures and validates the direction and offset before asynchronous work. Destination placement translates the complete Boolean/affine selection in document space and negates the sampling offset; the common bounds/coverage/solver pipeline then processes the resulting repair region. It never mutates the document selection to implement translation. Host lifetime, cancellation and single-layer commit behavior are shared across both modes. Tool settings are captured at gesture start, and the overlay distinguishes donor from destination placement. Gradient guidance remains `mode: source | mixed`; placement direction does not change the Poisson equation.

### Atomic isolated-script patch preparation

The sandbox Document's internal preparation callback sends its command prefix and validated patch request over the existing isolated channel. ScriptRetouch reconstructs that prefix against the captured host snapshot using parsed shared commands, validates referenced assets, and renders using a private asset view. Existing source bitmaps are borrowed; new corrected-pixel assets are owned by the preparation scope. A dedicated pixel worker is aborted when the script scope ends. Prepared layer DTOs are added to the sandbox document through ordinary layer.add commands, allowing subsequent script edits and repairs to reference them.

At final commit, only prepared assets referenced by the resulting document transfer to the live store. Failed transfer/dispatch removes assets installed by that attempt; remaining private assets are closed on disposal. Revision, session-generation and current plugin grants are checked during preparation and before transfer. Script failure/cancellation disposes the scope even if bitmap decoding is still pending; the late continuation checks abort and closes decoded output. Source bitmaps are never closed by private-scope cleanup. No source bytes, provider credentials or browser globals enter the worker. The five-second script budget remains; this change does not claim unlimited background script execution.

### Script healing on attached layers

Layer.healSpot delegates to its owning Document, capturing a validated layer identity, document-space center/radius, current selection and options before awaiting the host. DOM validation rejects detached targets, ancestor locks and use inside synchronous transactions. The host reconstructs the command prefix and independently checks layer existence/locks, then constructs a constant-pressure BrushStroke and calls prepareHealingStroke. Default sampling is current-layer; the prepared correction remains a root adjustment. Healing and patch preparation share cancellation, private asset ownership and final transfer; sequential calls can reference prior prepared assets through the reconstructed document. Neither operation changes source raster bytes.

### Automatic workspace checkpoint ownership

WorkspaceAutosave owns a sessionStorage tab identity and holds a browser Web Lock for its lifetime. If a cloned tab presents an already-held identity, it acquires a new UUID before saving. Checkpoints use independent `automatic:<uuid>` IndexedDB keys; manual `current` and named version keys are untouched. The controller coalesces notifications, serializes writes, waits for transaction completion before acknowledging success, retains dirty state on failure, and exposes an explicit retry/flush. Disposal prevents new saves and retains the writer lock through an already-started transaction. A storage/startup-restore error remains visible and cannot silently publish a blank replacement checkpoint.

Editor startup acquires identity, optionally restores its automatic checkpoint (or the manual fallback), then enables scheduling. Edits made while identity acquisition is pending are scheduled once initialized. Document/session events and viewport setters schedule checkpoints. Per-session project encoding is cached by immutable document snapshot and past/future stack identities, so changes to tab focus, selections or views reuse project blobs. Failed encodings are evicted from the cache. Startup restore validates every project before installing sessions; restored snapshots preserve content, views and the retained undo/redo window. This does not persist a complete crash-durable command log. The identity survives reload through sessionStorage; Recovery also enumerates automatic checkpoints for explicit restoration and removal after tab identity loss.

### Automatic workspace discovery and cleanup

SavedWorkspace document entries optionally include a captured name for lightweight listing; older version-1 entries retain generic numbered labels. Nested definitions recurse through the same resolution path. Expanded nodes have deterministic collision-free IDs per instance path. Expansion never mutates authored definitions, replaces original image bytes, or persists the expanded tree. ### Spatial-filter WASM worker foundation

`PixelProcessor.spatialFilter` snapshots input pixels and options before worker readiness, transfers only private bytes, and returns an independently owned RGBA buffer. This is an internal working-tile operation, not a serialized smart-filter stack or public scripting constructor. `applySpatialFilter` validates geometry and parameters, lays out aligned WASM buffers, and invokes the allocation-free `assembly/spatial-filter.ts` kernel.

Gaussian blur uses separable normalized Gaussian weights, independent horizontal/vertical sigma, finite support `ceil(3 * sigma)` and float64 intermediate premultiplied encoded-RGB/coverage values. Samples outside the supplied tile are transparent zero; edges are not renormalized. The result is unpremultiplied only at the final byte write, with RGB zeroed when rounded alpha is zero. Unsharp mask compares original encoded RGB to the unpremultiplied Gaussian result, applies amount and per-channel threshold, preserves original alpha, and leaves fully transparent source pixels unchanged. Zero blur support and zero unsharp amount return exact copies, preserving hidden RGB.

The caller must provide the full filter halo and crop it after processing; tests prove equality between whole-image and halo-tiled results, including image boundaries. Sigma is finite/nonnegative with at most 4096 halo pixels per axis; unsharp amount is 0–5 and threshold 0–255. These are internal work bounds, not document/import limits. Scratch storage consumes 32 bytes per pixel in addition to the RGBA tile and weight tables and is subject to the existing WASM memory maximum. Large-support performance is not yet evaluated. Instance stack serialization and renderer/export integration are described below; filter-mask blending is described below; the Inspector controls are described below.

Native filtered-tile signatures use the reachable component dependency closure, allowing unchanged captured-source Gaussian planes to survive unrelated retouch edits.

The internal spatial worker convention described above is unchanged. Rendering uses adaptive output tiles to bound typical native sampling footprints. Before allocating source canvases, padded native regions must fit 4,000,000 pixels and an 8192-pixel edge, keeping transient working surfaces within the WASM memory budget. These are working-tile bounds, not document/import limits. Very large cumulative radii, extreme minification and nested filters remain expensive; requests exceeding the bounds fail before canvas allocation. ### Smart-filter mask mixing foundation

`PixelProcessor.mixFiltered(original, filtered, mask, density = 1, inverted = false)` is an internal worker/WASM operation. All arrays are matching RGBA buffers, and mask alpha supplies raw coverage. Effective filter coverage is `1 - density + density * (inverted ? 1 - alpha : alpha)`, consistent with ordinary mask density conventions. It interpolates premultiplied encoded-sRGB color and alpha, then unpremultiplies; it does not preserve original alpha as adjustment-layer blending does. Exact zero/one endpoints retain the corresponding input bytes, including hidden RGB; intermediate results whose alpha rounds to zero have zero RGB. The processor snapshots every caller array before worker readiness, never detaches caller buffers, and returns a new result. Inputs are validated before WASM allocation, including finite density and matching buffer geometry. Model, constructor, rendering and persistence integration is described below. The Filter mask Inspector integration is described below.

### Retained native filter tiles

CanvasRenderer retains exact filtered RGBA and optional original copies in a separate 32 MiB, 64-entry LRU. Under memory pressure it drops original copies before evicting filtered results; a masked render reconstructs a missing original through the existing source renderer without rerunning that tile’s filters. An unmasked render needs only the retained filtered result. Keys include asset-store identity, component identity and padded native tile geometry; signatures include component definitions, filter order/settings and master dimensions. Instance filter-mask changes therefore reuse native results, while edited masters, nested dependencies and filter settings invalidate them. Cache reads and writes copy arrays so worker transfers and asynchronous renders cannot mutate retained pixels. Unlike Canvas round trips, byte retention preserves hidden RGB and alpha exactly. Cache:false bypasses reads/writes. Renderer clearing releases entries and epoch guards prevent already-processing tiles from repopulating the cleared cache. This retention budget does not limit document resolution.

### Batch observer isolation and validated generation metadata

BatchRunner and BatchRunnerService publish an independent structured clone to each event listener. ### Uniform filter-mask coverage

Before rasterizing native mask coverage, the renderer conservatively checks paint-mask base coverage, density, inversion, transformed stroke bounds and the full finite feather halo against the padded filter tile. Proven fully revealed tiles use filtered pixels directly; proven fully hidden tiles use original pixels without running filters. Unknown, non-paint or fractional coverage retains full rasterization and mixing. The optimization changes neither document resolution nor tile/cache budgets. Independent browser coverage compares against full rasterization rather than only cache bypass.

Uniform endpoints also select which retained buffers are copied: fully hidden tiles request only original pixels, and fully revealed/unmasked tiles request only filtered pixels. Fractional coverage requests both. Every returned array remains a private copy; selective reads preserve LRU refresh, signature checks and the same retained-byte budget.

Filter-mask finished composites share the existing 64 MiB Canvas LRU. Keys distinguish asset store, component, instance and padded native region; signatures include source/filter definitions, mask settings/transform and conservative paint-stroke support including feather halos. Non-paint masks retain full signatures. Raw prefix caching remains available to ordinary masks but is bypassed for filter masks to prioritize finished composites under this budget. Cache bypass disables both completed and filter-pixel retention; renderer epochs prevent stale publication after clearing.

Feather coverage processes a region of at most 1024×1024 in one job when its entire finite halo fits the existing four-million-pixel buffer budget. Larger/over-budget regions retain 512px subdivision. This prevents native filter tiles just over 512px from becoming four coverage jobs, without expanding document limits or allocation budgets. Translated Canvas brush coverage can retain the pre-existing one-level alpha difference across independently rasterized tile layouts; cache-versus-bypass output remains exact in the production fixtures.

PixelProcessor.mixFiltered captures all three caller arrays synchronously, then transfers those private snapshots to the worker. Filtered and mask snapshots are included in the transfer list, avoiding a second structured clone during dispatch. Caller buffers remain usable, including when inputs change before worker readiness; validation failures leave the processor available for subsequent requests.

The WASM filter mixer recognizes identical visible RGBA inputs as an interpolation invariant and avoids the remaining weighted color math for those pixels. Exact endpoint handling runs first to preserve hidden RGB; intermediate mixtures of two fully transparent pixels still canonicalize to transparent black. Unequal visible inputs retain the original premultiplied arithmetic.

Finished filter tiles can be drawn synchronously from CanvasCache under the compositor's current affine transform and output-tile clip. The cache exposes a draw operation, never the retained canvas, so callers cannot retain or mutate its surface. This avoids an intermediate canvas allocation/copy on hits while preserving LRU refresh. Cache-hit lookup and newly rendered tiles share validated padded geometry; context restoration runs in finally even on cache hits and rendering failures.

Painted-mask replay allocates one scratch surface for its stroke sequence. Each overlapping stroke clears the surface, saves/restores context state, applies its own clip and composites opacity exactly once. Standalone and active-stroke calls still own and release their temporary surfaces. The replay releases its scratch canvas in finally; no persistent cache or memory budget is added.

### Recipe parameter ownership and Unicode delivery names

Recipe parameter maps use own-property lookup and prototype-free dictionaries. Names such as `constructor`, `toString` and `__proto__` are ordinary data keys; inherited properties do not satisfy required parameters or override defaults. Interpolation preserves explicitly supplied keys without invoking prototype setters.

Delivery filename stems are limited to 180 UTF-8 bytes at complete Unicode scalar boundaries, with format extensions appended afterward. Lone surrogates are repaired before collision allocation, so the manifest path and encoded ZIP name agree. Collision suffixes reserve space within the same stem budget. This is a filename portability rule, not an image import limit.

Delivery ZIP exports use the shared ZIP/ZIP64 serializer through an asynchronous Blob-input path. CRC reads are bounded to 1 MiB and yield a task between chunks; empty-entry runs yield every 32 entries. The service verifies each output's full byte length and SHA-256 before retaining its immutable Blob for packaging, avoiding an array of all decoded output buffers. Optional AbortSignal checks reject cancelled work before packaging or download. The batch dialog shows verification/packing status and Cancel export; unmount aborts its export. SHA-256 still allocates one complete output buffer, and final Blob/directory assembly is synchronous: this is cooperative packaging, not a streaming archive or a proven multi-gigabyte memory guarantee.
