Schema 28 adds `LayerBlendMode`/`GROUP_BLEND_MODES`; ordinary `BLEND_MODES` remains unchanged for raster/brush/style algorithms. Native validation admits pass-through only on groups, with full fill opacity and disabled own overlay/shadow/Blend If. Legacy normal groups remain isolated after migration. Shared OO commands and REST validation use this same invariant. `CanvasRenderer` paints pass-through children against the true target backdrop. Optional opacity/mask coverage mixes before/after surfaces once using premultiplied destination-out/in plus additive composition. All temporary surfaces release in finally and cancellation checks precede publication. Backdrop-dependent tonal/patch prefix caches are disabled in that external-backdrop scope; ordinary isolated scopes retain their caches. WebGPU capability rejects visible pass-through groups and the adaptive renderer uses complete Canvas/WASM fallback.

Photoshop host export retains supported nested folder and separate pixel-mask records, recursively merging only unsupported backdrop dependencies in their true isolation scope; SVG still prepares a native prefix through pass-through groups. Direct helpers without native preparation reject richer content. Exported mask controls/linkage/off-canvas coverage, non-Normal pixel fill and styled-group internals bake; group fill folds into opacity. Document 28/project 3/workspace 2, source ownership, isolated privileges and separate REST sessions remain unchanged. See SCRIPTING_API.md for defaults, signatures, own-style restrictions, source retention and exact hierarchy/mask limits.

## Schema-29 authored pressure response

`core/pressure-curve.ts` validates monotonic normalized knots and evaluates piecewise linear response. Immutable public PressureCurve values feed optional brush metadata through existing constructors/commands; no recorded sample is replaced by its mapped output. Default/absent curves preserve existing size/alpha floors. Explicit curves permit zero, and native/SVG/GPU paths skip empty dabs before pencil rounding or allocation-sensitive stamp work. Bounds and spacing share the same mapping; finite replay grids and subpixel GPU fallback remain required. Model validation enforces field age on paint, masks/filter masks, raster erasures, tonal brushes and embedded masters, including history restoration. Valid legacy roots migrate to 29; project 3/workspace 2 stay unchanged.

Tool settings validate/copy a curve before changing state; a changed curve cancels an active gesture. The custom dialog edits only a local draft until Apply. App modal state preserves shortcut isolation and focus. Explicit curves retain finite zero/low browser pen pressure before existing smoothing; legacy normalization and mouse behavior stay unchanged. The isolated runtime registers only the pure constructor; existing host validation/grants/undo remain authoritative. See SCRIPTING_API.md for exact defaults, aliases, null-versus-DTO behavior, zero/spacing semantics, examples and limits. Physical tablet, richer dynamics and sustained/device F06/F14 acceptance remain open.


### Saved brush preference library

`brushes/presets.ts` owns immutable strict BrushPreset values, curated defaults and data-only portable packs. `brushes/library.ts` owns local IndexedDB transactions, record revisions, all-or-nothing imports, validated reloads and backup-checked recovery reset. EditorApplication owns/disposes the library; ToolController.applyBrushPreset validates before cancelling and configuring future gestures. The custom dialog selects tools through the normal UI path, preserving per-tool size memory and document paint targets. Preset state is outside document history; authored strokes still capture complete ordinary command data. Broadcast messages are reload hints, never data. No document/project/workspace version or isolated/REST privilege changes. See [BRUSH_PRESETS.md](BRUSH_PRESETS.md) for signatures, bounds, conflicts, recovery and limits.

## Authored brush tips and spherical pen tilt

`core/brush-tip.ts` owns strict tip/point schemas, pen sensor projection, inverse-linear orientation mapping and shortest-arc interpolation. `core/paint-stamps.ts` shares ellipse/rotated-pencil geometry and support/spacing across Canvas, SVG, WGSL and tool previews. Absent tips preserve the legacy native branch. Explicit zero response is skipped before pencil minimum-size rounding. Tiny/precision-sensitive GPU tips use whole-composition Canvas fallback. Cursor axes reuse the active or prospective stroke plane without commands, history or React pointer updates. Healing overlays show shaped endpoint support plus a centerline instead of claiming circular coverage.

Schema 30 admits authored tip and spherical point metadata; every brush-bearing context and embedded master checks field age outside immutable validation proofs. Valid old roots and retained history migrate without inserted tip fields; project 3/workspace 2 remain unchanged. Immutable BrushTip values participate in existing OO constructors, tonal options, script whitelist, strict REST DTOs, locks, transactions and undo. Preset/pack version 2 carries tips while legacy version 1 keeps default shape. No device verification, new script privilege, REST/browser synchronization or source-image cap is implied. See SCRIPTING_API.md for exact geometry, units, defaults, boundaries and errors.


## Self-contained affine brush symmetry

`core/brush-symmetry.ts` validates 1–31 nonidentity distinct invertible affine copies, with implicit original ink and registry-proven immutable matrix caching. Public BrushSymmetry factories create mirror/radial values; conjugation maps document-space tool preferences to layer, mask or smart-master stroke planes without replacing recorded points. Schema 31 checks all brush contexts/embedded masters/history outside cached drawing proofs; project 3/workspace 2 remain. Preset/pack 3 retains symmetry; legacy presets reset it. Runtime constructor whitelisting adds no host privilege.

The shared stamp iterator maps each copy's viewport to the original plane, merges clipped native stamp-index ranges and emits original-first/copy-array order at each dab. Full footprint bases include tip rotation/roundness/tilt and pencil pixel anchoring. Canvas/SVG consume these bases; WGSL instances carry nine floats (center, radii, alpha, full 2x2 basis), with float32 invertibility/minimum-coverage gates and complete Canvas fallback. Bounds, culling and clone source capture include every copy. Captured selection and whole-stroke opacity apply once after accumulated copy flow. Active prefix replay retains identical per-dab order. Clone samples its captured destination-relative source field for each footprint; symmetry does not mirror the source image itself. Healing/tonal coverage uses the same brush metadata and retains existing working-buffer/device limits.

The custom local-draft dialog exposes supported factory modes and preserves arbitrary valid copy data. Guides memoize settings interpretation. Hover cursors read immutable mask/master geometry and update retained SVG copy groups imperatively in a viewport-sized SVG, avoiding a document-sized cursor buffer or React updates per pointer. No source/image cap, paid call, new dependency, plugin permission or REST/browser synchronization is introduced. Full F06/F14 and physical hardware acceptance remain separate gates.

## Explicit texture source ownership — internal integration in progress

`AssetStore.shareTo` is an explicit shared-bitmap lifetime boundary. Each owner has a separate immutable asset record and copied TIFF decode choices while retaining the exact original Blob/bitmap. Per-store lease maps count live references; removing/disposal releases only that store's reference and the final release closes the bitmap. A WeakSet marks shared records so ordinary transfer/adoption cannot accidentally bypass the lease. Default sharing creates a fresh ID; explicit collisions, pending IDs, stale native geometry and disposed stores reject. Source IDs being imported are not yet shareable. Native geometry is independent of these metadata/lifetime constraints, and no worker/resample/thumbnail replaces the source. Existing unshared install adoption remains compatible. Disposed stores are terminal; cleanup still releases image ownership if metadata teardown fails.

`brushes/texture-source.ts` owns one retained texture source independently of document history. It can capture a ready source synchronously, privately decode a replacement with original TIFF choices, or ensure a collision-safe document lease synchronously. A weak per-target mapping reuses a still-owned record; ID reuse/source replacement invalidates it without overwriting foreign artwork. Invalid captures and failed imports retain current source state. Generation, abort and source-owner disposal guard pending decode publication, with old staging released without clearing a newer source. Clearing/replacing the owner cannot close textures retained by documents. ToolSettings stores only channel/inversion or null, never a portable document asset ID. The draft-based source dialog and pointer tools now use this owner; original-source portable presets are now connected and in verification. No model/project/workspace version or isolated privilege changes.

Read-only image views for isolated script repair and matting previews now take explicit leases rather than adopting borrowed source records. Script preparation shares promoted output into the document before disposing its private view; failures release staged/view references without closing live document sources. Matting preview owns/disposes both original-source leases and its private proxy bitmaps on success and validation/cancellation failure. These changes preserve existing isolated permissions and do not expose source pixels or host asset services. Recapturing an identical original source preserves the preference and existing per-document IDs instead of retaining redundant references.


## Texture tool controls and gesture capture — 2026-10-18

The custom BrushTextureDialog owns a private source draft until Apply. Owner-to-owner capture shares originals without inserting an unused document asset; Cancel, failed decode and late completion preserve the active preference. TIFF file selection inspects native pages and requires explicit precision-loss consent before decoding. Document sources retain their original TIFF choices. Coverage previews use the native worker through a private leased view, at 128 by 128 pixels only. Cursor image transforms follow the existing brush plane, tip/tilt and symmetry bases, with no React pointer updates; they show coverage proxies, not pressure/hardness/flow predictions.

ToolController captures a collision-safe document reference at the start of each brush, pencil, eraser, clone, dodge, burn, healing or painted-mask/filter-mask gesture. The captured DTO survives later preference changes. Cancellation/failure releases a newly created lease only if its exact record remains installed and current/past/future document snapshots do not reference it. Healing also releases its transient source after the native repair settles. Existing retained references survive undo/redo and project/workspace persistence. Combined dynamic preferences validate before cancelling a live gesture. Metadata-only BrushPreset capture explicitly rejects enabled texture, and legacy preset application resets texture to null. Source-bearing presets remain the next required slice; this is not complete F06/F14 acceptance.


Texture gesture continuation, queued previews and final commit also validate the captured store/record/bitmap identity. Removing or replacing the asset under the same ID cancels/rejects the stale gesture without document/history edits or deletion of the foreign replacement. This guard supplements document revision checks; asset IDs alone are not an ownership proof.


## Source-bearing brush presets — 2026-10-18, in verification

Preset/pack v4 carries image-backed coverage preferences and exact original Blob sources with native dimensions, MIME/name, SHA-256 and TIFF page/precision choices. Source-free JSON versions 1–3 remain readable/exportable. Binary packs use a checksummed 48-byte header, strict manifest and contiguous original-blob slices; readers reject missing/unused references, corrupted extents/checksums and native decode/dimension mismatches before any import commit. Portable source IDs are remapped and cannot bind to document asset IDs. The single existing IndexedDB v1 preset store now atomically stores optional source blobs alongside their preset; no physical schema migration is needed. Older strict readers reject these newer records while preserving bytes.

The library verifies actual stored source contents before writes and retains last-valid snapshots on failures. Read-only keepalive requests maintain the native write lock across asynchronous checks; only active request callbacks queue changes. Recovery v2 preserves raw records and original blobs, including invalid preset metadata, and compares complete content fingerprints under that lock before reset. Same-size byte changes and stale revisions cannot be erased with an old backup. Legacy JSON recovery remains available for source-free records; unsupported raw non-JSON values still fail without deleting data.

The custom preset dialog connects source-aware save/update/rename/duplicate/delete/import/export/download/recovery and shows source name/dimensions/coverage. Applying privately verifies/decodes an original, guards abort/supersession/document/tool/source changes, then uses normal tool selection/configuration; errors retain prior ready preferences and newer human edits. Preferences stay outside document undo; actual strokes still use shared OO commands/history and collision-safe document leases. Original images stay independent of viewport/cursor proxies, library deletion and closed source documents. This adds no isolated script/plugin file privilege, paid provider, upload, REST/browser sync or document schema bump. See [BRUSH_PRESETS.md](BRUSH_PRESETS.md) for signatures, binary contract, errors and limits. Complete native/production verification and wider F06/F14/device gates remain open.


### Bounded texture batches and partial readback

`BrushTextureSampler.prepareAffineBatch` validates and owns up to 64 affine samples with at most 1,000,000 total full-projection pixels. It batches actual WASM channel conversion while preserving individual native rasterization. Its optional fifth argument supplies one integer, positive, in-bounds readback rectangle per sample. These rectangles reduce captured/transferred bytes only: each original bitmap still projects onto the unchanged full canvas before readback. A bounded private canvas pool is reused synchronously after each owned ImageData capture and released before worker waits. Cache keys include complete projection settings and the readback rectangle. Caller outputs stay independent; any failed conversion releases every unpublished output. Original image dimensions and bytes are not constrained by these working budgets.

Raw texture replay may omit unchanged pixels only under the proven full-flow, binary-RGB source-over certificate. Accepted full-pressure inputs remain eligible even with pressure opacity enabled; fractional flow, changing pressure and non-binary pigments use full replay. Conservative alpha bounds and non-opaque rectangles remain valid as raw alpha increases. Readback intersects that rectangle with the existing dab support, while exact integer pencil mattes may use the smaller rectangle directly. Prepared alpha ceilings are captured from owned converted bytes. Saturated fast paths still share cooperative cancellation checkpoints and private-prefix publication; the complete accepted sample sequence stays in the model. Arbitrarily extreme native bitmap transforms can still lose visible samples in the browser rasterizer; this known limitation is not a geometry/import cap or a completed fidelity claim.

Canonical integer-native frequency compositions recognized by `frequencyIdentitySource` may use 512-pixel composition cores. Eligibility includes the inner Gaussian sampling halo in the existing 4 MP/8192-edge working budget. Affine/fractional placements, altered compositions and unsafe halos retain the established 256-pixel grid. Exact-pixel equivalence and responsive export remain distinct verification gates.


### Literal native raster frequency-band sampling

`nativeFrequencyRasterSource` recognizes a single full-frame raster at native bitmap dimensions, with neutral placement/opacity/blending and no source mask, effects or erasures. This is an internal read-only eligibility query. An integer unit-native frequency-band instance over that source, without a filter mask, may use a 1024-pixel sampling core to absorb composition overscan. Both1024 and512 preferences include the actual Gaussian halo plus four overscan pixels in the existing4MP/8192-edge working budget; unsafe halos retain the established512/256 fallbacks. Source appearance, multiple/non-raster children, resampling, affine/fractional instance placement and filter masks retain their current sampling grid. Canonical composition cores remain512. No public model/API/schema, original-source or history/isolation change is introduced. This reduces sampling requests; it does not imply instant full-frame export or complete F14 performance.


### Complete native footprints and canonical Canvas cells

`engine/native-canvas-grid.ts` retains complete projected raster/bitmap-mask/vector footprints when their document-anchored working rectangle, including gutters, fits the existing4MP/8192-edge budget. Larger footprints use full256-pixel native cells with two-pixel gutters. Requests copy their visible portions after rasterization; an export strip does not retessellate a curve or refilter a clipped image quad. Raster drawing preserves its five-argument image geometry. Exact integer native raster/bitmap placement keeps its original fast path, and extreme bitmap coordinates retain the bounded double-precision sampler. Native image smoothing preferences follow the caller. Working vector footprints follow resolved join geometry when it is well-conditioned; otherwise they keep the previous conservative hull. Authored miter limits and public geometry queries are untouched. Only temporary allocation bounds are selected; original geometry, dimensions and blobs remain unchanged.

Resampled smart instances prepare complete document-aligned output cells and project their sampled images through canonical cells as well. Cumulative spatial-filter halos, overscan and rounding remain inside the established4MP native allocation check; unsafe large cells reduce their preferred core before allocation. Native frequency grids retain their existing eligibility and partitions. Private surfaces release in finally, and existing asset identity/lifetime, cancellation, cache publication, OO history and script/plugin isolation rules remain authoritative. No persistent schema or public constructor/API changes. Crop/export consistency is functional correctness, not an input-latency, physical-display or process-memory guarantee.

Resolved vector tangents are memoized separately per contour and direction for one footprint query. Coincident-segment chains share the nearest resolved tangent; empty cycles and uncertain tangents are cached too. Each segment is inspected at most once in each direction, retaining linear coordinate work and temporary storage through the existing20,000-anchor path budget. The same tangent arithmetic, conservative uncertainty fallback and authored geometry remain authoritative. No cache persists across snapshots.


### Native spatial-filter transparent support

`assembly/spatial-filter.ts` trims only zero-alpha leading/trailing samples from each horizontal row and globally empty source rows from the vertical pass. Horizontal filtering cannot move coverage between rows. Every skipped contribution is positive zero; retained taps keep their original order, normalized Float64 weights, premultiplication, Float64 scratch, rounding and output traversal. Hidden transparent RGB does not become visible. Unsharp still preserves source alpha/hidden RGB, while frequency planes retain their opaque low/high/correction rules. Dense inputs keep full support. The function signature, scratch layout, worker ownership/result validation and4MP/8192-edge native job budgets are unchanged; no new allocation, source resize or import limit is introduced. This removes wasted convolution over transparent margins, not the general cost of a large dense Gaussian.


### Adjacent native spatial outputs

The scalar spatial kernel processes horizontal and vertical output pixels in pairs. Horizontal neighboring support intervals differ by at most one sample at each edge: the leading tap belongs to the first output, common source RGBA/alpha normalization serves both independent weighted accumulators, and the trailing tap belongs to the second. Each output retains ascending tap order and its original Float64 multiplications/additions. The vertical pass shares weight/address preparation and reads adjacent scratch pixels together. A scalar tail handles every odd final column, including one-pixel rows. The inline pixel writer retains existing Gaussian/unsharp/frequency rounding, alpha, hidden-RGB and threshold rules; returning from an invisible unsharp pixel never skips its neighbor.

The scratch layout remains four Float64 channels per pixel, with no new memory, module feature, worker/ABI, public constructor, format or mutation/history contract. No SIMD variant is shipped: isolated SIMD experiments did not produce a useful dense-kernel gain. Source geometry, all taps and original blobs remain intact; this is exact sample/load reuse, not approximate convolution or source downsampling.

# Implementation roadmap and planning record

### 2026-10-18 — F06 mixer/smudge native paint dependency in verification

Owner: implementation agent. Estimate: L within T16/F06. The intervening architecture answer was read-only and counts as no implementation progress. This continuation revalidated the portable-preset release/source baseline and resumed mixer/smudge implementation without reducing the original professional-editor objective.

Strict internal settings and actual-WASM kernels now load finite pigment and mix native destination/carried premultiplied RGBA, including alpha transport. Float32 reservoirs retain sub-byte pickup; pickup reads pre-deposit pixels and zero flow/coverage remains inert. The existing pixel worker captures all inputs before readiness, transfers private copies and validates returned extents/channels. Independent equations cover all256 source-alpha values against all256 coverage values, finite loaded-paint exhaustion, transparency lifting/deposition, tile partition identity, separate whole-stroke opacity/selection and memory/ownership/error boundaries. Initial focused tests pass; complete build/unit/browser/normal-production verification is pending.

This is an internal dependency of the real intended tool, not an alternative reduced completion target. Still required: spatial carried-pigment replay across the complete stroke, native dependency capture independent of viewport cropping, ordered replacement for paint/raster transparency, shared authored OO commands/history/assets, persistence, actual tools/controls/presets/cursors, preview/cancel and native/SVG/GPU/automation integration. No new public constructor, document schema, isolated host privilege, provider call, upload or arbitrary source-image limit is introduced. Physical tablets/hardware/display, sustained F14/process memory and every other unfinished roadmap family remain open.

Date: 2026-09-21. Status: planning deliverable completed and audited; implementation is active. See the dated progress record below for delivered slices and outstanding scope. Read [strategy/catalog](FEATURE_STRATEGY.md), [AI specifications](AI_FEATURE_SPECS.md) and [competitive evidence](COMPETITIVE_RESEARCH.md) together. This roadmap preserves the broad professional-editor ambition while sequencing work into independently testable releases.

## Delivery rules

- Implement vertical workflows, not disconnected demo buttons. A tool is done only when UI, commands/DOM, persistence, rendering/export, keyboard access, errors and relevant automation surfaces agree.
- Keep source assets immutable and no arbitrary MP import caps. Working budgets may constrain previews/jobs; format/device failures must be explicit.
- Plan changes do not implement APIs. Current references describe current behavior; proposed constructors/routes live only in the planning specs until shipped.
- Do not silently expand paid operations, cloud transfers or plugin permissions. No provider contract, account, payment, credential or external message was created by this planning task.
- Before implementation, inspect the latest worktree and update the baseline. Assign an owner and estimate the chosen ticket; phase membership is not a promise to ship every row at once.
- Each phase requires the prior relevant gates, not every unrelated feature in a prior phase. Metadata can ship before masks; standalone generation can ship before generative fill; neither may imply unimplemented mask/color/interchange support.

## First six months: capacity envelope, not a parity deadline

Assume 26 weeks at 10–20 hours/week = 260–520 gross hours. Reserve about 25% for user research, testing, support, documentation and deployment uncertainty, leaving approximately 195–390 implementation hours. Replace these assumptions with measured throughput after two slices.

- **First 2 weeks:** T01 subset, user task interviews and a small import/metadata fixture corpus. Decide one first customer workflow and define baseline measurements. No audience/contact list is assumed.
- **Next 4–8 weeks:** T04/T05 vertical slice with explicit schema changes, plus a bounded T02/T03 durability slice. If reliable persistence needs more time, reduce the release surface rather than claiming autosave works.
- **Next 4–8 weeks:** finish reliability blockers and choose either T06 manual mask foundation or the simplest standalone A03 candidate prototype. Do not implement a full transform rewrite and production cloud infrastructure simultaneously at the low end of the time budget.
- **Remaining capacity:** complete and evaluate the chosen slice, close failures, and conduct paid-use discovery. At higher demonstrated throughput, follow with provider evaluation/T11/T12; at lower throughput, deliver a reliable local metadata/editor milestone and carry the entire AI plan forward.

This envelope intentionally does not promise a complete AI suite or Photoshop replacement in six months. The long-term portfolio remains in scope. If the founder wants substantially faster breadth, revise time/capital/team assumptions explicitly; do not hide that cost in “AI will build it.”

## Acceptance gates by layer

| Gate              | Required proof before release                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Document contract | Constructor/command validation, locks/ownership, migration, transaction rollback, undo/redo and asset lifetime. No double commits on retry.                             |
| Render contract   | Mask/transform/effect reference fixtures, alpha edges, tile seams, source-size output and backend-specific tolerance; test hardware GPU separately from software tests. |
| Durability        | Forced termination, corrupt manifest/tail, disk quota, multi-tab conflict, interrupted save and reopen with original bytes. Never call browser storage a backup.        |
| AI control flow   | Consented input scope, budget reservation, rate limits, timeout/cancel/late result, idempotency, failed-charge reconciliation and revision mismatch.                    |
| AI quality        | Real held-out outputs and human task review; provider stubs alone do not count. Model changes require evaluation reruns.                                                |
| Metadata          | Extraction fixtures, origin labels, edits/review round-trip, exact export policy and injection-like strings treated as data.                                            |
| Interoperability  | Import/export a published supported subset in independent tools; errors include unsupported constructs. Do not silently flatten.                                        |
| UX/accessibility  | Keyboard and pointer task completion, progress/cancel, recoverable error states, light/dark contrast, no hidden essential actions.                                      |
| Automation        | UI, OOP/scripting and REST use the same valid operations; surface-specific asynchronous/asset limitations are explicit; plugin capabilities enforced by host.           |
| Commercial        | Repeat paid demand, cost-per-accepted-output measurements, bounded variable cost, visible usage and tested retention/deletion.                                          |

Initial proposed performance targets, to calibrate with T01: input-to-visible-stroke p95 ≤33 ms on a named reference desktop at a normal viewport; no routine gesture-related main-thread task >50 ms; metadata extraction runs off-thread; progress is shown for long work; local cancellation stops new work within 250 ms. Large-document load/export uses measured time/memory curves, not one universal promise. Provider latency is measured and reported separately. Hardware and corpus must be named for every performance claim; if a target fails, log the failure and remediate before advertising it.

## Commercial validation without replacing the product objective

Recruit five designers/image-production users through direct discovery (no outreach was sent in this task). Observe repeated tasks and existing artifacts with permission. Ask them to complete metadata cleanup, asset placement/protected edits and variant delivery, then repeat with their current editor. Test whether they return and will pay; willingness-to-pay interviews alone are weak evidence.

The $30K MRR goal remains business revenue, not personal income. Illustrative arithmetic only: 1,000 customers × $30/month, 500 × $60, or 200 teams × $150 each reaches $30K gross recurring revenue before credits, fees, churn and costs. These are not proposed final prices or evidence of demand. Do not depend on unlimited paid inference. Track activated/repeat users, paid conversion, retention, accepted-output cost, support hours and document-loss incidents. Prefer a smaller validated production workflow over an unsupported marketing claim of universal parity, while continuing the breadth roadmap.

## Risks and mitigation checkpoints

| Risk                                                                   | Mitigation / evidence required                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Foundation work overwhelms founder capacity                            | Split XL tickets, review actual throughput each slice, maintain scope transparently; no calendar claim without staffing assumptions. |
| AI changes protected labels, artwork or geometry                       | Enforce masks/composite checks, expose reference comparison, block incompatible transforms; retain source and manual correction.     |
| Expensive rejected generations or accidental retries                   | Reservation ledger, idempotency, capped attempts and cost-per-accepted-result evaluation before pricing.                             |
| Large assets exceed browser memory or storage quota                    | Streaming/disk-backed architecture, operation cancellation, quota recovery and device fixtures; no hidden source downsampling.       |
| Metadata/OCR suggestions are wrong or expose private fields            | Origin/review state, abstention, privacy export profiles and malicious/multilingual fixtures; no inferred ownership guarantees.      |
| Proprietary formats, fonts, codecs or model licenses limit deployment  | Explicit supported subsets and dependency/license review at T09/T10/T17; independent round-trip testing before claims.               |
| Provider/model updates change outputs or availability                  | Adapter capability checks, versioned evaluations, retained output bytes, useful local workflows and no silent provider switching.    |
| Collaboration/API/plugin expansion introduces data or credential leaks | Separate authenticated services, scoped capabilities, durable ownership and a dedicated security review before hosted rollout.       |

# Performance benchmark harness

## Native frequency tiling — exact band requests, measured full-frame reduction

Unit-native frequency-band planes with safe integer placement now use a 512-pixel tile cap when the worst-case padded footprint fits the existing 4 MP/8192-edge budget. They cover the outer composition tile plus overscan without a tiny extra request. Affine/fractional placement, unsafe halos, composition tiles and retouch canvas regions retain their prior grids. This changes no original resolution, persistent/public model, API, source bytes or undo semantics.

Fourteen frozen-renderer/candidate PNG pairs are exact across low/high/correction, zero radius, alpha, filter masks/inversion, affine/fractional placement, disabled filters and soft low/high/both retouch. New browser tests compare equivalent disabled-filter documents at 256/512 seams under native, affine, fractional and tone/mask appearances. A large-halo test captures matching actual canvas/input geometry before intentionally skipping its expensive kernel; full radius-280 output/performance is not claimed.

Three clean alternating unprofiled pairs on Linux, AMD Ryzen 9 3900X and Chromium 153.0.8010.12 export the same opaque 10,000×5,000 scene with sigma 2 and a full-frame low-band green retouch. Median export decreases **40,316.5 → 34,662.6 ms (14.0%)**. Every run drops Gaussian requests **6,241 → 3,160** and sampled Gaussian pixels **75,169,920 → 71,064,000**. Independent Pillow decoding hashes every RGBA byte in all six PNGs: they match each other and differ from the original. All document snapshots and source hashes remain unchanged. No build/tests ran during the pairs; external host activity remains uncontrolled.

Six injected 75 ms positive controls are observed; no overlapping native long task is reported during exports. Per-run animation callback p95 is about 19.3 ms for reference and 19.7–20.0 ms for candidate; maximum gaps range 40.6–63.1 ms and 45.3–48.0 ms respectively. These are headless scheduling proxies, not physical presentation, tool input-to-visible latency, sustained/hardware/tablet or general 60fps acceptance. Full-frame export still takes roughly 35 seconds; peak process/source bitmap memory remains unmeasured.

An excluded variant also enlarged native composition regions. It changed three/four soft-brush edge pixels in three retouch cases, at clipping boundaries: alpha is unchanged, straight RGB differs by up to four bytes and premultiplied RGB by up to two. It was not applied. This exposes a separate ordinary-brush crop-invariance investigation; fixed vector-mask grids already address an analogous coverage issue. No pixel tolerance was relaxed to accept the band-only change.

The main build, all **1,381 unit/API cases in 171 files**, **60 affected native cases**, and all **84 normal-production workflows** pass. The new source branch also passed all 24 isolated feature/interchange checks. Initial harness warm-up/type-annotation/path issues and the first Vite-optimization reload are retained separately from accepted results. [Sealed source, native PNGs, rejected comparison, raw timing/check reports and reconstruction](benchmarks/frequency-native-tiling-2026-10-19.json) preserve all 34 earlier artifacts. # Canoli Studio editor requirements

## Bitmap projection precision

Large affine bitmap placements must retain native pixels and representable source geometry in raster layers, bitmap masks, textures, native wet reconstruction and filtered projections. Keep the existing Canvas path at ordinary placements; use double-precision sampling when projected coordinates cannot reliably retain subpixel geometry. Axis-aligned image edges retain the established half-pixel tie rule; sheared image edges use actual pixel area. Nearest and encoded-sRGB premultiplied-byte bilinear sampling must use the unchanged original bitmap, with bounded native reads and no source-size intermediate.

Gathering must yield for cancellation and queued UI tasks. A texture batch may have only one numerical native reader active at a time; complete all captures before the existing validated worker conversion. Abort, source replacement/closure, clear and disposal must reject private results and prevent late conversion/publication. Cache retirement alone preserves independent readers. Capture mutable native canvases once and close private bitmap snapshots on success or rejection; never close borrowed original bitmaps. Mask retention distinguishes bitmap identities/dimensions. Verify mirrored/fractional/affine pixels, real oversized textured strokes, native 50 MP source/project preservation, software-GPU parity, full-batch event-loop turns and real production script/undo/reopen behavior. Working budgets are independent of original resolution. This does not establish general latency, process memory, physical-device or complete F14 acceptance.

## Ordinary paint crop consistency

Untextured brush, pencil, eraser and clone coverage, fills, ordinary masks and filter masks must retain exact pixels across crops on the same output-pixel lattice and between cold/incremental replay. Preserve complete authored geometry when projected footprints exceed scratch budgets; do not cap or downsample source geometry. Numerical work must yield across long runs of accelerated stamps, reject superseded/resized presentation, own mutable accepted input and keep cancelled extensions private. Mask cache budgets include retained native padding and changing reservations at existing keys.

Verify exact affine/scale/seam pixels, real oversized edits, source-coordinate precision, mutable-prefix invalidation, cancellation/input responsiveness and observed owned Canvas allocations. Existing source/history/project, 50 MP, export and supported-GPU tests remain required. Canonical antialiasing can change edge pixels relative to the former crop-sensitive renderer without changing authored data or persistent formats. Textured/wet crop stability, representative quality, sustained/editor-wide latency, hardware/tablet and process-memory acceptance remain open.

Include non-binary fractional zooms and numerical/native vector coverage in lattice tests. Cache resets must not cancel independent direct mask reads; simultaneous readers at the same cache key retain their own exact results, and retiring an in-flight owner releases its buffers after the current read completes. Explicit caller cancellation remains authoritative.

## F05 live frequency preview and shared controls — functionally verified

Prepare a full neutral native source privately once per dialog. Show actual low/detail native crops with original alpha, original comparison and pointer/keyboard panning; changing radius must show the latest actual worker result without queuing every intermediate slider value. Closing/cancel/Escape must release private resources and leave document/history/assets untouched. Create reuses that original-resolution capture and commits once. No fabricated progress, viewport downsampling of originals or new import cap.

Use one editable group radius for low/high/correction planes while preserving protected child locks, fallback records and retouch strokes. Exact fields and slider previews must support Escape and one undo; controller/ancestor locks and stale targets reject. Scripts and REST use the same schema 37 group property/commands. Native component boundaries retain independent scope; conversion, rasterization, copy and Photoshop planes must preserve effective settings. Project/workspace restoration, radius-patch recipe replay, actual native preview pixels, concurrency/ownership and 50 MP workflows are functionally verified; native capture creation is not a new recipe action. Full F05/F14 and the rest of the original roadmap remain active.

Exact unit-native integer frequency placements may combine rectangular sampling requests when their count falls without increasing estimated halo work. Recognized unchanged native-raster bands and native compositions prefer halo-inclusive jobs up to 1,000,000 pixels and 8192 working edges; the established 256/512/1024 grids and 4 MP allocation checks remain fallbacks. Affine/fractional placements, masks and complex masters retain their existing eligibility rules. Linear Light/Burn independently rasterized work retains its 1,048,576-pixel job budget while adapting to narrow strips. Cancellation must reject after the active job without publishing output or changing history. Original source dimensions/bytes, commands and persistent formats remain unchanged. Verify complete RGBA across native/retouched/transparent/masked scenes, large halos and real 50 MP exports. These bounds do not cap source geometry or establish full F14 acceptance.

## F05 frequency separation — native functional verification

Provide manual frequency separation from an unlocked raster via command search and canvas context menu. Preserve the original source layer/assets; privately capture full native neutral pixels (including expanded active wet ink), then create editable low/high bands, independent retouch paint layers, a protected precision-correction layer and source-alpha mask in one undo step. Preserve affine placement, tone, ordinary raster erasures, masks and appearance. Preparation must cancel or reject stale document/revision/selection/assets without partial edits or leaked output assets. Radius uses original pixels and paired exact/slider controls; no new rail tool/default key binding.

Schema-36 OO values, isolated constructor scripts and separate REST prepared-data commands must share validation, phase ordering, locks, source references and history. Verify actual WASM exhaustive RGB8 reconstruction, projected alpha/tone/masks, Edit contents retouch/apply, native/interchange output, project/workspace restoration and original 50 MP dimensions/bytes without a source-resolution cap. Functional evidence does not prove portrait-quality evaluation, full F05, physical devices or sustained 60fps. Live preview and coupled controls follow the verified contract above. Those requirements and the full roadmap remain active.

Current functional evidence: build and 1,373 unit/API cases across169files pass. All ten final native feature cases pass after correcting the independent unlinked-mask oracle to retain outside-frame coverage;147 other native regression cases pass. Evidence includes real retouch/apply, source-race rejection, isolated documented recipe, strict REST/history, actual65536-pair WASM reconstruction,15 focused WGSL scenarios, native/SVG/PSD pixels, 50MP capture/full PNG and exact source/project reopening. The separately pinned production release passes 83 existing workflows and the final frequency workflow without developer globals. The original failed oracle remains recorded; its strict pixel tolerance was not widened.

## Manual red-eye correction — functional verification

F05 includes selection-scoped non-destructive red-eye correction. Users select pupils and create a Red Eye adjustment through command search or the canvas menu. Creation must capture an editable mask in one undo step; absent selections fail without edits. Threshold (0–255, default 32) and Strength (0–100%, default 100) pair sliders with exact inputs and support preview, Escape, reset, locks and undo. Original pixels remain intact. Constructor scripting and REST share strict validation/history; schema-35 restoration and embedded masters reject old labels. Verify actual WASM, WGSL alpha/boundary equivalence, mask placement under affine parents, source hashes/project reopen, native export, and 50 MP geometry. The defined red-dominance rule is documented in SCRIPTING_API.md; this does not establish automatic eye detection, evaluated portrait quality, complete F05 or 60fps.

Verified in this slice: 1,363 unit/API cases, 38 focused browser regressions and seven final feature cases, including a full native 50 MP PNG export and source-hash/project round-trip. The 120 actual-WGSL comparisons use Chromium software WebGPU: maximum premultiplied RGB difference one byte, zero alpha mismatches. Physical GPU/tablet performance and portrait-quality evaluation remain open.

## Prepared wet prefix ownership and cadence — functional acceptance; latency open

Reuse prepared output only for a matching same-session native epoch. Rebuild changed cells, omit cells restored to original pixels, validate full candidates and keep snapshots/frames independently owned. Cached output leases share actual bitmap/Blob objects; earlier owned frames survive replacement, job disposal and later decode failure. Storage/source/decoded-pixel invalidation must reject before publication even when a fast path reads no pixels. Final commit preserves exact preview pixels and one undo without redundant output decoding. Wet previews retain one preparation start per owner/frame boundary, with no fresh wait after the previous boundary elapsed. Source geometry and extension permissions remain unchanged.

The isolated build/all 1,354 unit/API/65 native/82 production workflows pass. Continuous-pointer timing remains mixed and above33 ms. Separate release-to-History/final-canvas medians improve across six fixtures, with exact project/pixel/undo audits; actual main build/unit/native checks pass and all 51 non-documentation release resources match the isolated 82-workflow production runtime. See [prefix evidence](benchmarks/brush-wet-prefix-reuse-2026-10-18.json). Full F06/T16/F14, sustained/device/process-memory and every other unfinished original-roadmap requirement remain active.

## Resident wet cache — functional acceptance; input latency remains open

Transient wet epochs may remain in the existing bounded private cache. Dirty evictions persist atomically; referenced originals/results flush before finish transfers ownership. Completed prefixes remain independent, and quota/cancellation/source/storage failures publish no document, history or assets. Native uncached, evicted and resident paths preserve exact pixels and original source resolution; custom/used/modified stores retain write-through behavior.

Actual main build, all 1,352 unit/API and 56 native cases pass. The byte-identical non-documentation release passes all 82 production workflows. Three clean alternating pairs retain 720 matching-point samples, 36 native task controls and exact 108-PNG/108-project audits. [sealed evidence](benchmarks/brush-wet-resident-cache-2026-10-18.json) records 32.6–46.2% lower local median per-run p95, but all six fixtures remain at 88.1–119.7 ms, above the 33 ms target. Full F06/F14, sustained/device/process-memory and every other unfinished original-roadmap requirement remain open.

## Wet mask coverage — functional acceptance; performance gates open

Smudge/Mixer support ordinary and smart-filter mask targets through the same private retained job. Preserve selection/vector/bitmap/base geometry, ordered Hide/Reveal/Wet refinements and complete linked/unlinked/basis/native-master transforms. Capture neutral coverage before enabled/inverted/density/feather settings; Hide/Reveal controls initially loaded alpha and RGB is ignored. Immutable LayerMask.applyWetPaint and strict schema34 DTOs share commands/history, native alpha validation and asset persistence with isolated scripts and separate REST sessions. The [sealed functional baseline](benchmarks/brush-wet-masks-2026-10-18.json) records the actual build,1,352unit/API cases,595native cases across54files and82production workflows without accepted retries/skips/flakes. Coverage includes SVG/project and layered/flattened PSD pixels, real filter strength, pointer cancellation/undo/late-sample drain, isolated rollback, original50MP bitmap-mask bytes/dimensions and observed working canvases, affine crop partitions and actual software-WGSL parity/cache/undo. FullF06/F14, sustained usage, physical devices and process-memory gates remain open.

Numerical support/halo cropping and grouped private backing writes have functional acceptance. Actual head build,1,352unit/API,50native and82production cases pass, with exact PNG/project/point/undo audits and three clean paired timing runs. [Sealed evidence](benchmarks/brush-wet-gesture-performance-2026-10-18.json) records lower observed latency, but all six fixtures remain above33ms; sustained/device/process-memory and fullF06/F14 gates stay open. These changes preserve all source, public scripting, command/history and isolation contracts.


## Wet pointer tools — integration in verification

Smudge and Mixer brush now accept real pointer samples on paint/image layers, including transformed layers, selection clips, pressure curves, tip/tilt, symmetry and retained original texture sources. They keep separate normalized Initial foreground load / Wetness / Pickup preferences (Smudge 0/0/0.5; Mixer 1/0.25/0.5). Ordinary brush flow multiplies the wet operation once. These are finite encoded-sRGB pigment transport controls, not a spectral or physical-fluid simulation.

Native completed prefixes preview outside document history and the host AssetStore. Pointer release processes every accepted sample and commits one shared OO transaction. Escape, pointer cancellation, changed source/revision, tool changes and disposal reject stale work and release private resources. A render lease keeps retired prefix pixels alive until preparation completes. A no-op adds no history. Wet presets use data version 5, retain both mode preferences and original texture bytes; legacy presets restore default wet preferences. Layer publication acceptance is recorded in [wet-tool evidence](benchmarks/brush-wet-tools-2026-10-18.json); mask coverage extends this path as described above. The mask extension and sustained input-to-visible/device gates still require their own complete acceptance. No F06/F14 completion claim.


Schema-33 authored wet replacement is in verification: prepared OO values and trusted native preparation connect ordered paint/raster operations, unchanged original sources, shared validation/history, source references, native fallback rendering and SVG prefixes. Acceptance requires browser alpha/order/appearance/resize/cancel/persistence/script/50MP coverage and production checks. Mixer/smudge F06/T16 remains open: actual tools/controls/cursors/presets, incremental previews, mask/filter-mask planes and existing performance/device gates are still required.

Status: local editor foundation and rich tool milestone implemented; verification and limitations below. This document separates requested requirements from implementation decisions and future work.

Wet paint has a sealed schema-33 prepared-authoring baseline with ordered native replacements, shared validation/history, persisted source/result assets and native/SVG/automation publication. Retained internal append/snapshot workspaces and inert-record corrections are now in verification. The numerical engine transports premultiplied color/alpha with independent spatial reservoirs and whole-stroke selection/opacity. It remains a dependency of the unfinished interactive mixer/smudge workflow: actual tools, controls/cursors/presets, preview resource ownership/cancel, mask/filter-mask/master targets and existing sustained-performance/tablet/device gates remain required. Numerical/functional tests do not establish complete F06/T16/F14 acceptance or60fps.

## Product context

The owner is a full-stack engineer with image-processing and home-decor experience. The broader business target is $30,000+ in monthly recurring revenue, with little initial capital and low ongoing maintenance. Available development time is 10–20 hours per week. The current product direction is a browser-based AI-native photo editor, beginning with a small editing foundation. Business viability, pricing, and customer demand have not been validated.

## Confirmed requirements

| ID  | Requirement                              | Acceptance                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --- | ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| R1  | Browser-based application                | Runs in a modern desktop browser with no desktop installation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| R2  | Use WebAssembly                          | At least one real image operation executes in a compiled WASM module.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| R3  | Start bare-bones; preserve extensibility | Document model, UI, rendering, image processing, and persistence have separate boundaries.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| R4  | Photoshop-inspired document object model | Documents own ordered layers; groups own child layers; image layers refer to source assets and adjustments. This is not a claim of Photoshop API/file compatibility.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| R5  | Object-oriented design                   | Public DOM objects use constructors and methods/properties. The application uses the same DOM API intended for future integrations.                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| R6  | Public API uses DOM constructors         | `new Document`, `new RasterLayer`, `new LayerGroup`, `new TextLayer`, and `new ToneAdjustment` work today; attached mutations are validated and undoable.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| R7  | Keyboard shortcuts from the start        | A central registry drives shortcut handling and discoverable help; text entry is protected.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| R8  | Document requirements                    | This file records scope, acceptance criteria, decisions, limitations, and open questions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| R9  | Product brief for future agents          | The application objective, intended experience, constraints, and unvalidated decisions are recorded in `PRODUCT_BRIEF.md`; `AGENTS.md` links the documents.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| R10 | Distinct custom design system            | Professional, modern visual language appealing to artists/designers, with reusable components and tokens. No shadcn. See `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| R11 | REST API                                 | Local versioned document creation/query/commands/history endpoint, Bearer/X-API-Key authentication, binary asset management, asynchronous generation jobs and polling, and atomic candidate application with revision conflict checks and single-transaction undo/redo.                                                                                     |
| R12 | Scripting API                            | Users run custom JavaScript with DOM constructors from a Scripts panel; versioned host scripting bridge for non-blocking asynchronous jobs and asset inspection without sandbox credentials; successful edits apply atomically with shared undo. Constructor/member reference and runnable examples are maintained in [SCRIPTING_API.md](SCRIPTING_API.md). |
| R13 | Preserve high-resolution images          | No fixed MP, image-file-size or dimension cutoff; keep original dimensions/data, separate working-buffer budgets, test 50 MP end to end. Browser/device constraints must be reported honestly.                                                                                                                                                              |

## Plugin extensions

R14: Support plugins/extensions. The implementation installs versioned JSON packages (apiVersion 1 and 2) with named JavaScript commands, fine-grained capability permissions (`document:read`, `document:write`, `jobs:run`, `ai:generate`, `assets:read`, `assets:write`, `assets:analyze`), source review, interactive UI permission grant/revocation, local browser persistence, export/update/remove actions and sandboxed execution. Each successful editing command shares the DOM and one history entry, and revoked permissions are strictly rejected at the host boundary. See [PLUGINS.md](PLUGINS.md) for the current contract and future extension boundaries. Plugin UI panels, network capabilities, background hooks and a marketplace are not part of this first slice.

## First usable slice

| ID  | Capability                  | Acceptance                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| M1  | Import images               | PNG, JPEG, and WebP files become image layers, with clear validation errors.                                                                                                   |
| M2  | Layer editing               | Select, rename, show/hide, lock, duplicate, delete, reorder, group, and change opacity/blend mode.                                                                             |
| M3  | Canvas navigation           | Zoom, fit, hand pan, temporary Space pan, and drag an unlocked layer.                                                                                                          |
| M4  | Non-destructive adjustments | Exposure, contrast, and saturation are stored on the layer; original source pixels remain unchanged.                                                                           |
| M5  | Undo/redo                   | UI and constructor-API changes share one history; a transaction is one undo entry; invalid transactions roll back. A continuous drag/slider gesture creates one history entry. |
| M6  | Portable project files      | Save/open versioned `.luma` binary container containing document data and original image blobs; import legacy JSON; reopen reproduces the composition.                         |
| M7  | Export                      | PNG uses the same compositing path as the editor, without selection outlines or viewport zoom.                                                                                 |
| M8  | Local operation             | Browser editing requires no server backend, account, paid API, or image upload to an external service. The REST service is optional.                                           |
| M9  | Responsive processing       | WASM pixel loops run in a Web Worker; stale preview results cannot replace a newer document revision.                                                                          |

## Rich tools milestone

See [TOOLS_MILESTONE.md](TOOLS_MILESTONE.md) for the acceptance audit. Brush, pencil, clone, Bézier pen and rectangle/ellipse marquee use the shared command/history model. Drag layer rows above/below siblings, into the center of groups, or onto the document-root drop target. Reparenting via the UI preserves document position; dragging a selected group on canvas moves its children together.

Brush controls include color, size, hardness and opacity; pointer pressure changes stamp size. Pencil uses hard pixel-aligned marks. Clone uses Alt/Option-click to set a source, previews sampled pixels while drawing, persists source tiles on release, and supports aligned sampling. Drawing over an image creates a separate paint layer. Vector paths have editable anchors/handles, fill/stroke, close and finish actions. Marquee supports replace/add/subtract/intersect and constrains paint, clone, fill and clear operations. Layer properties include fill opacity, 18 blend modes, color overlay, drop shadow and source/underlying Blend If ranges with four endpoints each, in luminance/R/G/B.

The Developer docs link in both the rail and Scripts panel opens generated, locally served documentation; these pages are included in production builds. Scripts and REST commands represent every new document primitive; REST still has no asset/rendering service.

## Tool adjustment controls

R15: Every bounded numeric tool adjustment pairs a reusable slider with an adjacent exact number input. Brush/pencil/clone diameter and opacity, brush/clone hardness, and pen width support both methods, with equivalent bounds and synchronized values. Use the same paired control for path widths and bounded inspector adjustments. Inputs accept precise fractions; invalid/empty values revert. Sliders support keyboard steps/endpoints, live preview, cancellation, and one committed undo entry for document changes. Both inputs respect disabled/locked state. Tool settings remain outside document history. The bar must keep the controls accessible at narrower desktop widths. See [DESIGN_SYSTEM.md](DESIGN_SYSTEM.md#paired-numeric-adjustments).

## Responsive drawing

R16: Brush/pencil previews accumulate input samples without committing or validating the entire document on each movement. Publish previews and start queued drawing work at most once per animation frame; consume coalesced events where available. Render only new stroke segments and reuse unchanged layer content within bounded working-memory caches. A cached preview must match full replay with pressure, opacity, clipping, grouping and styles. Release retains the final endpoint and commits exactly one undo step; Escape, focus loss, pointer cancellation/capture loss and document replacement discard transient work. Changed content, transforms, viewport/scale and history must not display stale cached pixels. Export preserves full-resolution originals and uses the same compositing rules.

## GPU acceleration

R17: Prefer hardware WebGPU for supported viewport rendering, with automatic Canvas2D/WASM fallback on unsupported devices, unsupported effects, precision/allocation limits or device loss. Retain unchanged visible-region textures; draw new brush/pencil segments and run supported effects on the GPU without CPU readback for presentation. Keep source resolution, constructor APIs, history, clipping and exports intact. Report the actual displayed backend. Test real shader output against the reference renderer with documented rounding/antialiasing tolerances, check resource cleanup and device-loss recovery, and distinguish software-adapter correctness tests from real-GPU performance/presentation verification. See [GPU backend scope and limitations](ARCHITECTURE.md#gpu-viewport-backend).

## Initial keyboard map

`Mod` means Command on macOS and Control on Windows/Linux. Shortcuts are suspended while typing in inputs, textareas, selects, or editable content. Escape can close a dialog or cancel a gesture.

| Action                                          | Shortcut                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Move tool                                       | V                                                         |
| Hand tool                                       | H                                                         |
| Crop canvas                                     | C                                                         |
| Artboard editor                                 | A                                                         |
| Text tool                                       | T                                                         |
| Paint bucket (Fill)                             | G                                                         |
| Brush / Pencil / Eraser / Pen / Marquee / Clone | B / N / E / P / M / S                                     |
| Dodge / Burn                                    | O / Shift+O                                               |
| Brush/pencil/clone diameter                     | [ / ]                                                     |
| Finish active path / polygon selection / Apply crop | Enter                                                  |
| Clear crop frame                                | Delete / Backspace in Crop mode                           |

## Architectural decisions

1. TypeScript for browser UI, application orchestration, and public DOM classes; React for the UI.
2. AssemblyScript for the initial WASM pixel kernel. It resembles TypeScript but is a different, constrained language. Ordinary npm/React code is not compiled into WASM.
3. Public class handles resolve objects by ID in the current document revision. Plain, versioned data-transfer objects are used for snapshots, files, and worker boundaries; attached state is immutable outside commands.
4. Constructor-created layers are detached until added to a document/group. Ownership, stable IDs, validation, atomic transactions, and undo are enforced centrally.
5. Adaptive WebGPU viewport rendering with retained textures and WGSL shaders; Canvas 2D and a WASM worker provide reference/export rendering and automatic fallback. Public document APIs are independent of the selected backend.
6. Original image assets are held separately from document/history metadata. Duplicate layers share sources.
7. No model/provider API in this milestone. A future AI adapter should produce validated document commands and new assets through the same public API. It must not evaluate generated JavaScript.

## Current practical limits

- Desktop browsers; PNG/JPEG/WebP/SVG/PSD imports and PNG/JPEG/WebP/SVG/PSD exports.
- Working color spaces: sRGB, Display P3, Adobe RGB 1998, Linear sRGB. Bradford chromatic adaptation, CIELAB/CIEXYZ/DeviceCMYK conversions, Delta E 2000 calculations, and soft-proofing gamut warnings are supported. 16-bit float and native CMYK printing channels remain future work.
- No fixed source/canvas megapixel cap. Positive safe-integer document dimensions; 64 layers, 8 group nesting levels, 60 undo entries.
- No fixed image/project byte-size cutoff. Browser decoding, memory and document-manifest allocation (plus JSON/base64 for legacy input) still impose real practical constraints; there is no infinite-size guarantee. Original sources remain resident.
- Manual external project saves plus local atomic recovery checkpoints; see [STORAGE_FORMAT.md](STORAGE_FORMAT.md). Browser recovery is not an external backup or a power-loss guarantee. Source assets retained for undo are released when changing documents.
- Rectangular layer hit testing and isolated groups. Basic text layers and single-canvas artboard resizing are implemented. Prototype PSD/PSB interchange and preflight capability inspection are delivered under ticket T17; arbitrary rotation, RAW, and multi-document workspace remain future work.
- Drawing limits: 2048 operations or paths per layer; 20,000 points per stroke/path; 128 marquee regions; 4096 clone tiles per stroke. These bound metadata complexity, not image dimensions. Paint operations can be removed/replaced through scripting; there is no individual stroke inspector yet.
- Marquee displays component outlines rather than a traced combined contour. Clone previews source pixels from the pre-stroke document using a bounded native-resolution tile cache; final source-tile encoding completes on release. Canvas 2D uses encoded sRGB blending and browser antialiasing; Photoshop parity is not claimed.
- Low-level `layer.reparent` uses the destination group's coordinate system; UI placement through `layer.place` preserves world position. General affine transforms remain future work.
