## Verification

Automated tests should cover DOM constructor ownership, live handles after undo/redo, transactions/rollback, cycle rejection, locked ancestors, project validation, and actual WASM pixel output. Browser checks should cover import, edit, keyboard shortcuts/focus, save/reopen, and export through the real worker/rendering pipeline. A 10000 × 5000 fixture must retain dimensions and original pixels through import, adjustment, save/reopen, and PNG export; inspect pixels across tile boundaries. Verify constructor scripting rollback/timeout/network isolation/revision conflicts and REST conflict/atomicity behavior.

## Automation and large-image acceptance

- Scripts execute off the UI thread with no host object references or network access, a 5-second timeout and explicit cancellation. Validate all returned operations and asset references; discard stale-revision results. This is a local prototype sandbox, not a security-reviewed marketplace runtime.
- The REST service uses local in-memory sessions and exposes metadata/commands/history only. Browser synchronization and image upload/render endpoints remain future scope. Document this distinction wherever the API is presented.
- Viewport rendering uses visible regions and bounded preview surfaces. Adjustments use small WASM tiles. PNG export uses tiles/scanline strips at document resolution rather than a document-sized canvas. Preview budgets must never be applied to import acceptance.
- Decoder/allocation failures report device/browser capability problems without silently resizing originals. See ARCHITECTURE.md for current memory limitations.

### Appearance modes

The editor and all developer docs support Light, Dark, and System. The editor exposes a compact sun/moon toggle at the bottom of the tool rail, with System available in its right-click/keyboard appearance popover; docs retain the labeled selector. Default to the OS preference, persist explicit choices locally, synchronize tabs, and respond to OS changes while System is selected. Apply the preference before first paint. Theme changes affect UI chrome and syntax highlighting only; rendered artwork, exported pixels, document data, and undo history must be unchanged. Storage failure must not prevent switching for the current page. Docs remain readable and follow the OS with JavaScript disabled.

## Professional editor and AI roadmap — planned, not implemented

R18 (planning requirement): maintain a feature-rich professional-editor roadmap that competes with Photoshop-level workflows while differentiating through intelligent assets, inspectable AI, protected source content and repeatable production. The owner explicitly requested automatic metadata extraction and generating image assets as layers. The plan must cover manual editing fundamentals as well as AI; it does not authorize claiming parity or running paid services merely by documenting them.

Acceptance for this planning deliverable: a source-backed competitive review, a baseline audit, a prioritized tool catalog, detailed metadata/generation contracts, OOP/REST/scripting/plugin integration boundaries, privacy/cost/error controls, phased implementation tickets, measurable release gates and a recorded work log. See [FEATURE_STRATEGY.md](FEATURE_STRATEGY.md), [COMPETITIVE_RESEARCH.md](COMPETITIVE_RESEARCH.md), [AI_FEATURE_SPECS.md](AI_FEATURE_SPECS.md), and [IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md](IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md). Feature acceptance in those files remains future work.

### Local metadata extraction — initial implementation

Raster imports automatically analyze original blobs locally in a worker. Properties → Asset info distinguishes decoded file facts from embedded declarations, preserves namespaces, reports parsing failures, and exports JSON sidecars with explicit attribution/private-field controls. Source bytes are unchanged; no inference or network service is involved. Reopening a project regenerates derived analysis. See [ASSET_METADATA.md](ASSET_METADATA.md) for tested coverage and limits. Authored descriptions, attribution and keywords now use command-backed layer metadata with locks, undo/redo, schema-v2 persistence, constructor scripting and REST patches. Sidecar exports exclude private authored fields by default. Human review states, OCR/semantic analysis and embedded metadata writing remain planned.

### Layer masks — first T06 slice

Every layer/group supports a non-destructive mask captured from the current rectangle/ellipse selection, including Boolean holes. Properties offers create/replace, enable, invert, paired density slider/number input and remove actions; controls obey locks and support keyboard focus. Changes share constructor scripting, strict REST patches, undo/redo and schema-v3 persistence. Layer-local geometry moves with layers, and masking applies before styles in Canvas/WASM export and WebGPU composition. Closed Bézier paths can also be copied from an attached vector layer; compound masks support even-odd holes and nonzero winding, with detached path editing through scripting. Selection and vector masks now include 0–128 px fractional feathering through the WASM worker, with complete filter halos across export boundaries and a paired slider/input. Masks support independent x/y translation and linking/unlinking with position-preserving toggles; unlinked masks stay fixed through ancestor motion and reparenting. Bézier masks support direct pen anchor/handle editing; mask rotation/scaling, bitmap-mask import and edge refinement remain planned. See [LayerMask](SCRIPTING_API.md#layermask) for exact current behavior.

### Direct mask movement

The Move tool offers a **Move target** selector. Choose Mask to drag the selected layer’s mask anywhere on the canvas without hit-selecting another layer or moving source content. Drag deltas use document pixels in either linked or unlinked mode; linking is unchanged. Arrow keys nudge by 1 px, Shift+Arrow by 10 px. Pointer movement previews, release commits once, and Escape/pointer cancellation discards the preview. Layer/ancestor locks apply. Selecting another layer/document or choosing a tool resets the target to Layer. Mask mode hides layer resize handles; mask rotation and scaling remain planned.

### Mask painting

Properties offers Add painted mask (initially reveal-all), or an explicit Replace with painted mask action for other mask kinds. Brush/Pencil options offer these targets for every mask kind: Layer, Mask · Hide, Mask · Reveal. Strokes obey the existing size/hardness/opacity controls, pointer pressure, selection clipping, locks, cancellation and one commit per gesture. Selection/Bézier masks retain their editable geometry beneath ordered paint refinements. Strokes modify mask coverage only, preserve source content, and persist through project/recovery serialization. Existing inversion/density/feather/link/position controls apply. Mask painting uses transient renderer previews without document-command construction per frame, reuses finished coverage and incrementally appends active points within bounded working caches; disk-backed bitmap masks remain future work.

### Direct Bézier mask editing

With a Bézier mask selected, choose Pen → Pen target → Mask paths. Existing contour outlines, anchors and control handles appear in the resolved mask coordinate plane. Drag an anchor to move its handles with it; dragging a handle mirrors its counterpart unless Alt/Option is held. Release commits one validated mask update; Escape/pointer cancellation discards previews. Click an anchor, then use arrows (Shift for 10 px) to nudge or Delete/Backspace to remove it. Removing a contour’s last anchor removes that contour, leaving the layer, mask settings and paint refinements intact. Empty clicks create no paths and Delete without a selected mask anchor does not delete the layer. Source-path/layer geometry is unchanged, locks apply, and save/reopen/undo use the existing mask contract. Select an anchor and choose Insert midpoint to subdivide its outgoing segment without changing the curve; the new anchor becomes selected and the operation is one undo entry. Click a contour away from existing anchors/handles to insert a control point at the nearby curve location. The curve is subdivided without changing its shape; the inserted anchor becomes selected after release. Hit tolerance is seven screen pixels at any zoom, and existing anchors/handles take priority. Insertion previews without changing history, commits once on release, and Escape/pointer cancellation discards it. Clicking elsewhere remains a no-op unless New contour is active.

### Drawing Bézier mask contours

Properties → Add Bézier mask creates an empty vector mask on an unmasked layer. An empty mask hides content; the adjacent instruction explains how to reveal it by drawing a contour. Pen → Mask paths → New contour starts an explicit draft so empty clicks in normal anchor-edit mode remain harmless. Click adds a corner, dragging sets mirrored Bézier handles, and Delete/Backspace removes the last draft anchor. Enter or Close contour closes and commits; clicking the first anchor closes after at least two anchors exist. A single-anchor contour can be finished with Enter and edited afterward. The draft previews a closed contour and uses a dashed outline; it does not modify document history or saved project content until completion. Each completed contour is one undo entry, and existing geometry, mask settings and paint refinements remain intact. Even-odd nested contours make holes; nonzero follows winding direction.

Escape, Cancel contour, pointer cancellation, tool/target changes and document/selection changes discard the draft. Revisions and locks are checked before commit, and contour/anchor bounds apply before accepting more points. Existing linked/unlinked coordinate rules apply. Arrow nudging is for committed anchors; drawing drafts use pointer placement and last-anchor removal. Undo cancels a draft before applying the normal document undo. Controls preserve their footprint when entering/leaving drawing mode so the canvas does not shift. Project persistence/export uses the existing vector-mask contract.

### Non-destructive canvas crop — first T07 slice

Crop canvas (C) enters on-canvas crop mode. Drag a new frame or start from a single additive rectangular selection, rounded outward to whole pixels. Precise bounds opens the numeric X/Y/width/height dialog using the current frame when present. Reset and Use rectangular selection actions are explicit; compound/elliptical selections do not masquerade as a rectangular crop. Applying creates one undo entry; cancelling or rejecting a stale dialog changes no artwork. Bounds may extend outside the old canvas. Rotation, straightening and affine transforms remain planned.

Crop translates root layers and pixel selections into the new coordinate plane. Linked masks follow their layers; every unlinked mask origin is rebased, including masks inside groups. Locked content participates in this global coordinate change without losing its locks. Source bytes, source resolution, local path/stroke geometry, effects and off-canvas content remain intact. Save/reopen and PNG output use the new dimensions; a later negative-origin crop can recover the previous framing. Crop/resize and their undo/redo clear transient pen/clone coordinates. No arbitrary image resolution limit is added. UI, constructor scripting and strict REST commands share validation, history and failure atomicity.

### On-canvas crop frames

A crop frame is transient until Enter or Apply crop. Drag inside it to move; drag an edge or any of eight screen-sized handles to resize, with a one-pixel minimum. Drag outside the existing frame or choose New frame to draw another. Shift draws a square or preserves the original aspect ratio when dragging a corner, rounded to whole pixels. Edges resize one axis. Frames may extend beyond the current canvas; the overlay dims the excluded part of the current canvas and draws a thirds grid and pixel dimensions.

Arrows nudge a frame; focused handle buttons use arrows to resize their corresponding edges. Shift increases keyboard increments to 10 px. Delete/Backspace clears the frame without deleting artwork. Escape, Cancel crop, pointer cancellation, window blur, tool changes and document revision/replacement changes discard the frame. Undo first cancels the draft, then performs normal document undo. Numeric-dialog Cancel retains the prior frame; applying the dialog uses the same crop command. Pointer updates are scheduled once per animation frame and the final pointer endpoint is retained even before a scheduled frame runs. No document preview mutation, asset rewrite or history entry occurs before Apply.

## Generation and batch review corrections (2026-09-30)

Generation must reject unconfigured providers. Procedural providers belong exclusively in test fixtures; no synthetic fallback is permitted in job execution, reference capture, source-image loading, or batch export. The provider bakeoff remains incomplete and must not infer real scores from fixture images or profile constants.

Encoded candidate images must decode successfully, match declared dimensions, and have their transparency verified from decoded pixels. Invalid candidates cannot be promoted into project assets. Masked edits use reference-rendered document pixels, including groups, masks, text, paint and adjustments; capture errors prevent submission. Synchronous recipes reject `ai.generate` before applying any commands.

Batch runs persist source bytes and completed variant checkpoints. Reload recovery resumes interrupted work and skips successful items; completed variant bytes are hash-checked before reuse. Missing or undecodable sources and rendering/encoding failures fail the item explicitly. PNG, JPEG and WebP deliverables must contain the requested format and dimensions, independent of viewport allocation defaults.

Delivery variant IDs must be unique within a batch; creation and resume reject duplicates before writing outputs. Archive filenames preserve the format extension when truncating long stems, and colliding names receive distinct suffixes without losing that extension.

Batch delivery variants apply contain/cover/fill to the complete source artboard composition. Nested layers, text, masks and effects must share the fit mapping; the source document and its editable geometry remain unchanged. Contain margins are transparent and cannot reveal artwork outside the original artboard. Streamed PNG tiles and full-frame rendering must agree.

The command palette opens with Mod+K outside text inputs or from the search icon in the tool rail. It searches shared action labels/categories with exact-word, substring and abbreviation ranking. Arrow keys, Home/End, Enter and Escape navigate, execute and dismiss; unavailable actions remain discoverable but cannot run. The palette must retain search focus while typing, restore the previous control when dismissed, and close before an action opens another modal. It uses the same action callbacks and availability checks as keyboard shortcuts, including shared document undo. Multi-document tabs, layer filtering and multi-selection remain separate unfinished T22 work.

Layer search/filtering combines case-insensitive name words, layer type, effective visibility and effective lock state. Effective state includes ancestors' visibility/locking; opacity is not treated as the visibility switch. Matching descendants retain ancestor rows for context and temporarily expand those groups. Clearing filters restores the previous collapsed state. Filtering changes no document content, selection or undo history; an excluded active layer remains selected and is named in the panel. Filters reset when the active document ID changes. Empty results and a clear-filters action remain keyboard accessible.

Layer multi-selection: Ctrl/Cmd/Shift-click layer rows or canvas hits toggles membership; a normal layer-row click replaces the set. Selected rows remain pressed and the canvas shows union bounds. With Move and layer targeting, arrows nudge all selected roots; dragging an already selected member previews and commits their common translation once. Escape/pointer cancellation discards the preview; an intervening document revision rejects the multi-drag commit. The Layers panel offers six alignments and selected-root deletion in one undo transaction. Selecting both parent and descendant does not double-transform the descendant. Pixel marquee and active-layer inspector/tool properties remain independent. Multi-layer resize/rotation and richer range-selection semantics remain planned.

Document tabs support drag-and-drop ordering and Alt+Left/Right while the tab is focused. Ordering preserves keyboard focus, active document and undo state. Normal Left/Right/Home/End continue to navigate tabs. Tab ordering is session-only.

When another document tab is open, the Layers panel offers a keyboard-accessible “Copy selection to” destination selector. It is disabled during operations or with no selected layers. Copy preserves the source tab and source artwork, selects the copies in the destination, and creates one undo entry there. Destination choices use session identity and numbered labels so documents with identical names remain distinct.

Recover work includes explicit Save workspace and Restore workspace actions. Workspace saving captures all open documents and their tab order, active document, selections and zoom/pan. Restore preserves current edited tabs and opens restored copies only after all project snapshots validate. This manual checkpoint is separate from automatic workspace and per-document recovery; workspace snapshots do not retain undo history.

Recover work includes an opt-in “Restore saved workspace on startup” setting, off by default. Startup restores this browser tab’s latest automatic workspace checkpoint, falling back to the explicit Save workspace checkpoint when none exists. It restores once per app mount and reports failures through the normal editor error state. Manual checkpoints remain independent. Disabling the setting returns to normal blank startup.

Recover work supports named workspace milestones: enter a label, save an immutable version, and restore a listed version as copies beside existing work. Duplicate labels retain separate timestamped versions; saving a milestone does not replace the current startup checkpoint. Versions remain local to this browser.

The Layout inspector provides a shared Rotation slider and precise numeric input (-180° to 180°). The value is the layer's canvas-space x-axis angle; edits rotate around the center of its geometric canvas bounds, preserving its existing scale/shear. Parent transforms are accounted for. Pointer preview commits through shared layer updates, keyboard adjustment uses the reusable slider bindings, and undo reverses one committed adjustment. Locked or geometry-free layers disable rotation.

Generation recovery UI: the generation dialog includes a keyboard-operable expandable list of unfinished saved requests, with provider, request ID, timestamp and reserved amount. Users can refresh accounting and cancel undispatched requests. Dispatched requests remain reserved until confirmed host reconciliation; the UI does not guess charges or automatically resubmit work. Cancellation failures are visible and preserve accounting. Saved candidate pixels, provenance and protected references now restore to the review shelf with integrity/decode checks and explicit placement approval. Full job reconstruction and automatic queued resumption remain planned.

### On-canvas layer rotation

A single unlocked layer with geometry exposes a rotation handle above its selection bounds. Dragging previews canvas-space rotation around the geometric center; hold Shift to snap the rotation delta to 15° increments. Release commits one shared undoable layer update. Escape cancels the preview without changing the document. The Layout Rotation slider/input remains the keyboard-accessible precise adjustment path. Multi-layer rotation and guide snapping remain planned.

### Shared-center selected-layer rotation

The Layers panel offers 90° clockwise/counterclockwise and 180° rotation for multiple selected layers. Selected roots rotate together around the center of their combined geometric bounds in canvas space; selecting a group and its child does not transform the child twice. Parent scale/shear is respected. The operation rejects locked roots and missing geometry and commits in one undo transaction. Scripts can supply arbitrary finite angles through `document.layerSelection.rotate(degrees)`. Multi-layer pointer rotation and scaling remain planned.

The on-canvas rotation handle also supports multiple selected layers: it uses the shared geometric center and transforms selected roots, excluding descendants of selected ancestors. Drag preview leaves document revision unchanged; release commits every root together. Shift snaps the shared rotation delta, Escape cancels, and document revision changes invalidate commit. Any locked or geometry-free selected root suppresses the handle. Multi-layer scaling and guides/snapping remain planned.

### Shared-center selected-layer scaling

The Layers panel offers 50% and 200% scale actions for multiple selected layers. Scaling operates in canvas space around the shared geometric center and preserves editable source contents. Parent transforms, inherited locks, geometric-bounds validation, descendant exclusion and one-step undo match shared-center rotation. Arbitrary positive horizontal/vertical factors are available through `document.layerSelection.scale(x, y = x)`. Pointer scaling and paired slider/numeric UI controls remain outstanding.

Multi-layer scale also has a paired reusable slider/numeric input in the Layers panel (1–400%, 0.1% steps). The percentage is relative to the current selection and remains staged until Apply selection scale, which commits once and resets the control to 100%. Changing documents or layer selection resets the draft. These UI control bounds are not document or API scale limits; scripts accept other positive representable factors. Keyboard slider adjustment and precise typed values use the existing reusable control behavior.

### Multi-layer corner scaling

Multiple selected layers with editable geometry expose four corner handles. Dragging scales the selected roots in canvas space about the opposite corner; Shift uses a uniform factor. The gesture preserves editable source content, previews without changing document revision, and commits once on release. Escape cancels. Crossing the opposite corner clamps to a positive scale rather than reflecting the artwork. Locked or geometry-free roots suppress these handles. Single-layer resize behavior remains unchanged.

### Move-tool canvas snapping

Snap to canvas is an opt-in checkbox in Move tool options. Layer dragging aligns the moving geometric union's edges or center to canvas edges/center within six screen pixels, independent of zoom. Horizontal and vertical matches are chosen independently and displayed as temporary guide lines. Alt bypasses snapping during the gesture. Pointer release commits the snapped movement through existing commands; preview and cancellation do not add history. Mask movement and keyboard nudges are unchanged. The toggle is session-local; custom persistent guides and snapping to other artwork remain planned.

With Snap to canvas enabled, Include artwork optionally adds visible stationary artwork edges and centers as snap targets. Hidden/zero-opacity subtrees, selected moving roots and descendants, and groups containing moving roots are excluded. Bounds are geometric rather than shadow/effect extents. Targets share the same screen-space tolerance, transient guides and Alt bypass; both options remain session-local. Persistent user-authored guides remain planned.

Focused guide controls: Left/Right nudges vertical guides; Up/Down nudges horizontal guides by one document pixel, or ten with Shift. Escape cancels a guide drag without history. These focus-local controls consume their events so layer nudging does not also run.

Rulers: drag the horizontal ruler into the canvas to create a horizontal guide, or the vertical ruler for a vertical guide. Drop outside the document or press Escape to cancel. Enter on a focused ruler creates a centered guide. Creation is one undoable document edit.

### Dodge and burn tools

Dodge (`O`) and Burn (`Shift+O`) create editable tonal strokes on a separate tonal adjustment layer, or append to the selected tonal layer. The layer processes its live preceding backdrop within the same group; current-layer/all-layer sampling options are not implemented. Controls expose shadows/midtones/highlights, exposure and tone protection, plus shared brush size, hardness, opacity, flow, spacing, smoothing and pressure controls. Numeric settings use sliders beside precise inputs. The tools share brush-size memory and bracket shortcuts. Paint color is not used. Strokes capture the active pixel selection, preview before release, and commit as one named undo entry. Escape cancels the stroke. Original image bytes remain unchanged; layer/stroke data persists through project files using schema v8. Rendering currently uses the Canvas/CPU-worker path, without a GPU retouch or performance guarantee.

### Interactive patch retouching

Patch (`J`) uses an existing marquee selection. Drag on the canvas toward the donor region; a translated selection outline shows donor placement. Release to solve and add one alpha-preserving patch adjustment, with one undo entry. Zero-distance drags do not commit. Escape cancels the gesture or pending operation. Sampling options are current layer, current and below, or all layers (default); detail options are donor gradients (default) or stronger mixed gradients. Invalid donors, changed document/selection, allocation failure or solver nonconvergence report an error without committing. The current preview indicates geometry, not a live solved pixel result. Automatic donor selection and live solved previews remain planned.

### Spot Healing brush

Spot Healing (`Shift+J`) accumulates a brush path and repairs it on release using local donor search and Poisson blending. Size, hardness, opacity, flow, spacing, smoothing and pressure dynamics use the shared brush controls; an existing selection clips coverage. Sampling and source/mixed detail controls are shared with Patch. Search radius defaults to 64 document pixels and is adjustable. Successful strokes create separate alpha-preserving adjustment layers with one undo entry; source images remain unchanged. Escape aborts pending work. The overlay indicates stroke extent, not the solved result. No-donor/nonconverged/stale/cancelled operations do not commit. Donor choice is currently a local boundary heuristic; automatic semantic quality and the performance release gate remain unverified.

The Patch tool (`J`) supports Source and Destination placement modes. Source selects the repair region and drags toward a donor. Destination selects donor artwork and drags it to the repair region. Both retain original selection geometry and source assets, commit a new patch adjustment in one undo step, and support Escape cancellation. Source/mixed gradient guidance remains an independent “Patch detail” control. The translated outline indicates donor location in Source mode and repair location in Destination mode; it is not a solved-pixel preview.

Automatic workspace checkpoints now preserve open-document content, tab order, active tab, layer selection, color/proof settings and zoom/pan. Changes are coalesced on a two-second timer and published atomically after encoding. Recovery displays pending/saving/saved/error state, allows flushing pending changes, and can restore the automatic checkpoint as copies beside existing work. Reload restoration remains opt-in. A sessionStorage identity associates reloads with the same browser tab; browser Web Locks prevent simultaneous tabs from writing the same identity. A duplicated tab forks its identity while the original remains open. Named/manual checkpoints and per-document recovery remain separate. Pending edits can be lost if a crash occurs before the asynchronous checkpoint completes; the retained undo/redo window is persisted with the completed workspace checkpoint. A new browser session without the tab identity falls back to the manual checkpoint; Recovery lists saved browser workspaces across tab identities for explicit copy restoration and confirmed cleanup.

Recovery’s “Saved browser workspaces” list shows automatic checkpoints across browser-tab identities, including document names and save times. “Open workspace copy” restores validated projects beside current edited documents. Checkpoint removal requires a second confirmation click and is refused while any browser tab holds its autosave writer lock. Users can close that originating tab and retry. Damaged checkpoint metadata remains listed with restoration disabled and removal available. Listing checks metadata; complete project/source validation still occurs during restore. Startup selection remains unchanged: this tab’s automatic checkpoint, then the manual fallback. Other automatic checkpoints are chosen explicitly from Recovery.

Workspace checkpoints must retain each document's existing undo/redo window (60 combined entries), including image assets referenced only by those entries. Reloaded Undo/Redo must reproduce original pixels and new edits must discard the redo branch. Validate all histories and assets before installing any restored workspace documents. Automatic, manual and named workspace checkpoints share this behavior; ordinary project files and per-document recovery remain content snapshots. Edits after the last completed checkpoint remain subject to the documented recovery limitations.

Recovery displays browser-reported storage usage, quota, estimated remaining capacity and persistence status. These are origin-wide estimates, not per-project measurements or a guarantee of successful saves. Users can refresh estimates and explicitly request persistent storage; opening Recovery must never request it automatically. Unsupported APIs, failed estimates and declined persistence must leave editing, project downloads and recovery actions usable. Browser persistence does not replace external backups or protect against clearing site data.

Quota failures must report an actionable storage-full message, retain the latest failed capture for explicit retry without requiring another edit, preserve earlier completed checkpoints and keep project downloads available. Newer edits supersede a retained failed capture. Recovery provides Retry document recovery; retry must not run in a tight automatic loop or prevent other queued sessions from saving.

Recipe condition operands must be validated before executing any step, including direct service execution without JSON import. Invalid conditions reject the entire transaction, preserving document content and history. Every accepted variant ID must survive delivery manifest validation and ZIP export. ZIP export emits ZIP64 records when counts, entry sizes or offsets reach classic sentinel values, without truncating fields. UTF-8 filenames remain subject to the ZIP format’s 65,535-byte limit. Large-payload memory and responsiveness validation remain outstanding.

Smart objects use schema 14 and shared master definitions with independently transformed instances. Constructor-based scripting and REST command arrays must support creation, replacement and undo. Master edits update all dependent instances and reject if an affected placement is locked. Detached contents edits do not commit automatically. Save/reopen must preserve component identities, original source bytes and rendered appearance; missing references and cyclic graphs fail atomically. Brush/pencil/eraser/clone/tonal/healing share optional angle/roundness and spherical pen-tilt response through OO values, commands, masks, native/SVG/supported-WGSL replay, projects/history and versioned portable presets. Legacy absent-tip artwork must retain its old geometry. Tip controls edit only a draft until Apply; cursors use the same affine stroke plane. Schema 30 rejects falsely old labels across every brush-bearing context. Actual browser/script/REST and shader correctness are required; synthetic pen events do not prove physical-tablet or all-tool 60fps acceptance. Textured tips, symmetry, mixer/smudge and broader F06 remain separate work.

### Mirror/radial brush symmetry

F06 supports Off, vertical/horizontal mirror, both-axis and radial 2–32-sector settings with exact fractional document-space lines/centers. Immutable BrushSymmetry values and optional stroke metadata retain implicit original ink plus 1–31 affine copies through OO/script/REST commands, masks/filter masks, raster erasures, tonal/healing/clone, schema-31 validation, projects and retained history. No raw sample is replaced or dropped. Captured selection and whole-stroke opacity apply once after copy flow. Full footprint geometry must match native/SVG/supported WGSL; incremental ordering, clipped stamp grids, rotated-pencil support and inverse affine/master-plane input are required. UI draft cancellation/focus, guides, viewport-bounded ghost cursors and portable preset v3 persistence are part of the delivery. Legacy v1/v2 presets reset symmetry to Off. Real 50 MP symmetric edit/source/undo/project checks and normal production without globals are required. Physical devices, textured tips, mixer/smudge and full F06/F14 remain separate gates.

## Authored textured-brush increment — in verification

Schema-32 BrushTexture values reference existing image sources through ordinary brush/pencil/clone/eraser/tonal APIs, painted mask/filter-mask refinements and embedded masters. Retain original source bytes and TIFF decode choices through projects, workspace history, recipes and cross-document copies. Native coverage shares existing tip/pressure/symmetry, flow-before-opacity and captured-selection semantics; unsupported GPU paint falls back completely, and SVG embeds source-resolution coverage with explicit editability/sampling limits. Existing commands, locks, atomic rollback, revisions, undo and isolated permissions remain required. This increment is being verified; a complete F06 textured-tip workflow also requires active-tool source controls, texture cursors, explicit cross-document tool source ownership and original-source portable brush presets. Physical-tablet, hardware-GPU/display and sustained all-tool F14 acceptance remain open.


## Texture pointer controls — 2026-10-18, in verification

Brush-family tools must expose the custom Texture dialog with original file/document-source selection, explicit TIFF page/precision review, luminance/alpha and invert controls, and draft Apply/Cancel semantics. Preparing/changing a preference must not mutate artwork/history. Real brush, pencil, eraser, clone, dodge, burn, healing, layer-mask and filter-mask gestures must capture local source references, preserve full source geometry/bytes, support normal undo, and survive source-document closure. Cancelled/failed gestures release unused new references without deleting current/history or foreign replacement assets. Cursor/preview proxies may be bounded, but authored sources must remain original. This increment is connected and in verification. Source-bearing portable presets, mixer/smudge, tablet/hardware/display and sustained all-tool gates remain open.


Texture gesture continuation, queued previews and final commit also validate the captured store/record/bitmap identity. Removing or replacing the asset under the same ID cancels/rejects the stale gesture without document/history edits or deletion of the foreign replacement. This guard supplements document revision checks; asset IDs alone are not an ownership proof.


## Source-bearing brush presets — 2026-10-18, in verification

Preset/pack v4 carries image-backed coverage preferences and exact original Blob sources with native dimensions, MIME/name, SHA-256 and TIFF page/precision choices. Source-free JSON versions 1–3 remain readable/exportable. Binary packs use a checksummed 48-byte header, strict manifest and contiguous original-blob slices; readers reject missing/unused references, corrupted extents/checksums and native decode/dimension mismatches before any import commit. Portable source IDs are remapped and cannot bind to document asset IDs. The single existing IndexedDB v1 preset store now atomically stores optional source blobs alongside their preset; no physical schema migration is needed. Older strict readers reject these newer records while preserving bytes.

The library verifies actual stored source contents before writes and retains last-valid snapshots on failures. Read-only keepalive requests maintain the native write lock across asynchronous checks; only active request callbacks queue changes. Recovery v2 preserves raw records and original blobs, including invalid preset metadata, and compares complete content fingerprints under that lock before reset. Same-size byte changes and stale revisions cannot be erased with an old backup. Legacy JSON recovery remains available for source-free records; unsupported raw non-JSON values still fail without deleting data.

The custom preset dialog connects source-aware save/update/rename/duplicate/delete/import/export/download/recovery and shows source name/dimensions/coverage. Applying privately verifies/decodes an original, guards abort/supersession/document/tool/source changes, then uses normal tool selection/configuration; errors retain prior ready preferences and newer human edits. Preferences stay outside document undo; actual strokes still use shared OO commands/history and collision-safe document leases. Original images stay independent of viewport/cursor proxies, library deletion and closed source documents. This adds no isolated script/plugin file privilege, paid provider, upload, REST/browser sync or document schema bump. See [BRUSH_PRESETS.md](BRUSH_PRESETS.md) for signatures, binary contract, errors and limits. Complete native/production verification and wider F06/F14/device gates remain open.


### Textured coverage crop and retained-read correctness

On a shared output-pixel lattice, textured brush/pencil/eraser/clone coverage must agree across whole, cropped and incremental replay, including fractional zoom, affine placement, inversion and native mask/filter-mask targets. Preserve original texture/source bytes and geometry, complete authored samples, flow before whole-stroke opacity/selection, one-step history, and cancellation without partial publication. Retirement of cache retention must not cancel an independent read. Partial texture readback must preserve the full native projection canvas; smaller captures alone must not change affine edge pixels. Saturation shortcuts require proven native destination-byte identity; fractional-flow counterexamples must remain excluded. Working budgets and synthetic browser evidence do not establish whole-process memory, physical-tablet/display, representative-image quality or sustained all-tool performance.


### Native geometry across viewport and export — 2026-10-21

At the same native sampling scale, transformed raster artwork, bitmap-mask coverage, vector artwork and affine smart objects must retain exact complete RGBA across viewport rendering, irregular cropped regions and streamed native PNG output. Request clipping must not change the underlying primitive/image rasterization. Preserve complete small footprints inside the existing4MP/8192-edge working budget and use full canonical native cells for larger ones. Keep integer-native raster fast paths, original five-argument image geometry, source bytes/dimensions, shared mutation/history and public isolation contracts. Spatial halos and projection overscan must fit before allocating a complete sampling cell. These are working-buffer choices, never source-image/import limits.

Actual Gaussian processing with a331-pixel sigma did not finish within120seconds in one tiny affine-view prototype. Allocation planning is checked separately with processing explicitly stubbed; that check does not prove actual large-blur output or performance. FullF14, representative quality, sustained/editor-wide/release latency, physical hardware/tablet/display and process-memory acceptance remain open.


### Actual large-halo Gaussian verification — 2026-10-21

The earlier331-pixel Gaussian timeout is reproduced on the committed engine under the unchanged120-second browser timeout. A later exact support refinement removes only zero-alpha margin contributions. Its real-processing regression, separate from the existing explicitly stubbed allocation-planning test, must complete affine viewport and native PNG rendering with unchanged complete pixels, source bytes/dimensions and model data. All jobs retain the existing4MP/8192-edge budget. Empty, sparse and dense requests must preserve Gaussian, unsharp and all frequency-band semantics across reused worker memory. Passing this particular sparse case does not establish general large-dense-blur,33ms input, editor-wide/sustained, physical-device, quality or process-memory acceptance. Final validation is recorded in the roadmap and benchmark evidence.


### Native convolution reuse and geometry fidelity — 2026-10-21

Adjacent spatial outputs must preserve every original Gaussian/unsharp/frequency contribution and its floating-point order while reusing source/weight reads. Independent accumulators, clipped/empty support, zero-support axes, even/odd dimensions and single-column tails must retain native output and source ownership. Do not combine output pixels, approximate a Gaussian, add an unsupported-only module requirement or downsample the source. A scalar optimization must keep existing worker/ABI, scratch and4MP/8192-edge native work contracts. Kernel and controlled export measurements remain separate from33ms input, editor-wide/sustained, hardware, quality and process-memory acceptance.

# Canoli Studio System Design & Architecture Specification

## Large bitmap precision and ownership invariant

A source bitmap's full geometry survives precision fallback. Recover native premultiplied bytes through bounded patch reads; choose numerical sampling from projected-coordinate precision, without limiting or resizing originals. Preserve axis-aligned half-pixel ties and integrate affine support in the output pixel plane. Only one numerical reader is active per texture batch; its 64 native 64×64 entries are bounded independently of source dimensions. Share a task deadline across captures and reject clear/disposal/source changes before worker conversion/publication. Cache retirement cannot cancel independent reads. Mutable native canvases are snapshotted once, private copies close exactly once, and original ImageBitmaps remain borrowed. Source identities participate in retained bitmap-mask keys. Renderer/schema/history/isolation contracts remain unchanged; memory and latency claims require separate measured evidence.

## Native raster work partition invariant

Rectangular frequency sampling may reduce requests only without increasing estimated halo work. Include both nested composition projection margins before selecting a preferred 1,000,000-pixel job; retain existing native-source/placement eligibility, 256/512/1024 fallbacks and the 4 MP/8192-edge allocation checks. Independent Linear Light/Burn partitions retain the previous 1,048,576-pixel budget and 8192 working edges. Awaited work rechecks cancellation before publication. No working-grid choice changes original geometry, pixel equations, assets, OO mutation/history, persistent schemas or isolation.

## Ordinary paint crop and retained-buffer invariant

Untextured coverage on the same output-pixel lattice must be independent of viewport/export crop boundaries. Canonical native cells retain complete contributing primitives; oversized projected geometry uses bounded numerical pixel coverage. Preserve original sample indices, pressure, tilt, copy order and source geometry. Apply selection and whole-stroke opacity after raw stamp accumulation. Opaque shortcuts require certified complete pixels and identical destination bytes, rather than approximate edge coverage.

Accepted active prefixes own mutable inputs. Yielded extensions stay private until current-generation publication; cancellation preserves a reusable accepted prefix and releases failed stages. One task deadline spans consecutive numerical primitives as well as pixel blocks. Every retained native padding surface counts toward the mask LRU alongside the raw viewport, including size changes at an existing key. Working-surface budgets never become authored image or geometry limits. Logical owned-buffer checks do not establish browser process-memory or physical-display acceptance.

Normalize lattice indices only when an integral projected coordinate round-trips exactly through its inverse scale; preserve genuinely fractional origins. Retention epochs do not cancel independent reads. A busy mask-cache producer owns an exclusive lease: a second reader uses private work, and eviction/cache clearing retires the owner until its lease releases. Explicit caller cancellation still stops work and prevents partial publication.

## Shared native frequency radius and preview ownership — schema 37

A group radius is a parent parameter, not a rewrite of locked band records. The nearest explicit finite value controls descendant native frequency filters in the same document plane; null inherits and component entry resets scope. Resolver-derived sigma never mutates serialized fallback values. Preserve effective scope when extracting artwork for rasterization, conversion, isolated Photoshop output or another document. LayerGroup commands enforce group/ancestor locks, field age and atomic history normally.

One private captured source supports all dialog previews and final commit. A preview owns its bounded native crop/halo, worker copies and output canvases; obsolete/aborted work cannot publish a frame. Returned frames survive preparation disposal until explicitly released. The UI has one active preview request and coalesces pending choices. Commit uses a fresh model plus source/selection/revision/lifetime checks and only installs its original-resolution capture after render preflight. Failure must retain the base or dispose it safely, never publish partial layers/assets. Real native/50MP/cache/performance and full-roadmap gates remain open until measured.

An exact render shortcut may replace only structurally canonical, unchanged native regions with their captured raster. Retouch intersections and any changed filter/mask/geometry/source settings preserve full decomposition. Effective-radius and working-budget checks precede elision. Per-render Gaussian/original sharing is bounded to 8 MiB and never survives the render; source signatures and native prefixes distinguish cache inputs. Filter-mask mixing always retains the correct original pixels. Shared recursive task checkpoints and PNG tile boundaries yield for input/cancellation without reducing native output resolution or discarding edits.

## Frequency reconstruction and phase invariants — introduced in schema 36

Native captured O and rounded Gaussian L define opaque high H=round(127.5+(O−L)/2). Linear Light produces clamp(L+2H−255); a protected Linear Burn plane subtracts its single lost rounding bit, preserving exact native RGB8 before source alpha and affine resampling. Low/high/correction must derive from the same source and radius. Bands remain independently retouchable; original source records/bytes are never overwritten. Native composition must sample the real image-frame edge rather than transparent padded tile edges.

Preserve original raster ordering: document-pixel tone before ordinary erasures; active wet reconstruction owns its entire native sequence and expanded bounds. Raster-erasure mask records retain captured operation dimensions and source texture references. Post-placement document-tone filters must trail native filters; their mask coverage is feathered natively then projected, with inversion/density applied at mixing. Worker interfaces snapshot owned inputs and validate result types/extents. Preparation leases immutable source identities, rejects stale/cancelled work and commits once through shared commands. Cache keys include reachable-master dependencies and radius/prefix geometry; unrelated edits must not invalidate immutable captured-source low planes. Project/workspace remain 3/2. Native/50MP/interchange/automation and performance gates are still being verified; no whole-roadmap completion follows from this invariant.

## Red-eye correction invariant

Selection-masked pupil correction is an ordinary parametric adjustment, with a strict schema-35 record and immutable public constructor. UI captures document-space selection in the inserted layer's local plane atomically; scripts/REST may explicitly supply normal masks. Native WASM and GPU WGSL implement the documented straight-RGB8 red-excess predicate, modify only red, and preserve alpha. Worker calls snapshot inputs before readiness, validate returned type/extent and preserve caller ownership. Mask, opacity, affine placement, revision, lock, history and source-asset invariants remain shared. Working tiles do not cap source geometry. This local manual operation introduces no semantic detection, provider calls, cloud privileges or REST/browser synchronization.

## Prepared prefix epoch, storage and frame invariant — functional acceptance; latency open

Matching same-session native epochs permit reuse of prepared pixels. Captured hints plus new projections must cover exactly the complete current output; omit cells reverted to original pixels. Ordinary snapshots/finish remain complete and independently owned. Each view owns its leases independently of the adapter's separate current-output ownership. Replacing/discarding prepared output must not close resources held by older frames, renderer preparation or committed assets. Check active processing storage even on no-read reuse paths, then transfer final storage/result ownership explicitly. Full source/revision/native alpha checks precede one OO commit. Failure publishes no host edits/assets and clears private work. Output memory is workload dependent, sharing bitmaps with views; no source cap is introduced.

A stable wet owner shares the existing preparation frame boundary, avoiding an extra wait after asynchronous preparation while preserving one start per owner/frame boundary. Obsolete source/view/font/backend work remains cancelled and retained frame resources release independently. Actual main build/unit/native checks pass; its 51 non-documentation release files exactly match the isolated 82-workflow production runtime. [prefix evidence](benchmarks/brush-wet-prefix-reuse-2026-10-18.json) separates mixed continuous-pointer p95 from improved small-fixture release medians. Neither establishes33 ms, general60fps, sustained/device/process-memory or full-roadmap acceptance.

## Resident wet storage invariant — functional acceptance; performance gates open

Only a fresh, unused, exclusively claimed native store may defer unpublished working writes into the bounded cache. Capture caller arrays before asynchronous eviction. Commit dirty evictions atomically before advancing resident epochs, drop unreferenced unpublished scratch without I/O, and flush every referenced original/result before finish transfers its store/lock. Snapshots own independent native stores with paired original/result writes. Recheck source, cancellation, native method identity and storage lifetime around I/O; failures publish no host edits/assets. Explicit disposal drops unpublished memory. Custom/used/modified stores and zero-cache operation preserve write-through semantics.

Actual main build/unit/native acceptance and byte-identical production runtime are recorded in [sealed evidence](benchmarks/brush-wet-resident-cache-2026-10-18.json). Three clean paired runs preserve exact pixels, source/project operations and undo. Observed median per-run p95 improves to 88.1–119.7 ms, still above 33 ms for every fixture. No source geometry cap, public mutation bypass, isolated privilege, REST/browser sync or gesture durability guarantee is introduced. Full F06/F14, sustained/device/process-memory and the complete original roadmap remain open.

## Native wet working-set invariant — functional acceptance

Keep complete original backing cells independently of numerical working regions. Crop reservoir sampling, native coverage and worker transfers only to the cell/support/halo intersection while preserving global pixel centers, native raster grid, summation order and destination bytes outside support. Commit paired private planes and superseded destinations before advancing resident cache state. Earlier reservoir epochs remain readable until all dab cells are staged; bound cleanup groups and check cancellation without source-geometry limits. Custom storage fallback, private snapshot ownership, host validation, one shared undo and schema34/project3/workspace2 stay unchanged. The actual head and clean paired evidence are sealed in brush-wet-gesture-performance-2026-10-18.json. Every measured fixture still fails33ms, and sustained/device/process-memory gates remain open.

## Wet mask plane and commit invariant — implementation in verification

Mask operations preserve source geometry and reconstruct native raw alpha in order, before the full mask/world/master transform and mask-wide appearance. Coverage capture neutralizes enabled/inverted/density/feather and never samples rendered artwork or filter output. Private retained jobs, original asset leases, prefix/render ownership and source/revision guards are shared with layer wet authoring. LayerMask values serialize mode-tagged ordered operations under schema34; root/history/embedded age checks, central asset remapping and shared command discovery protect every external commit. Strict prepared-alpha validation precedes atomic scripts and independent REST transactions. Working ROI/cache budgets do not limit source resolution. Whole-process/device and sustained-throughput acceptance remain open.


## Wet gesture resource boundary — in verification

The pointer tools and trusted one-shot authoring share a retained native job with private original-source leases, immutable prefix documents and privately decoded output PNGs. Prefix assets have separate creator/render leases; obsolete queued and finished jobs release their references. Host source/revision/lifetime checks guard preparation and presentation. Final numeric workspace cleanup and prepared alpha validation precede one synchronous shared transaction, with collision checks and exact-owner rollback. Every accepted sample is retained; only preview publication is coalesced. Default memory/cache budgets do not restrict original image resolution. Mask/filter-mask coverage extends this boundary as described above; sustained/device acceptance remains unfinished; no new isolated capability, REST/browser synchronization, provider call or upload is introduced.


Retained wet workspaces serialize append/snapshot/finish operations over captured settings and immutable newly accepted samples. Each symmetry carrier and native canvas epoch advances only after a complete dab. Later prefixes reuse completed native work. Snapshot cropping never crops transport; selection/whole-opacity projections are cached per raw epoch and applied once. Result snapshots own independent private backing/locks and survive parent/source disposal. Finishing transfers job ownership only after canonical output and cleanup succeed. Abort or job failure publishes no command/asset; independent completed results remain owned. No new isolated service, REST synchronization or source-resolution cap is introduced. Tool/UI/preset/mask and full performance/device acceptance remain open.

Schema-33 prepared wet operations preserve ordered native pixel replacement before layer appearance. Output alpha is at most coverage alpha and is already masked; coverage removes destination alpha and output adds once. Whole-operation opacity envelopes all replacements once. Never mask already filtered output a second time or convert original rasters to paint layers. Source pixels and captured operation geometry survive resize/undo/persistence. Bounded native reconstruction precedes transforms; GPU falls back and SVG uses disclosed native prefixes. Async preparation/validation owns private resources and rechecks revision/session/selection/source identity before a synchronous OO commit. Scripts and REST share prepared-content validation within existing isolation/session boundaries. This adapter is in verification; gestures, incremental previews and full tool/preset/mask/performance gates remain open.

Native spatial wet preparation processes the complete recorded path before viewport cropping. Each symmetry copy owns a separate native spatial pigment field; copies sample completed preceding copies in shared dab order. Within one dab, all destination and carried reads use the same prior epoch. Complete private staging precedes advancement, and bilinear neighbors sum in a fixed order across backing partitions. Native coverage uses a fixed raster grid; final opacity/selection applies once and unchanged pixels remain byte-invariant. Disk-backed private jobs survive resident cache eviction, and active Web Locks prevent abandoned-job cleanup from deleting another tab/worker's state. Failed preparation publishes no model/assets and deletes its own namespace; completed output owns its bytes until disposal. The rendered-document sampler captures source/font identity and remains read-only. These are internal dependencies; authored ordered layer replacement, OO/history/persistence, tools/preview and export/automation integration remain unfinished. See ARCHITECTURE.md for defaults, bounds, cleanup fallback and current limits.

Wet paint currently has an internal numerical dependency, not a shipped mixer/smudge workflow. Captured pre-dab destination and spatial carried pigment are distinct immutable inputs. The worker executes actual WASM premultiplied RGBA transport and returns owned RGBA8 pixels plus Float32 reservoir state. Pickup samples pre-deposit pixels; each dab tile therefore has no dependency on the processing order of other tiles from that same dab. Zero flow/coverage is inert; alpha can increase or decrease. Initial load is finite; whole-stroke selection/opacity belongs to a later original/result composite. Caller data never transfers, and returned extents/normalized premultiplied channels are validated. Bounded working tiles must not become source/document limits. Full-stroke spatial transport, ordered layer mutations, captured sources, UI/cancel/history/persistence and export parity remain required before delivery; no new isolated host service or REST/browser synchronization is added. See ARCHITECTURE.md for the exact internal equations and defaults.

Pen overlay reconciliation retains every native control while memoizing long paths in contiguous 64-anchor blocks. A changed block refreshes its markers; unchanged blocks retain existing SVG nodes. Short paths render directly, and fragments preserve original SVG ancestry and paint order. Each block retains only its own at-most-64 point references, avoiding retention of complete prior path arrays across independent block updates. Basis, zoom, selection, geometry length/coordinates and the large-translation precision fallback remain invalidation inputs. This is a UI rendering optimization; public constructors, validation, history, persistence and isolated extension boundaries remain unchanged.

Native text spacing follows one shared state contract: OO text setters and strict commands validate schema-25 wordSpacing/fontKerning, then measurement, Canvas reference rendering, GPU reference textures and SVG preparation apply complete font/spacing/direction defaults. Whole lines stay in the browser shaping engine. Unsupported nondefault native controls reject explicitly; reset restores supported defaults in one command. Legacy valid roots/history migrate without inserting fields, and project/workspace/source asset boundaries stay unchanged. Schema-26 paragraph wrapping, gaps and indent share the native paragraph invariant below. Font substitution, headless estimated geometry and broader paragraph-style/variable-font/multilingual acceptance remain explicit limitations.

This document defines the system design, architectural boundaries, and non-negotiable invariants of Canoli Studio. All human contributors and AI coding agents working on this codebase must strictly adhere to these specifications.

---

## TIFF import invariant

TIFF/BigTIFF source identity includes original Blob bytes and selected page/precision-consent settings. The trusted inspector/decoder workers return validated reports and an intermediate PNG; the AssetStore retains original TIFF separately from its 8-bit bitmap. Native affine placement owns orientation, while revision/session/lifetime checks guard private staged publication. Project/workspace/recipe/copy/recovery must carry settings unchanged; recovery integrity keys include them, preserving existing non-TIFF hashes. No document schema, isolated file privilege, plugin permission or REST/browser synchronization is added. Decode streams rows rather than complete source strips, without claiming constant total memory or imposing arbitrary image limits. SCRIPTING_API.md defines the supported subset and explicit failures.

## 1. High-Level Architecture

PDF raster delivery is a trusted read-only export: pin immutable model/visible sources/fonts, render canonical native grid regions, stream compressed RGB/alpha rows and serialize one image/soft mask with physical DPI placement. A single image matrix avoids independent tile-edge rounding. Blob-backed objects use exact addressing and eight-byte cross-reference offsets; geometry failures and lifecycle/cancel errors publish no partial file. Surface/stream cleanup is required. Source/output/reader memory remains data dependent, and PDF prepress/editability/import/REST/batch are not implied. Generated sRGB/P3 output ICC uses the piecewise sRGB curve; original profiles, document precision/schema and extension privileges stay unchanged.

Canoli Studio is a browser-first, local-first image editor combining precision manual editing with future AI-assisted workflows. It decouples document representation, state mutation, image rendering, and execution surfaces.

## 2. Module Responsibilities & Boundaries

| Module                | Location                           | Responsibility & Rules                                                                                                                                                                   |
| :-------------------- | :--------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Public DOM**        | `src/dom/`                         | Public OOP constructors (`Document`, `RasterLayer`, `PaintLayer`, `VectorLayer`, `LayerGroup`, etc.). Browser-independent; wraps internal IDs; delegates attached mutations to commands. |
| **Core Model**        | `src/core/model.ts`, `drawing.ts`  | Plain, serializable Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) and structural schemas. Children are stored back-to-front. No UI state or pixel buffers.                                                |
| **Command Core**      | `src/core/commands.ts`, `store.ts` | Validated, atomic mutations and history management (undo/redo stack up to 60 revisions). Pure functions that transform document snapshots.                                               |
| **Validation**        | `src/core/validation.ts`           | Runtime schema validation (using Zod) for external commands and script results.                                                                                                          |
| **Asset Store**       | `src/core/assets.ts`               | Manages immutable original source images, small previews/thumbnails, and lifecycle cleanup.                                                                                              |
| **Persistence**       | `src/core/project.ts`              | Serializes/loads v2 `.luma` blob containers and legacy JSON. `src/core/recovery.ts` atomically persists local checkpoints/assets; see STORAGE_FORMAT.md.                                 |
| **Rendering Engine**  | `src/engine/`                      | Decoupled compositing pipeline (`DocumentRenderer`, `CanvasRenderer`), tile management, pixel worker communication, and streaming PNG export.                                            |
| **WASM Kernel**       | `assembly/pixels.ts`               | High-performance AssemblyScript pixel operations (exposure, contrast, saturation and Blend If math; Canvas 2D handles blend modes) compiled to `pixels.wasm`.                            |

## 3. Non-Negotiable System Invariants

### 1. Unified Object-Oriented DOM with Stable ID Indirection

- The public programming interface is strictly object-oriented.
- **Detached vs. Attached:** Constructors (`new RasterLayer(...)`) create detached instances. Adding a layer to a document or group attaches it.
- **Dynamic Handle Indirection:** Attached objects do not store mutable state in class fields. Instead, they store a stable `id` and read properties directly from the current document revision in `EditorStore`.
- **Handle Survival Across Undo/Redo:** Because handles resolve state by ID against the active revision, handles retained in code or UI remain valid after undo/redo cycles.

### 2. Pure Command-Driven Mutation & Synchronous Transactions

- **No Direct State Mutation:** Document trees and snapshots are strictly immutable outside commands. All UI gestures, shortcuts, scripting calls, and REST endpoints emit `EditorCommand` objects.
- **Transaction Atomicity:** Multi-operation edits run inside `Document.transaction(label, callback)`. A transaction groups all child commands into exactly **one** undo history entry.
- **Synchronous Only:** Transactions are strictly synchronous. Asynchronous work (e.g. decoding images, running worker jobs) must complete _before_ opening a transaction.

### 3. Asset Immutability & Decoupled Memory Budgets (No Fixed MP Limits)

- **Preserve Original Pixels:** Original imported images are immutable source assets in `AssetStore`. Edits, transforms, and adjustments never overwrite source data.
- **No Arbitrary Resolution Caps:** Never add arbitrary megapixel, image-byte, or dimension limits (e.g., no 8192px cutoff). Document dimensions are numeric coordinates in JavaScript safe-integer space.
- **Decoupled Allocations:**
  - Viewport renders visible document regions into preview surfaces (budgeted to $\le 4\text{ MP}$ / $4096\text{px}$).
  - Interactive layer/mask caches retain at most 64 MiB plus a 16 MiB active-stroke surface; painted-mask active coverage adds a separate bounded 16 MiB tile LRU. Cache eviction never changes source resolution. Export and clone tiles bypass viewport caching.
  - Pixel filters run on small tiles ($\le 1024 \times 1024$) in worker threads.
  - Full-resolution PNG export streams scanlines in bounded chunks ($\sim 4\text{ MB}$) directly through `CompressionStream('deflate')`.

### 4. Sandbox Isolation for Automation Surfaces

- **Scripting Security:** Scripts run off the UI thread in a Web Worker inside an opaque-origin sandboxed iframe. Network access, browser DOM, host objects (`window`, `fetch`), and raw pixel buffers are strictly blocked.
- **DTO Validation:** Scripts return command DTOs that are validated against strict Zod schemas before being applied as an atomic transaction.
- **REST Boundary:** The local REST server operates on separate in-memory documents and enforces concurrency via `expectedRevision`.

### 5. Multi-Threaded Engine & WASM Boundary

- **No Pixel Loops on Main Thread:** Pixel manipulation must run inside `src/engine/pixels.worker.ts`.
- **GPU path:** WebGPU/WGSL handles supported viewport pixel work; Canvas/WASM remains the export/reference and unsupported-device/effect fallback. Device loss must trigger a new fallback frame. GPU allocations never impose image import limits. See `ARCHITECTURE.md` for current shader scope, working budgets, tolerances and verification limits.
- **AssemblyScript vs. TypeScript:** AssemblyScript is a distinct, constrained language used exclusively for numerical pixel kernels (`assembly/pixels.ts`). General UI and business logic must remain in TypeScript.

### 6. Bespoke Design System & Centralized Shortcuts

- **No Third-Party Component Frameworks:** Do not introduce `shadcn`, Tailwind UI, or external widget libraries. Use the custom tokens in `src/ui/tokens.css` and custom components in `src/ui/controls.tsx` and `src/ui/Dialog.tsx`.
- **Central Shortcut Registry:** Keyboard binding definitions belong in `src/ui/shortcuts.ts`; the UI registers document-dependent actions against those definitions. Shortcuts must automatically suspend when text fields (`input`, `textarea`, `select`) have focus.

## Schema-29 pressure-response invariant

Authored pressure curves are immutable brush metadata, separate from recorded point pressure. One normalized monotonic mapping owns size/alpha/spacing/bounds in native, SVG and supported GPU replay. Preserve absent-curve legacy floors and allow explicit zero without a pencil pixel or stale cached dab. Empty segments do not require a numeric stamp grid; nonempty subpixel/numeric precision and cancellation rules remain. Validate settings before cancelling an active gesture or publishing a new curve. Native project/workspace containers, source ownership, shared commands/undo, inert plugins and separate headless REST sessions remain unchanged. ## Saved brush preference invariant

Immutable presets own complete supported brush settings, with optional foreground capture and no document/source/target references. Native IndexedDB write transactions re-read/validate all saved records before atomic writes, retaining concurrent additions and rejecting stale revisions. Imports validate the whole pack and assign fresh identities. Corrupt records, aborted transactions and failed writes preserve persisted bytes and last-valid cache. Raw recovery backups never install content; explicit reset must match every current record under a write lock. Cross-tab messages only trigger validated reads; focus refresh works without notifications. Applying uses the shared trusted tool configuration/cancellation path, while each actual stroke remains an ordinary document command/undo record. Library lifetime belongs to the editor, separate from project/workspace containers and isolated/REST capabilities.

Recovery JSON is emitted only for losslessly representable JSON trees. Unexpected binary/typed/date values, nonfinite numbers, undefined fields, sparse arrays, accessors, cycles and shared references reject backup and reset rather than silently dropping data. ## Brush-tip geometry invariant

Authored shape and spherical point orientation are complete stroke metadata, independent of transient UI preferences and local preset identities. The inverse affine plane transforms projected direction while preserving pen altitude; interpolation follows the shortest azimuth arc. Shared geometry defines native Canvas, SVG, supported WGSL, conservative rotated-pencil bounds and nominal-pressure cursors. Missing tip preserves legacy behavior; explicit zero pressure stays empty. Sensor ambiguities and numerical GPU fallbacks are explicit. Document schema 30 age validation spans ordinary/mask/filter-mask/erasure/tonal/master/history records; project 3/workspace 2 and original asset bytes remain intact. Portable tip presets require v2 without relabeling legacy v1. The public API remains object-oriented and attached edits use existing validation/history boundaries.

BrushSymmetry is metadata with implicit original ink and at most 31 validated distinct invertible nonidentity affine copies. Keep original pressure/tilt samples; transform complete tip geometry after interpolation and pencil anchoring. Original-first/copy-array ordering per dab must match incremental and full replay. Map copy viewports to source-plane stamp-index intervals and merge them without scanning invisible gaps. Apply captured selection/whole-stroke opacity once to the accumulated copy surface; overlapping copies build flow. Tool preferences live in document space and conjugate into attached layer/mask/native-master planes. Bounds/culling/source capture must include every copy; clone retains its destination-relative captured source field and healing keeps existing real working-memory limits. Supported WGSL uses complete per-instance bases and explicit precision fallback.

Schema 31 checks paint/masks/filter masks/erasures/tonal/master/history field age. Project 3/workspace 2 and original assets remain intact. Preset/pack 3 carries optional document-space symmetry without relabeling legacy defaults or changing IndexedDB store version. Host validation and isolated plugin permissions stay authoritative. Guides memoize settings, and imperative ghost cursors stay viewport-sized. These are functional invariants, not complete brush-engine, tablet/hardware-GPU, physical-display, sustained 60fps or peak-memory acceptance.

## Authored texture source invariant — in verification

Schema-32 image-backed brush coverage uses immutable OO values and the existing command/lock/revision/undo boundaries. Central reference visitors distinguish texture and ordinary image roles across paint, masks/filter masks, erasures, tonal strokes and embedded masters. Original Blob bytes and TIFF decode settings must survive project/workspace history, recipe packaging and document copies. Export preparation must pin these sources before progress callbacks. Native rendering samples bounded original-bitmap tiles; one renderer owns the shared sampler, while replay prefixes borrow it. Inverted affine alpha is opaque projected support minus sampled alpha, preventing inverse coverage outside the image frame. SVG prepares streamed source-resolution coverage PNGs, and unsupported GPU paint uses whole-composition Canvas fallback. Source selection/tool ownership and original-byte portable presets are unfinished; this invariant adds no isolated file/network/export privilege or REST/browser synchronization.

## Explicit source ownership for texture preferences — integration in progress

AssetStore sharing is an explicit reference-counted ownership operation, separate from ordinary owned-resource adoption. Shared records/TIFF decode choices are immutable, native geometry/Blob bytes are retained, and the final store reference closes the bitmap exactly once. Closed stores are terminal; metadata teardown failure still releases image ownership. Pending import IDs cannot be overwritten/adopted/shared before completion. No document schema, user-source cap, isolated file privilege, upload or REST/browser synchronization is added.


## Texture preferences and native gestures — 2026-10-18

The active source owner is now connected to a private-draft custom dialog and nullable channel/inversion preferences. Ownership is independent of document-local asset IDs. Beginning each brush-family/mask gesture leases its original into the active document and captures ordinary immutable BrushTexture metadata; no original decode/resample occurs during this synchronous capture.
